MAJAZ:v1p12/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p12/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p12/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayda treats the phrase’s order as fronting and delay: the intended sequence is ‘swelled and stirred.’
MAJAZ:v1p12/r1.anchor: قال: «فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء اهتزت وربت» (22/ 5) أراد ربت واهتزت.

ITQAN:v2p381/r23.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p381/r23.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p381/r23.anchor:
﴿ هضما ﴾ نقصا
2505 ﴿ هامدة ﴾ مغبرة
2506 ﴿ واقصد في مشيك ﴾ أسرع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p477/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p477/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p477/r3.claim: A morsel is a small piece of flesh about the size one can chew; formed means smoothed and complete without defect.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p477/r3.anchor: المضغة: اللحمة الصغيرة قدر ما يمضغ. المخلقة: المسواة الملساء لا نقص ولا عيب فيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p477/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p477/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p477/r4.claim: Child can name the period from birth to puberty, a young animal, or an adjective for any gender or number; related forms also describe having a child or gentleness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p477/r4.anchor: الطفل: يقال من وقت انفصال الولد إلى البلوغ، ويقال لولد الوحشية طفل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p477/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p477/r5.speaker: المبرد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p477/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad says child is a verbal noun like satisfaction or justice and can refer to one or many.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p477/r5.anchor: وقال المبرد: هو اسم يستعمل مصدرا كالرضا والعدل يقع على الواحد والجمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p477/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p477/r6.speaker: المبرد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p477/r6.claim: The verb for earth becoming barren can mean drying and falling into ruin; the same root can describe a worn garment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p477/r6.anchor: همدت الأرض: يبست ودرست، والثوب بلي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p477/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p477/r7.speaker: الأعشى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p477/r7.claim: Al-Aʿsha’s verse uses the word for barren and worn to describe clothing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p477/r7.anchor: وقال الأعشى: قالت قتيلة ما لجسمك شاحبا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p477/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p477/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p477/r8.claim: Bihīj means beautiful and pleasing to the eye, with related forms meaning beauty or delight.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r3.claim: Two clear arguments answer doubts about resurrection: human development through successive stages and the earth’s observable movement from barrenness to life; reason establishes possibility and revelation confirms its occurrence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r3.anchor: ذكر دليلين واضحين على ذلك أحدهما في نفس الإنسان وابتداء خلقه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r4.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r4.claim: Hasan reads resurrection with fatḥa on the middle consonant, a dialect form; Kufans analogize such vowel reduction around gutturals while Basrans treat attested cases as separate dialect forms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r4.anchor: وقرأ الحسن من البعث بفتح العين وهي لغة فيه كالحلب والطرد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r5.claim: Humanity comes from soil through Adam or through reproductive foods ultimately derived from land and water; the seed is semen, though al-Naqqash says it was Adam’s seed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r5.anchor: من تراب أي أصلكم آدم وسلط الفعل عليهم من حيث هم من ذريته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r6.speaker: النقاش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r6.claim: Al-Naqqash interprets the seed in this sequence as Adam’s own seed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r6.anchor: والنطفة المني. وقيل نطفة آدم قاله النقاش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r7.claim: A clot is a piece of congealed blood; unformed means incomplete or unsmoothed, explaining variation in stature and completeness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r7.anchor: والعلقة قطعة الدم الجامدة ومعنى وغير مخلقة أي ليست كاملة ولا ملساء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r8.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والشعبي وأبو العالية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r8.claim: These authorities say an unformed embryo is one that is miscarried.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r8.anchor: وقال مجاهد غير مخلقة هي التي تستسقط وقاله قتادة والشعبي وأبو العالية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r9.claim: The verb form intensifies the idea of creation because the human body contains many distinct organs, each fashioned with its own form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p484/r9.anchor: ولما كان الإنسان فيه أعضاء متباينة وكل واحد منها مختص بخلق حسن تضعيف الفعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r1.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r1.claim: Ibn Abi Abla reads formed and unformed as accusatives describing the preceding indefinite noun, a rare but analogically acceptable construction according to Sibawayh.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة مخلقة بالنصب وغير بالنصب أيضا نصبا على الحال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the stages show that the one who first created humans from unrelated soil and water can recreate them, which is even easier by analogy; the acts reveal knowledge and power beyond human grasp.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r2.anchor: ولنبين لكم بهذا التدريج قدرتنا وإن من قدر على خلق البشر من تراب أولا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r3.claim: The purpose clause to clarify is connected to created you; Ibn Atiyya instead takes it as an aside explaining resurrection, while al-Kirmani says it clarifies guidance and error.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r3.anchor: ولنبين متعلق بخلقناكم. وقيل لنبين لكم أمر البعث. قال ابن عطية:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r4.speaker: قول آخر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r4.claim: Another interpretation says formation is a choice of the choosing agent, which explains why some embryos remain unformed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r4.anchor: وقيل لنبين لكم أن التخليق هو اختيار من الفاعل المختار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r5.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r5.claim: Ibn Abi Abla reads the clause with a third-person verb, clarifying the process for you.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة ليبين لكم ويقر بالياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r6.speaker: يعقوب وعاصم في رواية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r6.claim: Yaqub and one transmission from Asim read we settle in the wombs in the accusative, coordinating it with to clarify.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r6.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب وعاصم في رواية ونقر بالنصب عطفا على لنبين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the nominative reading as a statement that God keeps in the womb whoever He chooses until birth; the accusative makes keeping another purpose so the children may be born, grow, and reach responsibility.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r7.anchor: والقراءة بالنصب تعليل معطوف على تعليل والمعنى خلقناكم مدرجين هذا التدريج لغرضين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r8.speaker: يعقوب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r8.claim: Yaqub also reads we settle with the verb form meaning pour out water; other named readers vary between accusative and nominative forms for settle and bring you out.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r8.anchor: وعن يعقوب ونقر بفتح النون وضم القاف والراء من قر الماء صبه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r9.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r9.claim: Yahya ibn Waththab reads what We will with kasra on the nūn; the appointed term varies for each fetus according to whether it miscarries or is carried to completion and live birth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r9.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب ما نشاء بكسر النون والأجل المسمى مختلف فيه بحسب جنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r10.speaker: المبرد والطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r10.claim: Al-Mubarrad and al-Tabari explain child as a singular verbal noun or generic term, and it is also singular because the sense is each one of you.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p485/r10.anchor: وحد طفلا لأنه مصدر في الأصل قاله المبرد والطبري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r1.claim: Al-ashudd denotes full strength, reason, and discernment; it is a plural form without a singular, like other collective plurals.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r2.claim: Another explanation derives al-ashudd as a plural of shiddah, as an'am is a plural of ni'mah.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r2.anchor: وإن من الناس من قال إنه جمع شدة كأنعم جمع نعمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r3.claim: One reading makes yatwaffa active, meaning that God completes the person's term; the majority read it passive, after strength and before decrepit old age.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r3.anchor: وقرىء يتوفى بفتح الياء أي يستوفي أجله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r4.claim: Decrepit age brings bodily weakness and impaired reason, but has no fixed onset: some centenarians remain vigorous while younger adults weaken.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r4.anchor: ولا زمان لذلك محدود بل ذلك بحسب ما يقع في الناس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r5.claim: God can bring a person from completed maturity to senility just as He developed him gradually, and can likewise resurrect bodies after their stages of development.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r5.anchor: فكذلك هو قادر على إعادة الأجساد التي درجها في هذه المناقل وإنشائها النشأة الثانية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r6.speaker: الكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r6.claim: The purpose of the return to the weakest age is that a person can no longer understand anything after his former understanding.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r6.anchor: قال الكلبي لكيلا يعقل من بعد عقله الأول شيئا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r7.claim: Another view says the person can no longer acquire knowledge and forgets what he had learned.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r7.anchor: وقيل لكيلا يستفيد علما وينسى ما علمه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r8.claim: Old age can make new learning vanish almost immediately, so the person repeatedly asks who someone is just after being told.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r8.anchor: أي ليصير نساء بحيث إذا كسب علما في شيء لم ينشب أن ينساه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو ونافع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r9.claim: Abu Amr and Nafi are reported to give the mīm in al-umur a sukūn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r9.anchor: وروي عن أبي عمرو ونافع تسكين ميم العمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r10.claim: The verse's first proof of resurrection is human creation; unlike the earth's revival, not every stage of this proof can be directly seen.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r10.anchor: ولما كان الدليل الأول بعض مراتب الخلقة فيه غير مرتبين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r11.claim: The revived earth is a second proof visible to the eye, which is why the verse explicitly says that the listener sees it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r11.anchor: ولما كان هذا الدليل الثاني مشاهدا للأبصار أحال ذلك على الرؤية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r12.claim: The rain includes rainwater, rivers, springs, and irrigation; the earth's movement is loosened, shifting soil as plants emerge, and rabat means it swelled.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r12.anchor: والماء ماء المطر والأنهار والعيون والسواني واهتزازها تخلخلها واضطراب بعض أجسامها لأجل خروج النبات وربت أي زادت وانتفخت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r13.speaker: أبو جعفر وعبد الله بن جعفر وخالد بن إلياس وأبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r13.claim: These readers pronounce rabat with hamza, rabat, meaning it rose or stood high; Ibn Atiyya explains the earth as stretching upward with water like a lookout rising above ground.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p486/r13.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وعبد الله بن جعفر وخالد بن إلياس وأبو عمرو في رواية وربأت بالهمز هنا وفي فصلت أي ارتفعت وأشرفت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p487/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p487/r1.speaker: الشاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p487/r1.claim: An anonymous poetic line uses rabi'an for a scout sent ahead, supporting the sense of rising to a high lookout.

MAJAZ:v2p45/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p45/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p45/r1.claim: Zawj bahīj means beautiful, fresh, and new; bahij is also used.
MAJAZ:v2p45/r1.anchor: «زوج بهيج» (5) أي حسن قشيب جديد ويقال أيضا بهج

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r1.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r1.claim: One dating view holds that the surah is Madinan except verses 52–55, which are Makkan.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r1.anchor: Some say it is Madinan except for vv. 52–55, which are Makkan (IK)

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r2.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r2.claim: Another dating view holds that the surah is Makkan except verses 19–22, which are Madinan.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r2.anchor: others say it is Makkan except for vv.19–22, which are from the Madinan period (Q)

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r3.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r3.claim: Most authorities regard the surah as containing both Makkan and Madinan verses.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r3.anchor: Most say it is a mix of Makkan and Madinan verses (Q)

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r4.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r4.claim: A tradition calls the surah remarkable because it came at night and by day, on journeys and at home, in war and peace, and includes abrogating and abrogated as well as clear and allegorical verses.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r4.anchor: and it has both muḥkam (unambiguous) and mutashābih (symbolic or allegorical) verses (Q)

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r6.claim: The opening warns of the world's destruction and Resurrection, comparing them with the human life cycle.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r6.anchor: compared to the individual life cycle of human beings (vv.5–7)

TABATABAI:22:3-16#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:3-16#2/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:22:3-16#2/r1.claim: A report describes angels recording what is decreed for a fetus from a tablet that reaches its mother's forehead, while stipulating possible change in what they write.
TABATABAI:22:3-16#2/r1.anchor: الملكين يكتبان جميع ما قدر له عن لوح يقرع جبهة أمه فيكتبان جميع ما في اللوح ويشترطان البداء فيما يكتبان

TABATABAI:22:3-16#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:3-16#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:3-16#2/r2.claim: The reports are reconciled by two tablets: the Preserved Tablet cannot change, while the Tablet of Effacement and Confirmation can; decree accordingly has inevitable and non-inevitable forms.
TABATABAI:22:3-16#2/r2.anchor: فإن لكل شيء ومنها الإنسان نصيبا في اللوح المحفوظ الذي لا سبيل للتغير والتبدل إلى ما كتب فيه ونصيبا من لوح المحو والإثبات الذي يقبل التغير والتبدل

TABATABAI:22:3-16#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:3-16#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:3-16#2/r3.claim: Complete causal chains do not change, incomplete chains can; inevitability in decree does not negate the voluntary character of human acts.
TABATABAI:22:3-16#2/r3.anchor: سلسلة العلل التامة ومعلولاتها ولا تقبل تغييرا وسلسلة العلل الناقصة مع معاليلها وهي القابلة وكأن الصنف الأول من الروايات يشير إلى ما يقضى للجنين من قضاء محتوم

TABATABAI:22:3-16#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:3-16#2/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:22:3-16#2/r4.claim: “Formed” refers to particles created in Adam's loins under the covenant and carried through later generations; “unformed” includes expelled semen and miscarried fetuses before ensoulment.
TABATABAI:22:3-16#2/r4.anchor: قال المخلقة هم الذر الذين خلقهم الله

TABATABAI:22:3-16#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:3-16#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:3-16#2/r5.claim: The interpretation of this report was explained earlier in the discussion of the primordial covenant.
TABATABAI:22:3-16#2/r5.anchor: وقد تقدم توضيح معنى الحديث في البحث الروائي المتعلق بآية الذر في سورة الأعراف

TABATABAI:22:3-16#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:3-16#2/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABATABAI:22:3-16#2/r6.claim: A report attributed to al-Sadiq through his father says that reaching one hundred years is the most decrepit stage of life.
TABATABAI:22:3-16#2/r6.anchor: قال إذا بلغ العبد مائة سنة فذلك أرذل العمر

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p163/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p163/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p163/r2.claim: Human development and earth's revival after drought argue for resurrection; doubters should reflect on themselves and the world instead of demanding to see punishment, since the Hereafter necessarily follows from God's attributes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p163/r2.anchor: Arguments in favour of the Hereafter are cited by referring to phases of creation of a human being and by the phenomenon of earth’s revival to life after a dry spell.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p169/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p169/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p169/r1.claim: Creation’s stages, observable signs in the universe, and the divine attributes they reveal argue for monotheism and resurrection; reflection on oneself and the surrounding world suffices to see these clear truths.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p169/r1.anchor: He does not need to go far.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p172/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p172/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p172/r1.claim: Arab idolaters doubted resurrection because they considered revival after bodily decay implausible; hypothetical belief left them relying on deities and intercessors to evade accountability.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p172/r1.anchor: they thought it was very unlikely for people to be raised to life again after they die and their bodies are decomposed into mud.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p172/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p172/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p172/r2.claim: The Qur’an insists the Hereafter is real life and this world its prelude and necessary consequence, while proving that the supposed deities and intercessors have no basis.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p172/r2.anchor: the real life is that of the hereafter; it iterated that this world is a prelude and the next one is its necessary consequence.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p172/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p172/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p172/r3.claim: Feeling their position threatened, the idolaters harassed the Prophet, demanding the promised doom or a tangible punishment as proof.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p172/r3.anchor: the only antidote they had to salvage the situation was to harass and corner the Prophet (sws).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p172/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p172/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p172/r4.claim: The Qur’an answers their doubts by directing them to human development and everyday observations: attentive people can see proof of God’s oneness and the Hereafter within themselves and around them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p172/r4.anchor: the Qur’ ān has directed their attention to their own phases of creation and everyday observations of the world.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p172/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p172/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p172/r5.claim: ʿAlaqah can mean a clot of blood or a small living insect; it is the womb stage after sperm when the embryo takes a blood-like form and shows signs of life.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p172/r5.anchor: This phase comes after the sperm is lodged in the womb when it assumes the shape of blood and a foetus, and shows signs of life.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p172/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p172/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p172/r6.claim: Muḍghah means a lump of flesh at the next fetal stage; some reach final form and others remain defective by God’s will, which no one can rectify.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p172/r6.anchor: This is the stage following the previous one when the foetus assumes the form of a lump of flesh.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p173/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p173/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p173/r1.claim: The stages of human development are not needed for God to create; He could make fully formed people at once, but chose this process to teach people His power, wisdom, and providence.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p173/r1.anchor: God was not dependent on all these phases in order to create human beings.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p173/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p173/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p173/r2.claim: Human creation testifies that people were not made for amusement but for a purpose that will become manifest; the Creator who made life from clay and fluid can readily resurrect it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p173/r2.anchor: his own being bears witness that He Who has created him in such an elaborate manner and shown favour to him has not made him a toy for amusement

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p173/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p173/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p173/r3.claim: The creation sequence in al-Mu’minūn describes the same reality as this passage and summarizes the stages that testify to resurrection.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p173/r3.anchor: The following verses of Sūrah al-Mu’minūn point to precisely the same reality:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p173/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p173/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p173/r4.claim: Modern philosophers and scientists observe the developmental stages but fail to grasp the divine purpose of this arrangement.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p173/r4.anchor: do observe all these phases of creation but they are not able to grasp the actual purpose for which God has made all this arrangement.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r1.claim: The phrase about keeping a fetus in the womb until an appointed time is followed by an insertion that interrupts the discourse to caution and awaken its addressees, after which it resumes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r1.anchor: The discourse was still going on when suddenly the words i were inserted in it to caution and prod the addressees

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r2.claim: The inserted phrase ‘whatever We want’ emphasizes that a child’s sex, appearance, and whether it is defective or perfect are wholly determined by God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r2.anchor: The words “whatever We want” show whether the child is a girl or a boy, attractive or ugly, defective or perfect entirely rests on God’s will.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r3.claim: The duration of pregnancy also lies within God’s discretion, and no one else can change it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r3.anchor: Similarly, the time of pregnancy is also in God’s discretion and none has the authority to change its duration.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r4.claim: The lām signals a suppressed verb: God lets a newborn gradually reach maturity, and no one can skip the stages of childhood.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r4.anchor: God gives time to the newly born child to gradually reach maturity and this pattern is always followed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r5.claim: A suppressed parallel expression means many die in childhood or adolescence while others reach extreme old age; lifespan is entirely under God’s authority.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r5.anchor: many human beings die in chidhood and adolescence and many who reach the exteme of old age.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r6.claim: The indefinite ‘knowledge’ can signify belittlement or magnification; the author prefers that old age erases the little knowledge one acquired, supported by 17:85, and warns knowledge is God-given and can be taken away.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r6.anchor: I would give preference to the first of these interpretations as parallel verses corroborate it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r7.claim: The dry earth revived by rain is an external sign of resurrection; people repeatedly witness this pattern, so the omitted words need not be repeated because the sign is obvious.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p174/r7.anchor: After directing attention to the signs of the Day of Judgement found within the stages of creation of human beings, the external world is focused upon.

SIBAWAYH:فالحروفالتيتشركالواووالفاءوثموأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فالحروفالتيتشركالواووالفاءوثموأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فالحروفالتيتشركالواووالفاءوثموأ.claim: In 22:5, ونقر is raised as a new clause: creation was mentioned to make the signs clear, not to state the act of keeping embryos in the womb.

BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r1.claim: Those who die are taken by God after reaching maturity or before it; tawaffī denotes death and the taking of the soul.
BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r1.anchor: أي : يقبض روحه ويموت بعد بلوغ الأشد أو قبله والتوفي عبارة عن الموت وتوفاه الله قبض روحه

BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r2.claim: Ardhal al-ʿumr is decrepit old age and senility; ʿumr is the span during which life animates the body.
BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r2.anchor: وهو الهرم والخرف والرذل والرذال المرغوب عنه لرداءته والعمر مدة عمارة البدن بالحياة

BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r3.claim: The phrase describes a severe reversal of knowledge and condition: the elderly may forget what they did and knew and lose abilities, though they still know some things like a child.
BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r3.anchor: وهو مبالغة في انتقاض علمه وانتكاس حاله وإلا فهو يعلم بعض الأشياء كالطفل

BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r4.speaker: الشيخ سعدي
BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r4.claim: Saʿdī’s verses lament that youth and the season of life pass, warning that desire and play consume the years and youth does not return.
BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r4.anchor: قال الشيخ سعدي قدس سره. طرب نوجوان زير مجوى كه دكر يدآب رفته بجوى

BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r5.speaker: النسفي
BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r5.claim: Al-Nasafī says ignorance before knowledge is hell because it breeds greed, whereas ignorance after knowledge is paradise because it brings acceptance and contentment.
BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r5.anchor: قال النسفي في "كشف الحقائق" : (أي درويش جهل يش ازعمل دوزخست وجهل بعد ازعلمبهشت

BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r6.speaker: البقلي
BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r6.claim: Al-Baqli reads the worst age inwardly as striving after witnessing and spiritual interruption after communion, when one loses awareness of lofty states and stations.
BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r6.anchor: وفي "عرائس البقلي" : ارذل العمر أيام المجاهدة بعد المشاهدة

BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r7.speaker: البقلي
BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r7.claim: Al-Baqli calls this God’s protective jealousy toward realized people who disclosed His secrets through excessive claims, and seeks refuge from the ego.
BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r7.anchor: وفي "عرائس البقلي" : ارذل العمر أيام المجاهدة بعد المشاهدة

BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r8.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r8.claim: The Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya says created beings rested in the wombs of nonexistence by God’s determination, each emerging only by His will at its anciently appointed term.
BURSEVI:v6p4#2/r8.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : في الآية إشارة إلى أن أطفال المكونات كانوا في أرحام

BURSEVI:v6p4#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p4#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p4#3/r1.claim: Bursevī rejects the philosophers’ dilemma that a world beginning in time implies divine deficiency, while eternal creative causes would require an eternal world.
BURSEVI:v6p4#3/r1.anchor: فنقول في جوابهم إن الآية تدل على أن الله تعالى كان في الأزل

BURSEVI:v6p4#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p4#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p4#3/r2.claim: Bursevī answers that God eternally existed alone and could create as He willed, while eternal wisdom and will fixed the world’s appointed emergence from nonexistence; before creation there was no ordinary time.
BURSEVI:v6p4#3/r2.anchor: فنقول في جوابهم إن الآية تدل على أن الله تعالى كان في الأزل ولم يكن معه شيء شاء وكان قادرا على إيجاد ما يشاء

BURSEVI:v6p4#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p4#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p4#3/r3.claim: Every created thing emerges from nonexistence ready for cultivation and reaches its perfection gradually; some perish before completion, while others pass beyond perfection and lose its qualities.
BURSEVI:v6p4#3/r3.anchor: يشير إلى أن كل طفل من أطفال المكونات يخرج من رحم العدم مستعدا للتربية وله كمال يبلغه بالتدريج

BURSEVI:v6p5/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p5/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p5/r1.claim: The earth is seen as dead and dry; hāmida is like a fire that has gone out and become ashes.
BURSEVI:v6p5/r1.anchor: {وترى الارض} يا من شأنه الرؤية وهو حجة أخرى على البعث

BURSEVI:v6p5/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p5/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p5/r2.claim: The revival of dead earth by rain is another proof that God can resurrect the dead and restore their scattered parts to their former state.

BURSEVI:v6p5/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p5/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p5/r3.claim: Ihtazzat means that the earth moves as vegetation appears; the word suggests joyful, pleasing motion and is rarely used for an unpleasant matter.
BURSEVI:v6p5/r3.anchor: {اهتزت} تحركت بالنبات والاهتزاز الحركة الواقعة على البهجة

BURSEVI:v6p5/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p5/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p5/r4.claim: Rabat means swollen, increased, and grown, from the root r-b-w; al-Qāmūs also uses it of a horse swelling from running or fright.
BURSEVI:v6p5/r4.anchor: {وربت} انتفخت وازدادت من ربا يربو ربا زاد ونما

BURSEVI:v6p5/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p5/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p5/r5.claim: Zawj means a kind; bahīj describes beauty of color and visible delight, as when joy shows on someone’s face.
BURSEVI:v6p5/r5.anchor: {وأنابتت من كل زوج} صنف {بهيج} البهجة حسن اللون

RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r1.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan vocalizes البعث with moving vowels, comparing it to الحلب and الطرد.

RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r2.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r2.claim: One reading puts kasra on the tāʾ and rāʾ of مخلقة وغير مخلقة; Ibn Abī ʿAblah reads both in the accusative.
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r2.anchor: { مخلقة وغير مخلقة } بجر التاء والراء

RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r3.claim: The familiar recitation uses nūn in لنبين, ونقر, and نخرجكم; Ibn Abī ʿAblah uses yāʾ in all three.
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r3.anchor: القراءة المعروفة بالنون في قوله : { لنبين } وفي قوله

RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r4.speaker: يعقوب
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r4.claim: Al-Sīrāfī reports from Dāwūd, from Yaʿqūb, ونقر with fatḥa on nūn and ḍamma on qāf and rāʾ, from قرّ الماء, “he poured the water”; another report has rāʾ in the accusative.
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r4.anchor: روى السيرافي عن داود عن يعقوب ونقر بفتح النون وضم القاف والراء وهو من قر الماء إذا صبه

RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r5.claim: Other nūn readings put ونقر and نخرجكم in the accusative.
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r5.anchor: وثالثها : ونقر ونخرجكم بنصب الراء والجيم

RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r6.claim: The yāʾ readings include يقر ويخرجكم with fatḥa on qāf, rāʾ, and jīm; another has ḍamma on those vowels; a third has fatḥa on yāʾ, kasra on qāf, and ḍamma on rāʾ.
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r6.anchor: يقر ويخرجكم بفتح القاف والراء والجيم

RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r7.speaker: أبو حاتم
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r7.claim: Abū Ḥātim reads يُتوفّى with fatḥa on yāʾ, making God the one who takes the person.
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r7.anchor: أبو حاتم { ومنكم من يتوفى } بفتح الياء

RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r8.speaker: ابن عمرة والأعمش
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r8.claim: Ibn ʿUmara and al-Aʿmash read العمر with a still mīm.
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r8.anchor: ابن عمرة والأعمش { العمر } بإسكان الميم

RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r9.speaker: عبدالله
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r9.claim: In ʿAbd Allāh’s codex the wording is ومنكم من يتوفى ومنكم من يكون شيوخا instead of the familiar reading.
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r9.anchor: وفي حرف عبدالله ومنكم من يتوفى ومنكم من يكون شيوخا بغير القراءة المعروفة

RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r10.speaker: أبو جعفر
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r10.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads وربأت, meaning it rose; al-ʿUmari reports this from him with the hamza softened.
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r10.anchor: وربت أبو جعفر وربأت أي ارتفعت

RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p7/r11.claim: The segment also notes the reading وأنه باعث without naming its reader.

RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r1.claim: Answering those who dispute resurrection without knowledge, God argues from two signs: the initial creation of humans and the revival of plants; human creation follows the argument in 36:79 and 17:51.
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r1.anchor: الدلالة على صحة ذلك من وجهين : أحدهما : الاستدلال بخلقة الحيوان أولا

RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r2.claim: One explanation is that humanity’s ancestor Adam was created from dust, as 3:59 and 20:55 say.
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r2.anchor: إنا خلقنا أصلكم وهو آدم عليه السلام من تراب

RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r3.claim: Alternatively, human semen and menstrual blood come from nourishment; animal nourishment ultimately traces to plants, and plants to earth and water, so humans are from dust.
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r3.anchor: وهما إنما يتولدان من الأغذية ، والأغذية إما حيوان أو نبات

RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r4.claim: Nuṭfa means a small amount of any liquid; here it means male semen, showing God’s transformation of dry dust into a subtle fluid with no resemblance to it.
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r4.anchor: والنطفة اسم للماء القليل أي ماء كان

RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r5.claim: ʿAlaqa is a clotted piece of blood, sharply different from the liquid that preceded it.
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r5.anchor: العلقة قطعة الدم الجامدة ، ولا شك أن بين الماء

RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r6.claim: A muḍgha is a small piece of flesh, roughly the amount one chews.
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r6.anchor: فالمضغة اللحمة الصغيرة قدر ما يمضغ

RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r7.claim: Mukhallaqa means smoothed, even, and free of defect; Arabic uses خلق for smoothing a tooth-stick or rod and calls a smooth rock خلقاء.
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r7.anchor: والمخلقة المسواة الملساء السالمة من النقصان والعيب

RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r8.speaker: قتادة والضحاك
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r8.claim: Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say the formed and unformed are embryos with complete or incomplete form, senses, and features; their difference explains variation in people’s bodies and appearance.
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r8.anchor: أن يكون المراد من تمت فيه أحوال الخلق ومن لم تتم

RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r9.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r9.claim: Mujāhid identifies the formed with a child born alive and the unformed with a miscarriage.
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r9.anchor: المخلقة الولد الذي يخرج حيا وغير المخلقة السقط وهو قول مجاهد

RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r10.claim: Another view calls the formed one shaped and the unformed one an unshaped lump of flesh.
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r10.anchor: المخلقة المصورة وغير المخلقة أي غير المصورة وهو الذي يبقى لحما من غير تخطيط وتشكيل

RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r11.speaker: عبدالله
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r11.claim: Alqama reports from ʿAbd Allāh that an angel asks whether the embryo is formed; if not, the womb expels it as blood, while a formed embryo’s sex, provision, lifespan, and fate are copied from the Mother Book and accompany it through its remaining stages.
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r11.anchor: عن عبدالله قال : ( إذا وقعت النطفة في الرحم

RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r12.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r12.claim: Al-Qaffāl derives the terms from successive creation through stages: what has completed those successive formations is formed, and what has not is unformed.
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r12.anchor: قال القفال : التخليق مأخوذ من الخلق فما تتابع عليه الأطوار

RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r13.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers the complete and incomplete human-form explanation because the verse addresses people who will become human; miscarriage is a less fitting referent where formation may never be complete.
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r13.anchor: والقول الأول أقرب لأنه تعالى قال في أول الآية : { فإنا خلقناكم } وأشار إلى الناس

RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r14.claim: The objection that some are not retained in the womb does not defeat his preferred view: an embryo may have complete or incomplete form and still be either retained or miscarried.
RAZI-FULL:v23p8/r14.anchor: فلنا إن ذلك لا يمنع من صحة ما ذكرنا في كون المضغة مخلقة وغير مخلقة

RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r1.claim: One explanation is that God shows His free choice by making some embryos fully formed and others incomplete.
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r1.anchor: لنبين لكم أن تغيير المضغة إلى المخلقة هو باختيار الفاعل المختار

RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r2.claim: Alternatively, the account of human origins removes doubt about resurrection: one able to create these stages can restore the dead.
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r2.anchor: إن كنتم في ريب من البعث فإنا أخبرناكم أنا خلقناكم من كذا وكذا لنبين لكم ما يزيل عنكم ذلك الريب

RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r3.claim: God retains in the womb those He brings to birth; the appointed term is the time of delivery, which may be six months, nine months, four years, or as God decrees.
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r3.anchor: من يبلغه الله تعالى حد الولادة

RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r4.claim: طفلا is singular because it denotes the generic class; alternatively, each person is brought out as an infant, like the singular of the angels in 66:4.
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r4.anchor: وإنما وحد الطفل لأن الغرض الدلالة على الجنس ويحتمل أن يخرج كل واحد منكم طفلا

RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r5.claim: Ashudd means full strength, intellect, and discernment; it is a plural-form noun with no used singular, perhaps because strength involves multiple capacities.
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r5.anchor: والأشد كمال القوة والعقل والتمييز وهو من ألفاظ الجموع التي لم يستعمل لها واحد وكأنها شدة في غير شيء واحد

RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r6.claim: God eases nurture and food so people pass through the stages between birth and maturity; an alternative says there is no intervening stage before the onset of full strength, so someone may remain an infant by age.
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r6.anchor: ثم سهل في تربيتكم وأغذيتكم أمورا لتبلغوا أشدكم فنبه بذلك على الأحوال التي بين خروج الطفل من بطن أمه وبين بلوغ الأشد

RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r7.claim: Some people die while still at their full strength and maturity.
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r7.anchor: أن منكم من يتوفى على قوته وكماله

RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r8.claim: Others return to senility and dementia, becoming physically weak, dull in mind, and slow to understand like infants.
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r8.anchor: إلى أرذل العمر وهو الهرم والخرف

RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r9.claim: Although an infant knows some things, the negation is emphatic: the old person’s reason disappears, making it as though he knows nothing.
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r9.anchor: قلنا المراد أنه يزول عقله فيصير كأنه لا يعلم شيئا لأن مثل ذلك قد يذكر في النفي لأجل المبالغة

RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r10.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects the claim that believers do not reach senility based on 95:5–6: being returned to the lowest state is blame or punishment, and the believers’ exception promises lasting reward.
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r10.anchor: ومن الناس من قال هذه الحالة لا تحصل للمؤمنين

RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r11.claim: The second proof of resurrection is plant life: just as God first creates animals, He revives dead earth with rain.
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r11.anchor: الوجه الثاني : الاستدلال بحال خلقة النبات على ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r12.claim: Hamidah describes earth that is dry and without vegetation or green growth.
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r12.anchor: وهمودها يبسها وخلوها عن النبات والخضرة

RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r13.claim: When rain falls, the land moves and swells with plants; اهتزت suggests joyful movement and is normally used for a good or beneficial event.
RAZI-FULL:v23p9/r13.anchor: والاهتزاز الحركة على سرور فلا يكاد يقال اهتز فلان لكيت وكيت إلا إذا كان الأمر من المحاسن والمنافع

RAZI-FULL:v23p9#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p9#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p9#2/r1.claim: Attributing growth to earth is metaphorical and expansive: God is the actual one who makes plants grow.
RAZI-FULL:v23p9#2/r1.anchor: فهو مجاز لأن الأرض ينبت منها والله تعالى هو المنبت لذلك

RAZI-FULL:v23p9#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p9#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p9#2/r2.claim: زوج means every kind of vegetation, including crops and planted growth; بهيج means pleasing, fresh, bright, and beautiful, as al-Mubarrad explains.

RAZI-FULL:v23p9#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p9#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p9#2/r3.claim: The succession of contrary states in bodies is evidence for a maker; this establishes that God is the real, existent, and abiding one.
RAZI-FULL:v23p9#2/r3.anchor: حدوث هذه الأمراض المتنافية وتواردها على الأجسام يدل على وجود الصانع

RAZI-FULL:v23p9#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p9#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p9#2/r9.claim: The stages of animal and plant creation demonstrate God's knowledge of all facts and power over all possibilities, the two principles on which denial of resurrection depends.
RAZI-FULL:v23p9#2/r9.anchor: قادر على كل الممكنات وعالم بكل المعلومات

STUDYQURAN:22:5/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:5/r1.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:22:5/r1.claim: Commentators connect human origin from dust both to Adam and to food animals and milk: plants nourish them, and plants grow from dust, making human bodies physically dust-derived.
STUDYQURAN:22:5/r1.anchor: Commentators see this verse as a reference not only to the fact that Adam

STUDYQURAN:22:5/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:5/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:22:5/r2.claim: The drop is understood as semen, as in the description of seed as base fluid.
STUDYQURAN:22:5/r2.anchor: The drop is often understood to refer to semen (R)

STUDYQURAN:22:5/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:5/r3.speaker: commentators (R, Ṭ)
STUDYQURAN:22:5/r3.claim: Formed and unformed flesh is generally taken to mean that some pregnancies reach term while others miscarry before a fully formed human being results; the appointed term is seen as indicating this.
STUDYQURAN:22:5/r3.anchor: while others miscarry before producing fully formed human beings (R, Ṭ).

STUDYQURAN:22:5/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:5/r4.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:22:5/r4.claim: Commentators cite a hadith describing 40 nights as a drop, then 40 as a clot, then 40 as a lump; an angel records provision, deeds, lifespan, and whether the person will be wretched or joyous.
STUDYQURAN:22:5/r4.anchor: some commentators mention a ḥadīth that states, “Your creation is such that you are brought together in your mother’s belly

STUDYQURAN:22:5/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:5/r5.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:22:5/r5.claim: Some die before old age, while the most abject life is weakness and loss of faculties in old age; the verse resembles other descriptions of declining strength and knowledge.
STUDYQURAN:22:5/r5.anchor: the most abject life refers to the weakness and loss of faculties one experiences in old age (IK).

STUDYQURAN:22:5/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:5/r6.speaker: Some commentators
STUDYQURAN:22:5/r6.claim: Some commentators say faith's strength can spare people the infirmities and weakness of old age.
STUDYQURAN:22:5/r6.anchor: Some commentators argue that people can be spared the infirmities and weaknesses of old age in accordance with the strength of their faith

STUDYQURAN:22:5/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:5/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:22:5/r8.claim: The revival of vegetation from dry earth is a recurring Quranic symbol for resurrection, linked to several passages describing dead land made alive.
STUDYQURAN:22:5/r8.anchor: The growth of vegetation from dry earth is a common symbol in the Quran for the resurrection of the dead

TAB-FULL:v16p460#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p460#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p460#2/r1.claim: The verse answers people disputing God without knowledge: if they doubt resurrection, their staged creation shows that restoring them after death is no harder for the One who first created them.
TAB-FULL:v16p460#2/r1.anchor: وهذا احتجاج من الله على الذي أخبر عنه من الناس أنه يجادل في الله بغير علم، اتباعا منه للشيطان المريد

TAB-FULL:v16p460#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p460#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p460#2/r2.claim: God recalls creating Adam from dust and then people from Adam's seed through successive stages, as evidence of His power to resurrect.
TAB-FULL:v16p460#2/r2.anchor: فإن في ابتدائنا خلق أبيكم آدم صلى الله عليه وسلم من تراب، ثم إنشائناكم من نطفة آدم، ثم تصريفناكم أحوالا

TAB-FULL:v16p460#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p460#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v16p460#2/r3.claim: Some take the adjectives as describing the drop: fully formed and sound, or expelled before becoming a formed embryo.
TAB-FULL:v16p460#2/r3.anchor: فقال بعضهم: هي من صفة النطفة. قال: ومعنى ذلك: فإنا خلقناكم من تراب، ثم من نطفة مخلقة وغير مخلقة

TAB-FULL:v16p460#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p460#2/r4.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v16p460#2/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that an angel asks whether the drop is formed; if so, it records sex, provision, lifespan, and destiny from the Mother of the Book; an unformed drop is expelled as blood.
TAB-FULL:v16p460#2/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله، قال: " إذا وقعت النطفة في الرحم

TAB-FULL:v16p460#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p460#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p460#2/r5.claim: Qatādah explains مخلقة وغير مخلقة as complete and incomplete.
TAB-FULL:v16p460#2/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، في قول الله: {مخلقة وغير مخلقة}

TAB-FULL:v16p460#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p460#2/r6.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v16p460#2/r6.claim: Another group says the adjectives describe a mudghah shaped like a human and one not yet shaped.
TAB-FULL:v16p460#2/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون: معنى ذلك المضغة مصورة إنسانا، وغير مصورة، فإذا صورت فهي مخلقة

TAB-FULL:v16p463/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p463/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p463/r1.claim: Mujāhid identifies formed and unformed cases as miscarried embryos, one formed and one not formed.

TAB-FULL:v16p463/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p463/r2.speaker: عامر
TAB-FULL:v16p463/r2.claim: ʿĀmir says a drop or embryo that reaches the fourth stage of formation is formed; one cast out earlier is unformed.
TAB-FULL:v16p463/r2.anchor: عن عامر، «أنه قال في النطفة والمضغة

TAB-FULL:v16p463/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p463/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v16p463/r3.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya glosses the phrase as miscarriage.

TAB-FULL:v16p463/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p463/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p463/r4.claim: Ṭabarī prefers fully imaged embryos as formed and miscarriage before formation is complete as unformed, when the womb expels an unshaped mudghah without ensoulment.
TAB-FULL:v16p463/r4.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب قول من قال: المخلقة المصورة خلقا تاما، وغير مخلقة: السقط قبل تمام خلقه

TAB-FULL:v16p464/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p464/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p464/r1.claim: Whomever God decrees to live until a fixed term is kept in the womb, neither miscarried nor delivered before the appointed time; God then permits birth.
TAB-FULL:v16p464/r1.anchor: منها، فيخرج. وبنحو الذي قلنا في ذلك

TAB-FULL:v16p464/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p464/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p464/r2.claim: Mujāhid glosses remaining in the womb until a fixed term as completion.
TAB-FULL:v16p464/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {ونقر في الأرحام ما نشاء

TAB-FULL:v16p464/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p464/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p464/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says the appointed term is the embryo's stay in the womb until it comes out.
TAB-FULL:v16p464/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ونقر في الأرحام ما نشاء

TAB-FULL:v16p465/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p465/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p465/r1.claim: Some die before maturity; others live past their prime into senility, becoming like children and losing knowledge they once had.
TAB-FULL:v16p465/r1.anchor: في أجله فيعمر حتى يهرم، فيرد من بعد انتهاء شبابه

TAB-FULL:v16p465/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p465/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p465/r2.claim: The oldest age means decrepitude after strength and maturity, when a person no longer understands what he previously knew.
TAB-FULL:v16p465/r2.anchor: ذلك الهرم، حتى يعود كهيئته في حال صباه لا يعقل من بعد عقله الأول شيئا

TAB-FULL:v16p465/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p465/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p465/r3.claim: Hāmidah describes dry, barren land whose plant traces have disappeared; the root denotes wearing away and extinction.

TAB-FULL:v16p465/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p465/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v16p465/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports Mujāhid's explanation of the dormant earth as land with no vegetation.
TAB-FULL:v16p465/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج، في قوله: {وترى الأرض هامدة}

TAB-FULL:v16p465/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p465/r5.speaker: الأعشى ميمون بن قيس
TAB-FULL:v16p465/r5.claim: Al-Aʿshā Maymūn ibn Qays uses همدا for worn-out garments, supporting Ṭabarī's sense of hamūd as wearing away.
TAB-FULL:v16p465/r5.anchor: ومنه قول الأعشى ميمون بن قيس: [البحر الكامل] قالت قتيلة: ما لجسمك

TAB-FULL:v16p467/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p467/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p467/r1.claim: Rain stirs barren land with vegetation and makes the plants grow and increase.

TAB-FULL:v16p467/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p467/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p467/r2.claim: Qatādah says the rain is recognized in the land's swelling.

TAB-FULL:v16p467/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p467/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p467/r3.claim: In another report, Qatādah says the land becomes good and the rain is recognized in its swelling.

TAB-FULL:v16p467/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p467/r4.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v16p467/r4.claim: Some direct the sense of “stirred” to the crops, although the verse grammatically speaks about the earth.
TAB-FULL:v16p467/r4.anchor: وكان بعضهم يقول: معنى ذلك: فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء اهتزت. ويوجه المعنى إلى الزرع

TAB-FULL:v16p467/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p467/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p467/r5.claim: Major readers have rabat, meaning growth and increase; Ṭabarī rejects Abū Jaʿfar's hamzated rabʾat as mistaken because rabʾ means guarding, which does not fit here.
TAB-FULL:v16p467/r5.anchor: وكان أبو جعفر القارئ يقرأ ذلك: (وربأت) بالهمز، حدثت عن الفراء، عن أبي عبد الله التميمي، عنه. وذلك غلط

TAB-FULL:v16p467#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p467#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p467#2/r1.claim: The dormant earth produces every kind of beautiful plant after rain; bahīj means beautiful or pleasing.
TAB-FULL:v16p467#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة: {وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج}

TAB-FULL:v16p467#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p467#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p467#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة: {وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج}

TABATABAI:22:3-5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r4.claim: The resurrection at issue is the revivification of the dead and their return to God.
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r4.anchor: المراد بالبعث إحياء الموتى والرجوع إلى الله سبحانه وهو ظاهر

TABATABAI:22:3-5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r5.claim: An ʿalaqah is a piece of clotted blood, and a muḍghah is a chewed piece of flesh.

TABATABAI:22:3-5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r6.claim: A reported interpretation takes the terms as fully formed and incompletely formed; this maps to embryo formation associated with the breathing of spirit, and thus to imaging or shaping.
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r6.anchor: المخلقة على ما قيل - تامة الخلقة

TABATABAI:22:3-5/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r7.claim: The stages demonstrate that resurrection is possible: the observed passage from dead soil through embryo stages to living human removes doubt, so the explanatory phrase appears here.
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r7.anchor: لنبين لكم أن البعث ممكن ونزيل الريب عنكم فإن مشاهدة الانتقال من التراب الميت إلى النطفة ثم إلى العلقة

TABATABAI:22:3-5/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r8.claim: God keeps in the wombs the embryos he wills, without miscarriage, until the full term, then brings them out as children.
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r8.anchor: ونقر فيها ما نشاء من الأجنة ولا نسقطه إلى تمام مدة الحمل ثم نخرجكم طفلا

TABATABAI:22:3-5/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r9.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r9.claim: Al-Majmaʿ explains the phrase as bringing children from their mothers' wombs; ṭifl is a young human and its singular can function as a collective, though it may mean each of you as a child.
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r9.anchor: قال في المجمع أي نخرجكم من بطون امهاتكم وأنتم أطفال

TABATABAI:22:3-5/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r10.claim: Reaching full strength means the stage when limbs and powers have grown strong.
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r10.anchor: والمراد ببلوغ الأشد حال اشتداد الأعضاء والقوى

TABATABAI:22:3-5/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r11.claim: The parallel clauses imply that some die before they are returned to the most decrepit age.
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r11.anchor: المقابلة بين الجملتين تدل على تقيد الأولى بما يميزها من الثانية والتقدير ومنكم من يتوفى من قبل أن يرد

TABATABAI:22:3-5/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r12.claim: The lowest age is senility, the most contemptible and weakest stage relative to what came before.
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r12.anchor: المراد بأرذل العمر أحقره وأهونه وينطبق على حال الهرم فإنه أرذل الحياه إذا قيس إلى ما قبله

TABATABAI:22:3-5/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r13.claim: The person loses knowledge that matters to the conduct of life as bodily and sensory powers weaken, until nothing of life's most valuable product remains useful.
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r13.anchor: أي شيئا يعتد به أرباب الحياة ويبنون عليه حياتهم

TABATABAI:22:3-5/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r14.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r14.claim: Raghib relates hāmida to a fire that has gone out, land without plants, or dried-up vegetation; the author says ruined or dead earth is close in sense.
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r14.anchor: يقال همدت النار طفئت، ومنه أرض هامدة لا نبات فيها

TABATABAI:22:3-5/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r15.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r15.claim: Raghib says the root denotes vigorous movement; a plant is described as moving when fresh.
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r15.anchor: الهز التحريك الشديد يقال هززت الرمح فاهتز واهتز النبات إذا تحرك لنضارته

TABATABAI:22:3-5/r16.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r16.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r16.claim: Raghib glosses rabā as increasing and rising, the growth of something reared.
TABATABAI:22:3-5/r16.anchor: ربا إذا زاد وعلا، قال تعالى

TABATABAI:22:5-7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:5-7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:5-7/r1.claim: The earth grows every plant type marked by beauty: pleasing color and an appearance that conveys joy.
TABATABAI:22:5-7/r1.anchor: أي وأنبتت الأرض من كل صنف من النبات متصف بالبهجة وهي حسن اللون وظهور السرور فيه

TABATABAI:22:5-7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:5-7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:5-7/r2.claim: Alternatively, zawj may mean a pair opposite to an individual; the Quran thus affirms plant pairing as well as plant life, which experimental sciences have confirmed.
TABATABAI:22:5-7/r2.anchor: أو المراد بالزوج ما يقابل الفرد فإن كلامه يثبت للنبات ازدواجا كما يثبت له حياة وقد وافقته العلوم التجريبية اليوم

TABATABAI:22:5-7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:5-7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:5-7/r3.claim: The earth's production and growth of plants parallels the womb's biological production of a human through the stages from soil to living person.
TABATABAI:22:5-7/r3.anchor: للأرض في إنباتها النبات وإنمائها له شأنا يماثل شأن الرحم في إنباته الحيوي للتراب الصائر نطفة ثم علقة ثم مضغة

TABATABAI:22:5-7/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:5-7/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:5-7/r9.claim: The five conclusions are selected to establish resurrection: a wholly real God produces only true acts, so human life cannot end in death without a lasting afterlife, which would make creation futile.
TABATABAI:22:5-7/r9.anchor: فإن الحق المحض لا يصدر عنه إلا الفعل الحق دون الباطل

TABATABAI:22:5-7#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:5-7#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:5-7#2/r1.claim: The argument parallels verses saying the heavens and earth were created in truth, but this passage proves resurrection from God's own truth, which entails the truth of his acts.
TABATABAI:22:5-7#2/r1.anchor: في مجرى قوله وما خلقنا السماوات والأرض

TABRISI:22:1-5/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:1-5/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABRISI:22:1-5/r3.claim: Abu Jafar reads وربأت with hamza here and in Ha Mim; the other readers read وربت.
TABRISI:22:1-5/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وربأت بالهمزة ههنا وفي حم والباقون وربت

TABRISI:22:1-5/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:1-5/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:1-5/r7.claim: ربت derives from ربا يربو, “to increase.”
TABRISI:22:1-5/r7.anchor: وأما قوله { ربت } فهو من ربا يربو إذا زاد

TABRISI:22:1-5/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:1-5/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:1-5/r8.claim: The hamzated form ربأت means to watch a group from a height; describing the ground’s elevation signals the spread of its increase.
TABRISI:22:1-5/r8.anchor: وأما الهمز فمن ربأت القوم إذا أشرفت عليهم عاليا لتحفظهم

TABRISI:22:1-5/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:1-5/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:1-5/r16.claim: A مضغة is an amount of flesh that can be chewed.
TABRISI:22:1-5/r16.anchor: والمضغة مقدار ما يمضغ من اللحم والهمود الدروس والدثور

TABRISI:22:1-5/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:1-5/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:1-5/r17.claim: همود means being effaced, dry, or worn away.

TABRISI:22:4-5/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:4-5/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:4-5/r3.claim: The author introduces the following proof of resurrection because most disputation concerned it.
TABRISI:22:4-5/r3.anchor: ثم ذكر سبحانه الحجة في البعث لأن أكثر الجدال كان فيه

TABRISI:22:4-5/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:4-5/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:4-5/r4.claim: ريب means doubt, specifically a particularly ugly or troubling doubt.
TABRISI:22:4-5/r4.anchor: } أي في شك { من البعث } والنشور والريب أقبح الشك

TABRISI:22:4-5/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:4-5/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:4-5/r5.claim: The proof is that God created humanity’s origin, Adam, from dust; the One who made living humans from dust can revive bones and restore the dead.
TABRISI:22:4-5/r5.anchor: معناه فالدليل على صحته أنا خلقنا أصلكم وهو آدم ع من تراب فمن قدر على أن يصير التراب بشرا سويا حيا

TABRISI:22:4-5/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:4-5/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:4-5/r6.claim: Human descendants are created from a small quantity of male and female fluid in the mothers’ wombs; any clear fluid is called نطفة, whether little or much.
TABRISI:22:4-5/r6.anchor: وهي الماء القليل يكون من الذكر والأنثى وكل ماء صاف فهو نطفة قل أم كثر

TABRISI:22:4-5/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:4-5/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:4-5/r7.claim: The نطفة becomes a clinging mass, a piece of congealed blood.
TABRISI:22:4-5/r7.anchor: بأن تصير النطفة علقة وهي القطعة من الدم الجامد

TABRISI:22:4-5/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:4-5/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:4-5/r8.claim: The embryo becomes something like a chewed piece of flesh; مضغة is the amount of meat one can chew.
TABRISI:22:4-5/r8.anchor: أي شبه قطعة من اللحم ممضوغة فإن معنى المضغة مقدار ما يمضغ من اللحم

TABRISI:22:4-5/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:4-5/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
TABRISI:22:4-5/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada explain the terms as fully formed and not fully formed.
TABRISI:22:4-5/r9.anchor: أي تامة الخلق وغير تامة عن ابن عباس وقتادة

TABRISI:22:4-5/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:4-5/r10.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:22:4-5/r10.claim: Mujahid explains them as shaped and unshaped, the latter being a miscarriage without visible form or features.
TABRISI:22:4-5/r10.anchor: وقيل: مصورة وغير مصورة وهي ما كان سقطا لا تخطيط فيه ولا تصوير عن مجاهد

TABRISI:22:4-5/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:4-5/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:4-5/r11.claim: The purpose may be to show God’s power by moving people through forms, to prove that the One able to originate can restore, or to remove doubt; the object of the last reading is omitted.
TABRISI:22:4-5/r11.anchor: لندلكم على مقدورنا بتصريفكم في ضروب الخلق أو لنبين لكم أن من قدر على الابتداء قدر على الإعادة

TABRISI:22:4-5/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:4-5/r12.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:22:4-5/r12.claim: Mujahid says God keeps in the wombs whatever He wills until it is fully formed.
TABRISI:22:4-5/r12.anchor: معناه ونبقي في أرحام الأمهات ما نشاء إلى وقت تمامه عن مجاهد

TABRISI:22:4-5/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:4-5/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:4-5/r13.claim: Alternatively, God keeps in the mother’s womb until its term whoever has been assigned a specified lifespan.
TABRISI:22:4-5/r13.anchor: وقيل: ونقر من قدرنا له أجلا مسمى في رحم أمه إلى أجله

TABRISI:22:4-5/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:4-5/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:4-5/r14.claim: طفلا means infants; it is singular despite referring to many because it functions like a verbal noun, as in رجل عدل and رجال عدل.
TABRISI:22:4-5/r14.anchor: والطفل الصغير من الناس وإنما وحد والمراد به الجمع لأنه بمعنى المصدر كقولهم رجل عدل

TABRISI:22:4-5/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:4-5/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:4-5/r15.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means that each one of you is brought out as an infant.
TABRISI:22:4-5/r15.anchor: وقيل: أراد ثم نخرج كل واحد منكم طفلا

TABRISI:22:4-5/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:4-5/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:4-5/r16.claim: One explanation of reaching maturity is the conjunction of reason, strength, and complete physical development.
TABRISI:22:4-5/r16.anchor: وهو حال اجتماع العقل والقوة وتمام الخلق

TABRISI:22:4-5/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:4-5/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:4-5/r17.claim: Alternatively, reaching maturity means the onset of sexual maturity and puberty; the author has discussed earlier disagreements over its meaning.
TABRISI:22:4-5/r17.anchor: وقيل: هو وقت الاحتلام والبلوغ وقد سبق تفسير الأشد واختلاف العلماء في معناه

TABRISI:22:4-5/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:4-5/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:4-5/r18.claim: Some die before maturity, in childhood or youth.
TABRISI:22:4-5/r18.anchor: أي قبل بلوغ الأشد أي يقبض روحه فيموت في حال صغره أو شبابه

TABRISI:22:4-5/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:4-5/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:4-5/r19.claim: أرذل العمر means the worst or ugliest period of life in the eyes of one’s family; alternatively, the lowest and most contemptible age.
TABRISI:22:4-5/r19.anchor: أي أسوأ العمر وأخبثه عند أهله. وقيل: أحقره وأهونه وهي حال الخوف

TABRISI:22:4-5/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:4-5/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:4-5/r20.claim: Old age is called worst because one then anticipates death and decline, unlike childhood weakness, which may lead to growth and completion.
TABRISI:22:4-5/r20.anchor: وإنما صار أرذل العمر لأن الإنسان لا يرجو بعده صحة وقوة وإنما يرتقب الموت والفناء

TABRISI:22:4-5/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:4-5/r21.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:4-5/r21.claim: One explanation is that the elderly no longer acquire knowledge and forget what they once knew.
TABRISI:22:4-5/r21.anchor: أي لكيلا يستفيد علما وينسى ما كان به عالما

TABRISI:22:4-5/r22.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:4-5/r22.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:4-5/r22.claim: Alternatively, old age may extinguish reason or erase knowledge; losing most of one’s knowledge can be described as losing all of it.
TABRISI:22:4-5/r22.anchor: وقيل: معناه لكي يصير إلى حال ينعدم عقله أو يذهب عنه علومه هرما

TABRISI:22:4-5/r23.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:4-5/r23.speaker: عكرمة
TABRISI:22:4-5/r23.claim: Ikrima says a person who has recited the Qur’an will not reach this condition, and he cites a proof that is not included in this excerpt.
TABRISI:22:4-5/r23.anchor: قال عكرمة: من قرأ القرآن لم يصير بهذه الحالة واحتج بقوله

TABRISI:22:5/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:5/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:5/r2.claim: After the preceding proof, the revival of dead earth by rain is presented as another proof of resurrection.
TABRISI:22:5/r2.anchor: ثم ذكر سبحانه دلالة أخرى على البعث فقال

TABRISI:22:5/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:5/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:22:5/r3.claim: Mujahid explains the earth as dead; the author also glosses it as dry and worn bare of vegetation.
TABRISI:22:5/r3.anchor: يعني هالكة عن مجاهد أي يابسة دارسة من أثر النبات

TABRISI:22:5/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:5/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:5/r4.claim: The water sent down upon the earth is rain.
TABRISI:22:5/r4.anchor: وهو المطر { اهتزت } أي تحركت بالنبات

TABRISI:22:5/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:5/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:5/r5.claim: The earth moves as vegetation grows; the word denotes vigorous movement in every direction.

TABRISI:22:5/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:5/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:5/r6.claim: “It grew” means the earth increased and multiplied its vegetation.

TABRISI:22:5/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:5/r7.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:22:5/r7.claim: Hasan offers the alternative that the earth swells as its vegetation appears.
TABRISI:22:5/r7.anchor: وقيل: انتفخت لظهور نباتها عن الحسن

TABRISI:22:5/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:5/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:5/r8.claim: “Every pair” means every kind, and “delightful” means pleasing to the eye in its beautiful appearance and color.
TABRISI:22:5/r8.anchor: من كل زوج } أي من كل صنف { بهيج } مؤنق للعين حسن الصورة واللون

THALABI:v7p7/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p7/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p7/r2.claim: To establish the resurrection for its deniers, God presents the stages of human creation as evidence of His power.
THALABI:v7p7/r2.anchor: ثم ألزم الحجة منكري البعث فقال عز من قائل يا أيها الناس إن كنتم في ريب

THALABI:v7p7/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p7/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p7/r3.claim: The first creation from soil is Adam, the source and father of humankind; his descendants come from a nutfah, semen.
THALABI:v7p7/r3.anchor: يعني أباكم آدم الذي هو أصل النسل ووالد البشر من تراب ثم ذريته من نطفة وهو المني

THALABI:v7p7/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p7/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p7/r4.claim: The original sense of nuṭfah is a small amount of water, and its plural is niṭāf.
THALABI:v7p7/r4.anchor: وهو المني وأصلها الماء القليل وجمعها نطاف ثم من علقة

THALABI:v7p7/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p7/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p7/r5.claim: An ʿalaqah is clotted, pure blood; its plural is ʿalaq.
THALABI:v7p7/r5.anchor: ثم من علقة وهي الدم العبيط الجامد وجمعها علق ثم من مضغة

THALABI:v7p7/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p7/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p7/r6.claim: A muḍghah is a small piece of flesh, about the size of a morsel one can chew.
THALABI:v7p7/r6.anchor: ثم من مضغة وهي لحمة قليلة قدر ما تمضع مخلقة وغير مخلقة

THALABI:v7p7/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p7/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
THALABI:v7p7/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatādah explain the terms as fully formed and not fully formed.
THALABI:v7p7/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس وقتادة: تامة الخلق وغير تامة.

THALABI:v7p7/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p7/r8.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v7p7/r8.claim: Mujāhid says they mean formed and unformed, referring to a miscarried fetus.
THALABI:v7p7/r8.anchor: وقال مجاهد: مصورة وغير مصورة يعني السقط.

THALABI:v7p7/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p7/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
THALABI:v7p7/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that an angel asks whether the drop will be formed; if not, the womb expels it as blood, while a formed pregnancy prompts questions about sex, provision, lifespan, and destiny. The angel copies its description from the Mother of the Book and keeps it until it is fulfilled.
THALABI:v7p7/r9.anchor: قال عبد الله بن مسعود: إذا وقعت النطفة في الرحم بعث الله عز وجل ملكا

THALABI:v7p7/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p7/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p7/r10.claim: The stages demonstrate the completeness of God's power and wisdom in changing the forms of human creation.
THALABI:v7p7/r10.anchor: لنبين لكم كمال قدرتنا وحكمتنا في تصريفنا أطوار خلقكم

THALABI:v7p7/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p7/r11.speaker: عاصم وغيره
THALABI:v7p7/r11.claim: ʿĀṣim reads the rāʾ in nuqirru with fatḥah, coordinating the verb; others read it with ḍamma, meaning and We settle in the wombs what We wish.
THALABI:v7p7/r11.anchor: روي عن عاصم بفتح الراء على النسق، غيره: بالرفع على معنى ونحن نقر

THALABI:v7p7/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p7/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p7/r12.claim: The appointed term is the time of birth, once the fetus has completed its form and term in the womb.
THALABI:v7p7/r12.anchor: إلى أجل مسمى وقت خروجها من الرحم تام الخلق والمدة

THALABI:v7p7/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p7/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p7/r13.claim: The singular ṭiflan stands for newborns collectively, as Arabs sometimes name a group with a singular noun.
THALABI:v7p7/r13.anchor: ثم نخرجكم من بطون أمهاتكم طفلا صغارا ولم يقل أطفالا لأن العرب تسمي الجمع باسم الواحد

THALABI:v7p7/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p7/r14.speaker: ابن جريج
THALABI:v7p7/r14.claim: Ibn Jurayj compares the singular to a verbal noun, such as ʿadl and zawr.
THALABI:v7p7/r14.anchor: وقال ابن جريج : تشبيها باسم المصدر مثل: عدل وزور،

THALABI:v7p7/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p7/r15.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v7p7/r15.claim: Another explanation compares the noun to collective terms such as khāṣm and ḍayf.

THALABI:v7p7/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p7/r16.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p7/r16.claim: Reaching one's full strength means attaining complete understanding and the peak of physical power.
THALABI:v7p7/r16.anchor: ثم لتبلغوا أشدكم كمال عقولكم ونهاية قواكم

THALABI:v7p7/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p7/r17.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p7/r17.claim: Some die before maturity; others live to senility and mental decline, until they know nothing after having had knowledge.
THALABI:v7p7/r17.anchor: ومنكم من يتوفى قبل بلوغ الأشد ومنكم من يعمر حتى يرد إلى أرذل العمر وهو الهرم والخرف

THALABI:v7p8/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p8/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p8/r1.claim: The earth is inert, dry, and stripped of traces of crops and plants, like a fire gone out.
THALABI:v7p8/r1.anchor: وترى الأرض هامدة يابسة دارسة الأثر من الزرع والنبات كهمود النار

THALABI:v7p8/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p8/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p8/r2.claim: When rain falls, the earth stirs with vegetation, swells, and grows, increasing its plants with the coming of rain.
THALABI:v7p8/r2.anchor: فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء المطر اهتزت تحركت بالنبات وربت أي زادت وأضعفت النبات

THALABI:v7p8/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p8/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر
THALABI:v7p8/r3.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads rabāʾat with hamzah, as also in 41:39; it means rose, increased, or swelled, related to Arabic for rising to a prominent place and the term for a scout.
THALABI:v7p8/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر: ربأت بالهمز، ومثله في حم السجدة أي ارتفعت وعلت وانتفخت،

THALABI:v7p8/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p8/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p8/r4.claim: The revived earth grows every beautiful kind of plant.
THALABI:v7p8/r4.anchor: وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج صنف حسن

THALABI:v7p8/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p8/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p8/r5.claim: The revived earth demonstrates that God is the Real, revives the dead, has power over all things, and will raise those in the graves at the coming Hour.
THALABI:v7p8/r5.anchor: لتعلموا بأن الله هو الحق والحق هو الكائن الثابت وأنه يحي الموتى وأنه على كل شيء قدير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes the address as directed to the people of Mecca.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد أهل مكة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257/r2.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the verse addresses polytheists who denied resurrection and were in doubt about it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257/r2.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: قيل للذين جحدوا البعث وهم المشركون إن كنتم في شك من

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257#2/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257#2/r1.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the deniers should reflect on their beginning: divine power does not differ between initiating creation and restoring it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257#2/r1.anchor: أن الله يبعث الموتى فتدبروا أمر خلقكم وابتدائكم فإنكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
