WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257#2/r2.claim: The author lays out the sequence: Adam from soil, then his descendants from a sperm-drop, a clot, and a morsel, thereby showing their creation stages.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257#2/r2.anchor: أنهم خلقوا من تراب، وهو خلق آدم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257#2/r3.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257#2/r3.claim: The author of al-Naẓm paraphrases the argument: if you doubt resurrection, God informs you that He created you from dust.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257#2/r3.anchor: صاحب النظم: معنى الآية إن كنتم في ريب من البعث فإنا نخبركم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257#2/r4.claim: Here the sperm-drop means the child of Adam, formed from the father’s semen; Arabic calls a small amount of water nuṭfa.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257#2/r4.anchor: والذي يخلق منه الولد يسمى نطفة، لأنه ماء يقطر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257#2/r5.claim: Nuṭfa derives from dripping: it can mean a clear remnant of water, a cloud’s dripping, or rain lasting through the night; semen is so named because it drips.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p257#2/r5.anchor: في الغدير نطفة زرقاء، أي بقية ماء صاف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p258/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p258/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p258/r1.claim: ʿAlaqa is thick, congealed blood before it dries, and a piece of that blood; the cited al-Qaṭāmī line witnesses the word ʿalaq.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p258/r1.anchor: العلق الدم الجامد قبل أن ييبس، والقطعة علقة منه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p258/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p258/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p258/r2.claim: The drop that forms a child thickens into blood; when the clot becomes flesh it is a muḍgha, a piece of flesh, as the human heart is a bodily morsel.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p258/r2.anchor: وذلك أن النطفة المخلوق منها الولد تصير دما غليظا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p258/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p258/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p258/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses muḍgha as flesh.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p258/r3.anchor: فهي مضغة. قال ابن عباس. يريد من

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p258/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p258/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p258/r4.claim: A hadith cited here says each stage lasts forty days—drop, clot, then morsel—after which an angel is sent to breathe in the spirit.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p258/r4.anchor: وهذا كله في الأطوار أربعة أشهر، وهذا معنى ما روي في الحديث:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p258/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p258/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p258/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the fetus is formed during the ten days after four months, then receives the spirit; this explains the widow’s four months and ten days of waiting, and movement signals pregnancy.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r1.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r1.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī says mukhallaqa is a stage whose form has begun to appear, while ghayr mukhallaqa has not yet been shaped.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r1.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي: {مخلقة} قد بدا خلقه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r2.claim: The author identifies Ibn al-Aʿrābī’s explanation of mukhallaqa as the word’s lexical sense.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r3.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r3.claim: Mujāhid, in Ibn Nujaḥ’s transmission, says the words describe miscarriage: a miscarried fetus is both formed and unformed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r3.anchor: مجاهد -في رواية ابن نجيح- {مخلقة وغير مخلقة} قال: السقط مخلوق وغير مخلوق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r4.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r4.claim: Al-Suddī details the miscarriage stages: a woman may miscarry a drop, a clot, unformed flesh, partly formed flesh, or a fully formed fetus.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r4.anchor: السدي عن هذا المعنى الذي ذكره مجاهد فقال: هذا في السقط

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r5.claim: He supports the miscarriage interpretation by reading ‘We establish in wombs what We will’ as what reaches its full term rather than being miscarried.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says mukhallaqa is what lives and ghayr mukhallaqa is miscarriage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r6.anchor: ابن عباس -في رواية عكرمة-: المخلقة ما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r7.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r7.claim: Mujāhid, in Khusayf’s transmission, identifies mukhallaqa as the child and ghayr mukhallaqa as miscarriage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r7.anchor: مجاهد -في رواية خصيف- قال: المخلقة: الولد،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, in ʿAṭāʾ’s transmission, says the formed fetus is one for whom the covenant was taken, whereas the unformed one had no covenant and is not created.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r8.anchor: ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: المخلقة: ما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r9.claim: Alqama reports from Ibn Masʿūd that an angel asks whether the drop is formed; if not, the womb expels it, but if so, the angel records sex, provision, lifespan, and destiny from the Preserved Book.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r9.anchor: روى علقمة، عن عبد الله بن مسعود

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r10.claim: He takes mukhallaqa here as fully created through the breathing of the spirit: a fetus completed alive goes to term, while miscarriage is incomplete in this sense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p259/r10.anchor: وعلى هذا القول معنى (المخلقة): المخلوقة كما ذكره ابن عباس -في رواية عطاء-

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p262/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p262/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p262/r1.claim: Al-Kalbī glosses the pair as created and uncreated: a full-term child is created, and miscarriage is uncreated; the author says this is most commentators’ view and notes Abū ʿUbayda agrees.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p262/r1.anchor: الكلبي: {مخلقة وغير مخلقة} يقول مخلوق وغير مخلوق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p262/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p262/r2.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p262/r2.claim: Qatāda understands mukhallaqa and ghayr mukhallaqa as complete and incomplete; Abū Isḥāq and Thaʿlab choose this interpretation, which concerns born children rather than miscarriage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p262/r2.anchor: قال قتادة في قوله {مخلقة وغير مخلقة}: تامة وغير تامة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p262/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p262/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p262/r3.claim: Abū Isḥāq says some morsels complete their human organs and faculties, while God does not complete the formation of others.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p262/r3.anchor: أبو إسحاق: وصف أحوال الخلق أن منهم من يتم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p262/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p262/r4.speaker: أبو العباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p262/r4.claim: Abū al-ʿAbbās says people are of two kinds: fully formed or deficient and incomplete.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p262/r4.anchor: الناس خلقوا على ضربين: منهم تام الخلق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p262/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p262/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p262/r5.claim: On the third interpretation, mukhallaqa means complete in bodily form and limbs; the author summarizes three interpretations of mukhallaqa.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p262/r5.anchor: وعلى هذا القول معنى المخلقة: التام الخلقة والأعضاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the purpose is to show people what they should do and leave, and to distinguish the best of them and what worship requires.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r1.anchor: ابن عباس: لنبين لكم ما تأتون وما تذرون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the stages of human creation demonstrate God’s power to do as He wills and inform people how He first created them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r2.anchor: وقال الزجاج: أي. ذكرنا أحوال خلق الإنسان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r3.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r3.claim: The author of al-Naẓm says the purpose is to make clear that resurrection is true, since the verse was revealed as evidence for resurrection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r3.anchor: صاحب النظم: لنبين لكم أن البعث حق يدل على هذا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r4.speaker: ابن مسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r4.claim: Ibn Muslim takes the purpose as showing how God creates people in the wombs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r4.anchor: وقال ابن مسلم: لنبين لكم كيف نخلقكم في الأرحام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r5.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r5.claim: The scholars of meaning say the varied forms of creation point people to God’s power to bring about what He can do.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r5.anchor: أهل المعاني: لندلكم على مقدورنا بتصريف ضروب الخلق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r6.claim: The phrase means God keeps in the womb what He wills rather than letting it miscarry until the appointed birth term.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r6.anchor: في الأرحام ما نشاء فلا يكون سقطا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r7.claim: Alternatively, God does not let the fetus leave before its customary term, which He decreed for it in the Preserved Book; pregnancies range from six months to four years.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى: {ونقر في الأرحام ما نشاء} فلا يخرج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r8.claim: The usual reading of ونقرُّ has the verb in the indicative; al-Mufaḍḍal reports ʿĀṣim’s accusative reading ونقرَ.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r9.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r9.claim: Abū Isḥāq rejects the accusative: God did not create humanity in order to keep people in wombs, but to guide them toward right guidance and good conduct.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r9.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: ولا يجوز فيه إلا الرفع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r10.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r10.claim: The author of al-Naẓm treats ونقر as a new independent statement after the clause ending at لنبين لكم, explaining its indicative mood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p264/r10.anchor: صاحب النظم: انقطع الخبر عند قوله {لنبين لكم}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p266/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p266/r1.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p266/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj says ṭiflan has plural sense, supported by the plural address; understood distributively, it means each of you is brought out as a child.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p266/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p266/r2.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p266/r2.claim: Al-Mubarrad parses ṭiflan as a verbal noun functioning circumstantially; others call it specification, which is possible, as in the cited construction.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p266/r2.anchor: وقال المبرد: انتصب "طفلا" على المصدر الذي هو في موضع الحال.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p266/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p266/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p266/r3.claim: The author supports the verbal-noun analysis by noting that the form occurs as a verbal noun like riḍā and ʿadl; the child wording in 24:31 is evidence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p266/r3.anchor: إلا أنا قدمنا المصدر؛ لأنه قد استعمل مصدرا كالرضا والعدل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p266/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p266/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p266/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayda also takes ṭiflan to stand for a plural, a usage he illustrates with a line of poetry.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p266/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: طفلا في موضع أطفال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p266/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p266/r5.speaker: أبو الهيثم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p266/r5.claim: Abū al-Haytham says a child is called ṭifl from birth until puberty; Arabic uses the same form for singular, dual, and plural feminine or masculine cases, but not ṭiflat.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p266/r5.anchor: وقال أبو الهيثم: الصبي يدعى طفلا حين يسقط من بطن أمه إلى أن يحتلم.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p266/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p266/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p266/r6.claim: The author gives the further forms ṭifl, ṭifla, dual ṭiflān/ṭiflatān, and aṭfāl, and says a woman or gazelle ‘has a child’ when she becomes mother to one.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p266/r6.anchor: جارية طفل، وجاريتان طفل، وجوار طفل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r1.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r1.claim: The author of al-Naẓm gives two constructions: omit ‘then We make you live’ before reaching maturity, or treat the second ثم as extra, yielding ‘We bring you out children to reach maturity.’
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r1.anchor: ذكر صاحب النظم منه وجهين: أحدهما: أن يكون فيه إضمار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r2.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r2.claim: His second construction regards ثم as inserted, like a coordinating wāw, so the sense is that people are brought out as children to attain maturity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r2.anchor: والوجه الآخر: أن تكون "ثم" في قوله {ثم لتبلغوا} مقحمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the age of full maturity as eighteen years.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد ثماني عشرة سنة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj defines full maturity as completeness, strength, and discernment, placing it between thirty and forty.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج: وتأويله الكمال والقوة والتمييز وهو ما بين الثلاثين إلى الأربعين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that some people die before reaching full maturity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد من قبل ذلك. يعني من قبل بلوغ الأشد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r6.claim: Ardhal al-ʿumur is the lowest, most decrepit age: senility, when a person becomes confused and loses the ability to reason.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says this is when age changes a person’s mind until he no longer understands anything, and says it occurs only among polytheists.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد يبلغ من السن ما يتغير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r8.speaker: عكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r8.claim: ʿIkrima says a Qurʾān reciter will not reach this state, citing the exception in 95:5–6 and interpreting those who believe and act righteously as Qurʾān readers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p268/r8.anchor: وقال عكرمة: من قرأ القرآن لم يصر بهذه الحالة، واحتج بقوله: {ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r1.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj says God demonstrates His power to revive the dead by reviving the earth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج: ثم دلهم على إحيائه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r2.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r2.claim: The author of al-Naẓm calls this a separate passage because it shifts from addressing a group to one person, but says it remains linked as evidence for resurrection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r2.anchor: وقال صاحب النظم: هذا فصل منقطع مما قبله؛ لأن الأول مخاطبة جماعة وهذا مخاطبة واحد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r3.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r3.claim: Al-Layth defines hāmida as hard, crusted earth without vegetation except broken dry remnants; a hāmid plant is dry.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r3.anchor: قال الليث: أرض جامدة مقشعرة لا نبات فيها إلا يبيس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r4.speaker: شمر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r4.claim: Shammar says hāmid is barren land without life; he also uses the root for settled, layered ash and cloth crumbling from wear.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r5.speaker: الأصمعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r5.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī says a fire hamadat when it went out completely; the cited al-Aʿshā line uses hamdan of worn-out clothes.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the earth has settled and lost its moisture.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هامدة يريد التي قد تلبدت وذهب عنها النذى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r7.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r7.claim: Mujāhid calls it perished, meaning dry and parched, since the earth’s death is its dryness.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r8.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r8.claim: Qatāda describes it as gray and broken, meaning its vegetation is shattered.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r9.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r9.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the earth is dry and covered with soil.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r9.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: يعني جافة ذات تراب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r10.speaker: ابن مسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r10.claim: Ibn Muslim describes it as dead and dry, like a fire extinguished and gone.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p270/r10.anchor: وقال ابن مسلم: ميتة يابسة كالنار إذا طفئت فذهبت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r1.claim: The commentators say the earth moves with vegetation when water falls; it rises and swells as growth appears.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r1.anchor: المعنى على هذا تحركت بالنبات عند وقوع الماء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r2.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r2.claim: Al-Layth says the expression ‘the earth trembled’ is used when it sprouts.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r3.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r3.claim: Al-Mubarrad supplies an ellipsis: ‘its vegetation trembled’; this is more apparent because vegetation is said to tremble when it grows tall.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r3.anchor: والاهتزاز في النبات أظهر، ويقال: اهتز النبات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r4.claim: Rabat means increased and grew, referring either to the earth or its plants; the root also yields rabwa and ribā.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses every pair or kind as beautiful; bahja is beauty and freshness, and bahīj is beautiful to look at and pleasing to the eye.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r5.anchor: ابن عباس: من كل صنف حسن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r6.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r6.claim: Al-Mubarrad defines bahīj as something bright and beautiful, connecting it with ‘gardens of beauty’ in 27:60.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r6.anchor: قال المبرد: هو الشيء المشرق الجميل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r7.speaker: أبو زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r7.claim: Abū Zayd analyzes bahīj as an adjective from bahija, meaning beautiful, and notes the related forms bahāja and bahja.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r7.anchor: وعلى هذا هو فعيل من بهج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r8.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r8.claim: Al-Layth cites tabāhaja al-rawḍ when a meadow fills with blossoms, with a poetic line describing its blossoms as resplendent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r8.anchor: ويقال: تباهج الروض إذا كثر نواره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r9.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p273/r9.claim: Most grammarians, including al-Akhfash and Ibn Muslim, parse bahīj here as an active-participle form.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r3.claim: The people addressed are the unbelievers of Mecca.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r3.anchor: يا أيها الناس } يعني: كفار مكة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r4.claim: Their doubt concerns being brought back to life.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r4.anchor: { إن كنتم في ريب من البعث } شك من الإعادة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r5.claim: God created humanity’s forefather, the origin of humankind, from soil.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r5.anchor: خلقناكم } خلقنا أباكم الذي أصل البشر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r6.claim: The ʿalaqa is congealed blood; the stages follow the creation of Adam’s descendants from a drop.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r6.anchor: ثم } خلقنا ذريته { من نطفة ثم من علقة } وهي الدم الجامد

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r7.claim: A muḍgha is a small piece of flesh, about the amount one could chew.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r7.anchor: وهي لحمة قليلة قدر ما يمضغ

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r8.claim: The formed stage is complete in shape; the unformed stage is what the womb expels as blood, a miscarriage.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r8.anchor: مخلقة } مصورة تامة الخلق { وغير مخلقة } وهي ما تمجه الأرحام دما، يعني: السقط

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r9.claim: The stages of human formation demonstrate the completeness of God’s power to shape creation.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r9.anchor: لنبين لكم } كمال قدرتنا بتصريفنا أطوار خلقكم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r10.claim: God keeps in the womb what will not miscarry until the appointed time of birth.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r10.anchor: ونقر في الأرحام ما نشاء } ننزل فيها ما لا يكون سقطا { إلى أجل مسمى } إلى وقت خروجه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r11.claim: God brings people from their mothers’ wombs as infants, then they reach full intellect and strength.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r11.anchor: { ثم نخرجكم } من بطون الأمهات { طفلا } صغارا { ثم لتبلغوا أشدكم } عقولكم ونهاية قوتكم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r12.claim: Some die before reaching full strength.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r12.anchor: ومنكم من يتوفى } يموت قبل بلوغ الأشد

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r13.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r13.claim: Others reach decrepit old age and senility, until they know nothing after having had knowledge.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r13.anchor: وهو الهرم والخرف حتى لا يعقل شيئا، وهو قوله: { لكيلا يعلم من بعد علم شيئا }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r14.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r14.claim: The earth is dry, with bare soil.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r14.anchor: وترى الأرض هامدة } جافة ذات تراب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r15.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r15.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r15.claim: Rain moves the earth with new growth, raises it, and brings forth every beautiful kind of plant as another sign of resurrection.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:4-5/r15.anchor: { اهتزت } تحركت بالنبات { وربت } زادت { وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج } من كل صنف حسن من النبات

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354/r8.anchor: {يأيها الناس إن كنتم في ريب من البعث} [الحج: 5] في شك من البعث.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354/r9.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354/r9.claim: Creation from soil refers to the creation of Adam.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354/r9.anchor: {فإنا خلقناكم من تراب} [الحج: 5] وهذا خلق آدم.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354#2/r1.claim: The drop is the offspring of Adam.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354#2/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354#2/r2.claim: The formed and unformed clinging substance and lump refer to miscarriage.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354#2/r2.anchor: {ثم من علقة ثم من مضغة مخلقة وغير مخلقة} [الحج: 5] قال: هو السقط.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354#2/r3.claim: Mujāhid says both the formed and unformed refer to miscarriage.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354#2/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هما جميعا السقط مخلق وغير مخلق.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354#2/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354#2/r4.claim: What God leaves in the wombs is carried to completion.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354#2/r4.anchor: {ونقر في الأرحام ما نشاء} [الحج: 5] يعني التمام.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports the Prophet describing three forty-day stages, after which an angel records provision, lifespan, deeds, and whether the person is wretched or happy.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354#2/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إن خلق أحدكم يجمع في بطن أمه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354#2/r6.speaker: أبو ذر
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354#2/r6.claim: Abū Dharr says after semen remains forty nights, the Angel of Souls asks God whether the child is male or female and wretched or happy; God decrees and the angel records its fate. Abū Dharr then recites five opening verses of al-Taghābun.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p354#2/r6.anchor: حدثني ابن لهيعة، عن بكر بن سوادة، عن أبي تميم الجيشاني، عن أبي ذر أن المني إذا مكث في الرحم أربعين ليلة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r1.claim: The purpose is to make clear how you were created.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r2.claim: The wombs are the wombs of women.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r3.claim: The appointed term is the time at which the child is born.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r3.anchor: {ما نشاء إلى أجل مسمى} [الحج: 5] الوقت الذي يولد فيه.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r4.claim: Reaching full strength means reaching puberty.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r4.anchor: {ثم نخرجكم طفلا ثم لتبلغوا أشدكم} [الحج: 5] يعني الاحتلام.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r5.claim: The omitted completion is that some die before senility, as stated explicitly in 40:67.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r5.anchor: {ومنكم من يتوفى} [الحج: 5] وفيها إضمار: أي يتوفى من قبل أن يبلغ أرذل العمر.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r6.claim: The most decrepit age means senility.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r6.anchor: {ومنكم من يرد إلى أرذل العمر} [الحج: 5] الهرم.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r7.claim: The elderly person becomes like a child who understands nothing.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r7.anchor: {لكيلا يعلم من بعد علم شيئا} [الحج: 5] يصير بمنزلة الصبي الذي لا يعقل شيئا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r8.claim: The lifeless earth is dusty and broken up.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r8.anchor: قوله: {وترى الأرض هامدة} [الحج: 5] أي: غبراء متهشمة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r9.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r9.claim: Rain makes the earth swell for growth, open, and shake with vegetation as it sprouts.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r9.anchor: {فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء اهتزت وربت} [الحج: 5] وفيها تقديم: ربت للنبات انفتحت واهتزت بالنبات إذا أنبتت.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r10.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r10.claim: He notes an inversion in the order: it swells for vegetation, then shakes as vegetation emerges.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r10.anchor: وفيها تقديم: ربت للنبات انفتحت واهتزت بالنبات إذا أنبتت.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r11.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r11.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r11.claim: Bahīj means beautiful; each kind of plant growing from earth is called a pair.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r11.anchor: {وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج} [الحج: 5] حسن. وكل ما ينبت في الأرض فالواحد منها زوج.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r12.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r12.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r12.claim: Plants are beautiful because they grow in many colors, including yellow, red, and green.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p355/r12.anchor: وحسن ذلك النبات أنها تنبت ألوانا من صفرة، وحمرة، وخضرة وغير ذلك من الألوان.

QASHANI:22:5-8/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:22:5-8/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:22:5-8/r1.claim: The earth is the soul, dead through ignorance and barren of virtues and perfections.
QASHANI:22:5-8/r1.anchor: { وترى } أرض النفس { هامدة } ميتة بالجهل لا نبات فيها

QASHANI:22:5-8/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:22:5-8/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:22:5-8/r2.claim: Knowledge descending from the spirit's heaven brings true life to the soul, advances it through spiritual ranks, and grows its beautiful virtues and perfections.
QASHANI:22:5-8/r2.anchor: { فإذا أنزلنا عليها } ماء العلم من سماء الروح

ELMALILI:22:5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:5/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:5/r1.claim: Doubt about resurrection should be dispelled because its proof is visible both in human selves and in the surrounding world.
ELMALILI:22:5/r1.anchor: zira o enfüs ü âfâkta delîlini görüp durduğunuz bir hakikattir

ELMALILI:22:5/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:5/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:5/r2.claim: Creating a living being from inert soil is a greater display of power than reviving the dead, so resurrection is certainly within God's power.
ELMALILI:22:5/r2.anchor: câmid topraktan bir zîhayat yaratmak, bir ölüyü diriltmekten daha yüksek bir kudret olduğunda şüphe mi edilir

ELMALILI:22:5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:5/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:5/r3.claim: Nutfa means semen, more precisely the seed within semen.
ELMALILI:22:5/r3.anchor: bir nutfeden bir meniden, daha doğrusu menideki tohumdan

ELMALILI:22:5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:5/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:5/r4.claim: The alaqa develops after the male nutfa fertilizes the female ovum and is a clotted mass of blood.
ELMALILI:22:5/r4.anchor: erkek nutfesinin kadın yumurtacığını telkīhinden sonra bir alekadan mütekevvin bir kan totuğundan

ELMALILI:22:5/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:5/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:5/r5.claim: The mudgha is a morsel of flesh formed from the alaqa, partly with discernible form and partly without it.
ELMALILI:22:5/r5.anchor: kısmen hilkati belirmiş kısmen de belirmemiş bir çiğnem etten yarattık

ELMALILI:22:5/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:5/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:5/r6.claim: These stages make God's power evident and bring people to clear understanding so that they do not doubt.
ELMALILI:22:5/r6.anchor: kudretimizin beyyinesini izhar edelim, sizi beyâna mazhar eyleyelim de şüphe etmeyesiniz için

ELMALILI:22:5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:5/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:5/r7.claim: The gradual stages each express a distinct form of life and entail a kind of giving life, demonstrating that the Creator can and does revive the dead.
ELMALILI:22:5/r7.anchor: her biri hayâtın bir sûret-i mahsûsasını ifade ve her mertebesinde bir nevi ihyâyı tazammun eyleyen şu tedrîcî merâtib-i hilkati

ELMALILI:22:5/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:5/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:5/r8.claim: Besides God's power, the embryonic stages also show His will and choice.
ELMALILI:22:5/r8.anchor: bunlarda kudret delilinden mâ‘adâ bir irade ve meşiyyet delîli bulunduğundan da gaflet etmemelidir

ELMALILI:22:5/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:5/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:5/r9.claim: God keeps whom He wills in the womb until an appointed term: some miscarry, while others remain for the divinely decreed gestation period; this shows His will to give life.
ELMALILI:22:5/r9.anchor: Bazılarında sıkt vâki‘oluyor, düşüyor da diğer bazıları ezelde takdir olunmuş bir müddet-i haml kadar rahimlerde duruyor

ELMALILI:22:5/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:5/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:5/r10.claim: God brings people out as infants and raises them to full strength, intellect, and discernment.
ELMALILI:22:5/r10.anchor: sonra da eşüddünüze bâliğ olmanız için yani kuvvette, akl ü temyizde kemâlinize ermeniz için büyütürüz

ELMALILI:22:5/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:5/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:5/r11.claim: Some people die before reaching maturity, after it, or just as they reach it.
ELMALILI:22:5/r11.anchor: ve sizden kiminiz vefat ettirilir büluğdan sonra veya evvel veya tam o sırada rûhu kabzolunur

ELMALILI:22:5/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:5/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:5/r12.claim: Others are returned to the most decrepit age, weakened and made helpless by old age.
ELMALILI:22:5/r12.anchor: kiminiz de ömrün erzeline reddedilir. Gerisin geri kuvvetten düşürülüp kocaltılarak pek düşkün bir hâle getirilir

ELMALILI:22:5/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:5/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:5/r13.claim: The elderly may lose knowledge and return toward the weakness and impaired understanding of infancy, approaching their origin in dust.
ELMALILI:22:5/r13.anchor: bu suretle tufûliyet hâlindeki za‘f u acz ve idraksizliğe doğru dönerek mebde’i olan türâba yaklaşır

ELMALILI:22:5/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:5/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:5/r14.claim: All these transformations within human beings prove resurrection through the power and will of the Creator, who can do whatever He wills.
ELMALILI:22:5/r14.anchor: enfüste olan bütün bu tehavvülât her dilediğini yapmaya kādir olan Hâlık teâlâ’nın kudret ü iradesiyle ba‘sin sıhhatine delâlet eyleyen beyyinâttır

ELMALILI:22:5/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:5/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:5/r15.claim: Although the image first suggests summer land dried by the sun, Elmalılı prefers a literal reading of the earth as burnt ash because it proves the point more clearly.
ELMALILI:22:5/r15.anchor: bunu teşbih tarîkiyle değil, hakikat üzere anlamak

ELMALILI:22:5/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:5/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:5/r16.claim: Elmalılı explains that earth was once burning fire and that soil is essentially the hardened, deposited ash of an extinguished fire, utterly opposed to life; he says contemporary scientific theories agree.
ELMALILI:22:5/r16.anchor: toprak esas itibariyle yanıp sönmüş bir ateşin kül hâlinde tesallüb ve teressübüdür

ELMALILI:22:5/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:5/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:5/r17.claim: When water descends, the burnt earth's particles display vital force and begin to vibrate.
ELMALILI:22:5/r17.anchor: zerrât ve eczâsı kuvve-i hayâtiye ibraz ederek bir hareket-i ihtizâziye ile teprenmekte

ELMALILI:22:5/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:5/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:5/r18.claim: The earth swells and grows after the water arrives.

ELMALILI:22:5/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:5/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:5/r19.claim: The revived earth produces plants of every beautiful kind.
ELMALILI:22:5/r19.anchor: ve her dilber çiftten nebâtât bitirmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r1.claim: To assess doubts about resurrection rationally, the verse offers clear evidence from human creation and the revival of dry earth by rain; both show that resurrection is intelligible and within God's power.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r1.anchor: Öldükten sonra dirilmenin aklen kabul edilebilirliğini ve Allah’ın buna kadir olduğunu görmek için dikkatleri iki şeye yöneltmek yeter

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r2.claim: The soil from which humanity is created may refer to Adam, humanity's first ancestor, or to the relation between bodily elements and nourishment.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r2.anchor: Topraktan yaratılma ile insanoğlunun ilk atası Hz. Âdem’in yaratılışının kastedildiği görüşünün yanı sıra, insan vücudundaki elementlerle bedenin beslenmesi arasındaki ilişkiyi öne çıkaran yorumlar da vardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r3.claim: Depending on context, nutfah can mean the man's sperm or the fertilized egg, the zygote, that this sperm produces.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r3.anchor: Nutfenin Kur’an’da farklı bağlamda farklı anlamlarda kullanıldığı görülür

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r4.claim: Considering the word's use elsewhere and embryonic development, alaqah means a fertilized egg attached to the inner wall of the uterus.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r4.anchor: Alaka kelimesinin başka âyetlerdeki kullanımı ve embriyonik gelişmeye ilişkin bilgiler dikkate alındığında bu kelimeyle aşılanmış yumurtanın ana rahminin iç cidarına asılı vaziyetinin kastedildiği anlaşılmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r5.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r5.claim: Commentators gloss muhallaka as formed, ensouled, complete, carried to normal birth, or flawless; ghayru muhallaka as unformed, not ensouled, incomplete, expelled, miscarried, or defective.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r5.anchor: muhallaka) tefsirlerde, “biçimi belirli hale gelmiş, kendisine ruh üflenmiş, tam, tamamlanmış, normal doğumla sonuçlanan, kusursuz noksansız biçimde”; ikincisi (gayru muhallaka) ise

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r6.speaker: Muhammed Esed
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r6.claim: Esed translates the pair as complete in basic elements and capacities but not yet complete in all components; the authors find the positive-negative contrast logically plausible.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r6.anchor: Muhammed Esed’in âyetin bu kısmına “(temel unsurları ve istidatlarıyla) tamamlanmış ama (bütün öğeleriyle) henüz tamamlanmamış” şeklinde mâna vermesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r7.claim: The authors reject Esed's attribution of this reading to Ibn Abbas and Qatada: the cited sources do not support that attribution.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r7.anchor: bu yorumu İbn Abbas ve Katâde’nin açıklamalarına dayandırması isabetli değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r8.speaker: Katâde
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r8.claim: Qatada's gloss transmitted by Tabari is “complete” for the first adjective and “incomplete” for the second.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r8.anchor: Taberî’nin Katâde’den naklettiği yorum birinci kelime için “tam”, ikinci kelime için “tam olmayan” şeklindedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r9.claim: Baydawi does not transmit Ibn Abbas on these terms; the authors note that Esed's source attribution is therefore mistaken.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r9.anchor: Beyzâvî ise bu konuda İbn Abbas’tan bir nakilde bulunmamıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r10.speaker: İbn Abbas
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r10.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas glosses the pair as creation completed and creation not completed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r10.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan bu ifadeyle ilgili olarak nakledilen yorum da, birinci kelime için “yaratılışı tamamlanmış”, ikinci kelime için “yaratılışı tamamlanmamış” şeklindedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r11.claim: The authors suggest Esed may have taken the report to be in Baydawi because Khazin's commentary appears immediately below Baydawi's in the collection.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r11.anchor: Hâzin’in tefsiri, Mecmû‘a mine’t-tefâsîr içindeki Beyzâvî tefsirinin hemen altında yer aldığı için Esed bu ibareyi Beyzâvî tefsiri kapsamında görmüş olabilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r12.claim: Since the verse recounts stages people pass through, it is unlikely that the first adjective means normal birth and the second miscarriage.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r12.anchor: Âyette insanların bulundukları duruma hangi aşamalardan geçerek geldiklerine değinildiğine göre birinci kelimeyi “normal doğumla sonuçlanan durumlar”, ikincisini de “düşük hali” olarak anlamak isabetli görünmemektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r13.claim: It is unclear whether the conjunction “and” between the adjectives implies a sequence, so other recorded interpretations besides normal birth and miscarriage remain possible.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r13.anchor: bu iki sıfatı birbirine bağlayan “ve” bağlacının bir sıralama anlamı taşıyıp taşımadığı açık değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r14.claim: The authors prefer reading the adjectives as referring to stages in gradual creation, which fits embryological knowledge and the flow of the passage.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r14.anchor: embriyonik gelişmeyle ilgili bilgilere ve buradaki ifade akışına uygundur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r15.claim: Several grammatical links connect being brought out as a baby with reaching maturity, but causality is strongest; hence the authors translate it as being brought out so one may later reach adulthood.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r15.anchor: bunlar arasında nedensellik bağının bulunduğu görüşü daha kuvvetli görünmektedir (İbn Âşûr, XVII, 200)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r16.claim: Because the verse immediately says some die early, it does not imply that every person born as a baby reaches adulthood.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r16.anchor: Hemen ardından kimilerinin erken vefat ettirildiği belirtildiğinden, bu ifadenin bebek olarak dünyaya gelen her insanın yetişkinlik çağına ulaşması sonucunu içerdiği ileri sürülemez

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r17.claim: The phrase erzel-i ömür means the most decrepit stage of old age.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r17.anchor: “ömrün en düşkün çağı” diye çevrilen “erzel-i ömür” deyimi hakkında bk. Nahl 16/70

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r18.speaker: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r18.claim: Elmalili renders the earth as extinguished ash: although the phrase first suggests sun-dried land, he argues a literal reading is clearer and fits scientific theories of earth as hardened, settled ash from a once-burning fire, the opposite of life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:5/r18.anchor: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi “arzı da... sönmüş kül halinde” anlamını vermiş ve bunu (özetle) şöyle açıklamıştır

QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r1.claim: Those who doubt resurrection dismiss it without considering the evidence; God answers their doubt with proof that cuts off their argument, and following guidance brings success.
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r1.anchor: فلم ينكر الحق عليهم إلا بإعراضهم عن تأمل البرهان ، واحتج عليهم في ذلك بما قطع حجتهم ، فمن تبع هداه رشد

QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r2.claim: God argues for resurrection from the stages of human creation and the transitions from infancy through youth, old age, and death: the One who first creates and changes people can raise them again.
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r2.anchor: وأنه ينقلهم من حال إلى حال أخرى ؛ فبدأهم من نطفة إلى علقة

QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r3.claim: Spring's revival of the dead winter earth shows that the One who restores it can bring life to decayed bodies and worn bones.
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r3.anchor: يحيي الأرض - في حال الربيع - بعد موتها ، فتعود إلى ما كانت عليه في الربيع

QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r4.claim: One inward gloss calls the lowest age a period of spiritual stagnation after striving.

QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r5.claim: Another gloss identifies it as being veiled after having witnessed God.

QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r6.claim: Another interpretation is returning to the pursuit of personal desires after fulfilling one's duties.

QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r7.claim: A further gloss calls it a lapse in old age.

QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r8.claim: Another interpretation is remaining in the abodes of disobedience.

QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r9.claim: Another gloss describes lingering in places of abasement.

QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r10.claim: Another view sees the lowest age as keeping company with adversaries.

QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r11.claim: Another gloss means living without recognizing one's own worth.
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r11.anchor: عيش المرء بحيث لا يعرف قدره

QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r12.claim: Another interpretation is being left to rely on oneself.

QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r13.claim: Another gloss is wandering in the illusion that anything exists independently of God.
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r13.anchor: التطوح في أودية الحسبان أن شيئا بغير الله

QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r14.claim: A final gloss describes relying on self-management while blind to God's decree.
QUSHAYRI:v2p311/r14.anchor: الإخلاد إلى تدبير النفس ، والعمى عن شهود تقدير الحق

BURHAN:v1p118/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p118/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p118/r7.claim: The parallel phrase about no longer knowing after knowledge varies by the presence or omission of مِن.
BURHAN:v1p118/r7.anchor: لكيلا يعلم من بعد علم شيئا

BURHAN:v1p345/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p345/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p345/r10.claim: Some explain Joseph's intention as an omitted aim, namely to push her away; this reading separates the two reports and parallels stopping at li-nubayyina lakum before beginning wa-nuqirru in 22:5.
BURHAN:v1p345/r10.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أنه على حذف مضاف أي هم بدفعها وعلى هذا فالوقف على ﴿ همت به ﴾ كالوقف

BURHAN:v4p104/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p104/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p104/r1.claim: Some treat renewed explicit subjects as proof of a new sentence, but Zarkashi argues that examples such as wa-nuqirru are resumptive because coordination would require different verb forms; he likewise treats wayamḥu and al-rāsikhūn as resumptive.
BURHAN:v4p104/r1.anchor: قلت وكثير من هذا لا يرد عليهم فان كلامهم في الواو العاطفة

BURHAN:v2p361/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p361/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p361/r3.claim: In uses a conditional form to address everyone although only some doubt, since a universal address adopts the majority and doubt from those not doubting is treated as uncertain.
BURHAN:v2p361/r3.anchor: فاستعمل ان مع تحقق الارتياب منهم لان الكل لم يكونوا مرتابين فغلب غير المرتابين منهم على المرتابين

BURHAN:v4p296/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p296/r1.speaker: صاحب البسيط
BURHAN:v4p296/r1.claim: The Sahib al-Basit says apparent delay varies with the time an action takes; the sequence in the example allows for lengthy stages and so does not conflict with the sense of fa in a parallel account.
BURHAN:v4p296/r1.anchor: وقال صاحب البسيط طول المدة وقصرها بالنسبة إلى وقوع الفعل فيهما فإن كان الفعل يقتضي زمنا طويلا

BURHAN:v4p296/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p296/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p296/r2.claim: A view distinguishes thumma, which looks to the beginning of the preceding event, from fa, which looks to its end, resolving why the same subject can take either particle.
BURHAN:v4p296/r2.anchor: ولهذا قال لبعضهم ثم لملاحظة أول زمن المعطوف عليه والفاء لملاحظة آخره

BURHAN:v1p420/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p420/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p420/r2.claim: Kailā is joined when negation covers a universal, since denying the whole also denies its parts; it is separated when it negates a particular, since denying a part does not negate the whole.
BURHAN:v1p420/r2.anchor: وإنما يوصل حيث يكون حرف النفي دخل على معنى كلي فيوصل لأن نفي الكلي نفي لجميع جزئياته

BURHAN:v1p420/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p420/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p420/r4.claim: Pronouns such as hum denote the named group as a whole without dividing it into separately existing parts; dividing the referent is only a mental abstraction.
BURHAN:v1p420/r4.anchor: ومن ذلك هم ونحوه من الضمائر تدل على جملة المسمى من غير تفصيل والإضمار حال لا صفة وجود

SULAMI:v2p18#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p18#4/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p18#4/r1.claim: The dead earth is still and dry; rain makes it move, swell, become moist, and sprout. As God revives earth through qualities, He revives people here through knowledge and in the afterlife through spirits.
SULAMI:v2p18#4/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله تعالى : اندرج ما علم منه بما بسط له وفتح عليه وضرب له مثلا ﴿ وترى الأرض هامدة ﴾ : أي ساكنة عن الثبات ،

ITQAN:v4p357/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p357/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p357/r1.claim: The staged creation and aging of humans, alongside land revived by rain, make observed creation and death evidence that the promised resurrection and Hour will occur.
ITQAN:v4p357/r1.anchor: وضرب لذلك مثلا بالأرض الهامدة التي ينزل عليها الماء فتهتز وتربو وتنبت من كل زوج بهيج

ITQAN:v2p321#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p321#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p321#2/r1.claim: The word بهيج means beautiful or pleasing.
ITQAN:v2p321#2/r1.anchor:
﴿ بهيج ﴾ حسن
1813 ﴿ ثاني عطفه ﴾ مستكبرا في نفسه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r11.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r11.claim: In the scope verses, al-nas refers to the people of Mecca; the wording remains general although the address is directed to Meccans.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p601#2/r11.anchor: وهو اللفظ عام وإن خوطب به أهل مكة .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p336/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p336/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p336/r1.claim: Zawj is one of two matched things of the same kind and can name either member; a man or woman may each be called zawj.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p336/r1.anchor: الزوج : ما ( كان ) له قرين من جنسه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p336/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p336/r2.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p336/r2.claim: Ibn Fāris says zawj can mean a kind or variety of plant.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p336/r2.anchor: قال ابن فارس : والزوج [ من ] النبات اللون

FARRA:v2p216/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p216/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p216/r1.claim: A circumstantial accusative can modify either definite or indefinite nouns; in هل من رجل يضرب مجردا, مجردا is a circumstantial phrase, not an adjective.
FARRA:v2p216/r1.anchor: والحال تنصب في معرفة الأسماء ونكرتها. كما تقول: هل من رجل يضرب مجردا.

FARRA:v2p216/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p216/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p216/r2.claim: Farrāʾ starts a new clause at ونقر rather than coordinating it with لنبين; reading ليبين لكم, with God as subject, would be sound, though he has not heard it.
FARRA:v2p216/r2.anchor: وقوله: (لنبين لكم ونقر في الأرحام ما نشاء) استأنف (ونقر في الأرحام) ولم يرددها على (لنبين)

FARRA:v2p216/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p216/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p216/r3.claim: أرذل العمر is the lowest age; لكيلا يعلم means that a person no longer reasons after prior knowledge and cannot understand anything.
FARRA:v2p216/r3.anchor: وقوله: (ومنكم من يرد إلى أرذل العمر) : إلى أسفل العمر (لكيلا يعلم) يقول لكيلا يعقل

FARRA:v2p216/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p216/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p216/r4.claim: The readers use ربت from ربا; Abū Jaʿfar instead read ربأت with hamza, which can mean the land rose like a lookout, but Farrāʾ rejects mistaken hamza readings of this kind.

FARRA:v2p216/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p216/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر المدني
FARRA:v2p216/r5.claim: Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī read اهتزت وربأت with hamza; if he intended a lookout's elevated place, the sense is that the ground rose to such a height.
FARRA:v2p216/r5.anchor: حدثنا أبو العباس قال حدثنا محمد قال حدثنا الفراء قال حدثني أبو عبد الله التميمي عن أبي جعفر المدني أنه قرأ (اهتزت وربأت) مهموزة

FARRA:v2p216/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p216/r6.speaker: الحسن
FARRA:v2p216/r6.claim: Farrāʾ cites al-Ḥasan's hamzated ولأدرأتكم as another mistaken hamza and says such forms are rejected in recitation.
FARRA:v2p216/r6.anchor: وهو كما قرأ الحسن (ولأدرأتكم به) يهمز. وهو مما يرفض من القراءة.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p290#4/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p290#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p290#4/r2.claim: Ghayr mukhallaqah means not fully formed, referring to a miscarriage.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p290#4/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p290#4/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p290#4/r3.claim: The purpose is to make clear how God creates people in the wombs.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p290#4/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p290#4/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p290#4/r4.claim: Some people die before reaching senility.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p290#4/r4.anchor: {ومنكم من يتوفى} يعني قبل بلوغ الهرم.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p290#4/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p290#4/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p290#4/r5.claim: The worst age is dementia and old age.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p290#4/r5.anchor: {ومنكم من يرد إلى أرذل العمر} أي الخرف والهرم.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p290#4/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p290#4/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p290#4/r6.claim: Hāmidah means dead and dry; a fire is called hāmid when extinguished.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p290#4/r6.anchor: {وترى الأرض هامدة} أي ميتة يابسة. ومثل ذلك همود النار: إذا طفئت فذهبت.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p290#4/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p290#4/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p290#4/r7.claim: The earth stirs with plants and swells.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p290#4/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p290#4/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p290#4/r8.claim: Bāhīj means beautiful and joy-giving; it is an active participle, as in the phrase for a woman of pleasing character.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p290#4/r8.anchor: {وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج} أي من كل جنس حسن، يبهج، أي يشرح. وهو فعيل في معنى فاعل.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r5.claim: Karīm can mean good or beautiful: good plant species, beautiful growth, and gracious speech; all these senses derive from nobility.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r5.anchor: والكريم: الحسن، وذلك من الفضل. قال الله تعالى: أولم يروا إلى الأرض كم أنبتنا فيها من كل زوج كريم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p173/r10.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p173/r10.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p173/r10.claim: A singular may stand for a group: ضيف, رسول, and طفل appear in singular form for plural referents.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p41/r10.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p41/r10.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p41/r10.claim: The codex writes ما نشؤا with wāw after alif in Shuʿayb's verse, while the same form elsewhere lacks wāw, without a difference in meaning.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p41/r10.anchor: بواو بعد الألف، وفي موضع آخر

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r1.claim: حزن describes elevated, rough ground; if it rises a little more, it is حزم.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r1.anchor: ولما ارتفع من الأرض: حزن فإن زاد قليلا قيل: حزم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r2.claim: A person who feels cold is خصر; if also hungry, the word is خرص.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r2.anchor: وللذي يجد البرد: خصر فإن كان مع ذلك جوع قيل: خرص

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r3.claim: A fire that has gone out is هامدة; خامدة describes one whose flame died while embers remain.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r3.anchor: وللنار إذا طفئت: هامدة فإن سكن اللهب وبقي من جمرها شيء قيل: خامدة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r4.claim: The source distinguishes صائم, a person made stationary by injury, from صائن, one whose standing results from foot injury or soreness.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r4.anchor: وللقائم من الخبل: صائم فإن كان ذلك من حفى أو وجى، قيل: صائن

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r5.claim: شكد is a gift; شكم is one given in requital.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r5.anchor: وللعطاء: شكد فإن كان مكافأة قيل: شكم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r6.claim: غلط is an unintentional mistake generally, while غلت is an error in calculation.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r6.anchor: وللخطأ من غير التعمد: غلط فإن كان في الحساب قيل: غلت

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r7.claim: خوص describes a narrow eye; حوص refers to narrowness at its rear corner.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r7.anchor: وللضيق في العين: خوص فإن كان ذلك في مؤخرها قيل: حوص

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r8.claim: Arabic derives terms for belly conditions: مبطن for lean, بطين for naturally large, مبطان from overeating, بطن for a glutton, and مبطون for a belly ailment.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r8.anchor: كاشتقاقهم من البطن للخميص: مبطن وللعظيم البطن إذا كان خلقة: بطين

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r9.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r9.claim: وجد can mean finding a lost object, anger, sadness, or self-sufficiency; its nouns vary respectively as وجود or وجدانا, وجدا, موجدة, and وجدا.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r9.anchor: ثم يجعلون الاسم الضالة: وجودا ووجدانا وفي الحزن وجدا وفي الغضب موجدة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r10.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r10.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r10.claim: Arabic poetry serves as a book: a storehouse of knowledge, guardian of etiquette, record of genealogies, and durable register of history.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r10.anchor: وللعرب الشعر الذي أقامه الله تعالى لها مقام الكتاب لغيرها، وجعله لعلومها مستودعا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r11.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r11.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r11.claim: Meter, rhyme, ordering, and careful choice protect poetry from falsification, which is easier in prose.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r11.anchor: وحرسه بالوزن، والقوافي، وحسن النظم، وجودة التخيير- من التدليس والتغيير

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r12.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r12.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r12.claim: Departures from poetic convention are called sinād, iqwāʾ, ikfāʾ, or iṭwāʾ; this segment defines sinād and begins iqwāʾ.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r12.anchor: وقد تجد الشاعر منهم ربما زال عن سننهم شيئا، فيقولون له: ساندت، وأقويت، وأكفأت

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r13.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r13.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r13.claim: Sinād involves differing rhyme supports or letters before them; ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm’s lines contrast kasra in فأصبحينا with fatḥa in جرينا.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r13.anchor: كقول عمرو بن كلثوم : ألا هبي بصحنك فاصبحينا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r14.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r14.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r14.claim: Iqwāʾ is described as a letter omitted from the first hemistich; the promised poetic example is not included here.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p19/r14.anchor: وخالف في (الإقواء) بحرف نقصه من شطر البيت الأول

MAJAZ:v1p7/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p7/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p7/r6.claim: A singular form can carry a plural meaning: “a child” in 22:5 stands for “children.”
MAJAZ:v1p7/r6.anchor: ومن مجاز ما جاء لفظه لفظ الواحد الذي له جماع منه

NAHHAS:v3p87/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p87/r1.speaker: الكوفيون
NAHHAS:v3p87/r1.claim: Kufan grammarians allow words whose second consonant is guttural to alternate between sukun and fatḥa, citing نعل and بخل; Abu Ishaq rejects that general rule and says usage is lexeme-specific, as with وعد and قدر.
NAHHAS:v3p87/r1.anchor: وأجاز الكوفيون في كل ما كان ثانية حرفا من حروف الحلق

NAHHAS:v3p87/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p87/r2.speaker: أبو عبيد
NAHHAS:v3p87/r2.claim: Abu Ubayd defines العلقة as blood once its redness has become intense.
NAHHAS:v3p87/r2.anchor: قال أبو عبيد العلقة الدم إذا اشتدت حمرته

NAHHAS:v3p87/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p87/r3.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v3p87/r3.claim: Al-Kisa'i allows مخلقة and غير مخلقة in the accusative, construing them as verbal or detached forms.
NAHHAS:v3p87/r3.anchor: قال الكسائي ويجوز ( مخلقة ) بالنصب ( وغير مخلقة ) على الفعل

NAHHAS:v3p87/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p87/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p87/r4.claim: The purpose is to show God's power to shape people as He wills.
NAHHAS:v3p87/r4.anchor: أي لنبين لكم قدرتنا على تصويرنا ما نشاء

NAHHAS:v3p87/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p87/r5.speaker: عاصم
NAHHAS:v3p87/r5.claim: A report from Abu Hatim transmits Asim's accusative reading ونقر, coordinated with لنبين.
NAHHAS:v3p87/r5.anchor: وروى أبو حاتم عن أبي زيد عن المفضل عن عاصم ( لنبين لكم ونقر في الأرحام ما نشاء )

NAHHAS:v3p87/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p87/r6.speaker: أبو حاتم
NAHHAS:v3p87/r6.claim: Abu Hatim says the accusative ونقر is coordinated with the preceding verb.
NAHHAS:v3p87/r6.anchor: قال أبو حاتم النصب على العطف

NAHHAS:v3p87/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p87/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p87/r7.claim: Abu Ishaq insists on indicative ونقر: people were not created to remain in wombs, but to be guided toward right and good.
NAHHAS:v3p87/r7.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق ( ونقر ) بالرفع لا غير لأنه ليس المعنى

NAHHAS:v3p87/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p87/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p87/r8.claim: Abu Ishaq says طفل is singular in form but means children collectively, with each person brought out as a child.
NAHHAS:v3p87/r8.anchor: قال وطفل بمعنى أطفال قال ودل على ذلك لفظ الجميع

NAHHAS:v3p87/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p87/r9.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p87/r9.claim: Abu Ishaq understands يُتوفى as reaching the full term of one's life.
NAHHAS:v3p87/r9.anchor: ومن قرأ ( ومنكم من يتوفى ) فمعناه عنده يستوفي أجله

NAHHAS:v3p87/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p87/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p87/r10.claim: Arذal al-ʿumur is advanced age, when a person no longer hopes for strength or a long life.
NAHHAS:v3p87/r10.anchor: أي إلى الكبر لأنه لا يرجو قوة ولا طول عمر

NAHHAS:v3p87/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p87/r11.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v3p87/r11.claim: Al-Farra glosses the phrase as losing the ability to reason after one's former understanding.
NAHHAS:v3p87/r11.anchor: مذهب الفراء لكي لا يعقل من بعد عقله الأول شيئا

NAHHAS:v3p87/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p87/r12.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v3p87/r12.claim: Al-Kisa'i gives the Arabic forms بهج بهجة and بهاجة.
NAHHAS:v3p87/r12.anchor: قال الكسائي يقال بهج بهجة وبهاجة

SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r1.claim: من البعث may be attached directly to ريب.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r1.anchor: قوله: { من البعث }: يجوز أن يتعلق ب " ريب " ،

SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r2.claim: Alternatively, من البعث may be an omitted adjective qualifying ريب.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يتعلق بمحذوف على أنه صفة ل ريب.

SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r3.speaker: الحسن
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads البعث with a fatḥa on ʿayn, a dialectal form alongside the version with a quiescent ʿayn.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن " البعث " بفتح العين. وهي لغة كالطرد والجلب

SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r4.claim: The Shaykh says Kufans permit easing a guttural-middle word by quiescing it, while Basrans do not generalize this rule and treat attested forms as lexical alternatives.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r4.anchor: قال الشيخ: " والكوفيون إسكان العين عندهم تخفيف [يقيسونه] فيما وسطه حرف حلق

SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r5.claim: The author clarifies that the dispute is whether a heard form with an open guttural may be quiesced, not whether every quiescent guttural form must originally have been open.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r5.anchor: قلت: فهذا يوهم ظاهره أن الأصل البعث بالفتح، وإنما خفف، وليس الأمر كذلك، وإنما محل النزاع

SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r6.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r6.claim: The general reading has مخلقة and غير مخلقة in the genitive as adjectives; Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads both accusative as circumstantial phrases from an indefinite noun, rare though Sibawayh analogizes it.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r6.anchor: العامة على الجر في " مخلقة " ، وفي " غير " ، على النعت.

SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r7.claim: علقة is a clotted piece of blood; an anonymous answer about the hardest thing uses the phrase وقع الزلق على العلق for slipping on battlefield blood.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r7.anchor: والعلقة: القطعة من الدم الجامدة. وعن بعضهم وقد سئل عن أصعب الأشياء فقال:

SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r8.claim: مضغة is a piece of flesh about the size of a mouthful; الغرفة and الأكلة similarly name what is scooped or eaten.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r8.anchor: والمضغة: القطعة من اللحم قدر ما تمضغ نحو: الغرفة والأكلة

SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r9.claim: مخلقة means smooth and flawless, from صخرة خلقاء; خلقت السواك means that one shaped and smoothed the tooth-stick.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r9.anchor: والمخلقة: الملساء التي لا عيب فيها من قولهم: صخرة خلقاء أي: ملساء.

SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r10.speaker: الشعبي
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r10.claim: Al-Shaʿbī, Qatāda, and Abū al-ʿĀliya say the doubled form signals abundant creation, since a human has many differing limbs and formations.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5/r10.anchor: وقيل: التضعيف في " مخلقة " دلالة على تكثير الخلق لأن الإنسان ذو أعضاء متباينة وخلق متفاوتة. قاله الشعبي

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r1.claim: The general reading has ونقر in the indicative as a new clause, not as a coordinated purpose clause.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r1.anchor: قوله: { ونقر } العامة على رفع " ونقر " لأنه مستأنف، وليس علة لما قبله

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r2.speaker: يعقوب
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r2.claim: Yaʿqūb and a transmission from ʿĀṣim read ونقر in the subjunctive.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب وعاصم في رواية بنصبه.

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r3.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ analyzes the subjunctive as formally coordinated with لنبين but serving a different sense: its implied lām denotes an outcome.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " على أن يكون معطوفا في اللفظ، والمعنى مختلف؛ لأن اللام في " لنبين " للتعليل،

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r4.claim: The author objects that an implied lām makes ونقر subjunctive through an understood أن after that lām, not by direct coordination with the preceding phrase.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r4.anchor: وفيه نظر؛ لأن قوله " معطوفا في اللفظ " يدفعه قوله: " واللام المقدرة " فإن تقدير اللام يقتضي النصب بإضمار " أن "

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r5.speaker: عاصم
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r5.claim: A separate transmission from ʿĀṣim reads the jīm of نخرجكم with fatḥa, in the subjunctive.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r5.anchor: وعن عاصم أيضا " ثم نخرجكم " بنصب الجيم.

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r6.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads ليبين ويقر with yāʾ in both verbs, with God as the agent as in the nūn reading.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة " ليبين ويقر " بالياء من تحت فيهما، والفاعل هو الله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r7.speaker: يعقوب
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r7.claim: In another transmission, Yaʿqūb reads ونقر with fatḥa on nūn, ḍamma on qāf, and indicative ending, from قر الماء meaning to pour water.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب في رواية " ونقر " بفتح النون وضم القاف ورفع الراء،

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r8.speaker: أبو زيد النحوي
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r8.claim: Abū Zayd al-Naḥwī reads ويقر with yāʾ fatḥa, qāf kasra, and subjunctive ending, meaning God pours or settles it.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ أبو زيد النحوي " ويقر " بفتح الياء من تحت وكسر القاف ونصب الراء

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r9.speaker: ابن جبارة
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r9.claim: Ibn Jibāra's al-Kāmil records the preferred nūn forms of لنبين ونقر ثم نخرجكم all in the subjunctive.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r9.anchor: وفي " الكامل " لابن جبارة " لنبين ونقر ثم نخرجكم " بالنصب فيهن

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r10.speaker: أبو حاتم
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r10.claim: Abū Ḥātim reports the two verbs with yāʾ and subjunctive endings; ʿUmar ibn Shabba reports the yāʾ forms in the indicative.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r10.anchor: بالياء فيهما مع النصب: أبو حاتم، وبالياء والرفع عمر بن شبة

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the indicative reports that God settles in the wombs whom He wishes to keep there.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r11.anchor: وقال الزمخشري:/ " والقراءة بالرفع إخبار بأنه تعالى يقر في الأرحام ما يشاء أن يقره ".

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the subjunctive coordinates two purposes: demonstrating divine power and keeping some in the wombs until birth, growth, and maturity for legal responsibility; ثم لتبلغوا أشدكم supports this.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r12.anchor: ثم قال: " والقراءة بالنصب تعليل، معطوف على تعليل. معناه: خلقناكم مدرجين، هذا التدريج لغرضين،

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r13.claim: The author objects to calling acts attributed to God purposes or ends.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r13.anchor: قلت: تسمية مثل هذه الأفعال المسندة إلى الله تعالى غرضا لا يجوز.

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r14.speaker: ابن وثاب
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r14.claim: Ibn Waththāb reads نشاء with kasra on the initial nūn, a kasra on the imperfect prefix discussed earlier in the work.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#2/r14.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب " نشاء " بكسر النون، وهو كسر حرف المضارعة،

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r1.claim: طفلا is a circumstantial accusative from the object of نخرجكم; al-Mubarrad explains its masculine singular form by its origin as a verbal noun like رضا and عدل.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r1.anchor: قوله: { طفلا } حال من مفعول " نخرجكم " ، وإنما وحد لأنه في الأصل مصدر كالرضا والعدل،

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r2.claim: The singular may be generic, or mean each individual among you; it may also agree with the intended number, as in طفلان and أطفال.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r2.anchor: إما لأنه مراد به الجنس، وإما لأن المعنى: يخرج كل واحد منكم نحو: القوم يشبعهم رغيف

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r3.claim: A hadith asks about the children of the polytheists, illustrating the plural أطفال.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r3.anchor: وفي الحديث: " سئل عن أطفال المشركين "

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r4.claim: الطفل names a child from birth until puberty; الطفل with fatḥa means soft or delicate, and a woman may be called طفلة, as in the cited verse.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r4.anchor: والطفل يطلق على الولد من حين الانفصال إلى البلوغ.

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r5.claim: The cited line uses طفلة for a soft or delicate girl; no poet is named in the source.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r5.anchor: وأما الطفل بالفتح فهو الناعم، والمرأة طفلة قال: 3371 ولقد لهوت بطفلة ميالة

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r6.claim: With both ṭāʾ and fāʾ open, الطفل is the time after midafternoon when the sun inclines to set; أطفلت المرأة means she became a mother.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r6.anchor: أما الطفل بفتح الطاء والفاء فوقت ما بعد العصر، من قولهم: طفلت الشمس

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r7.speaker: فرقة
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r7.claim: A group reads يتوفى with fatḥa on its initial yāʾ; one analysis makes God the subject and supplies the object, as al-Zamakhshari does.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r7.anchor: وقرأت فرقة " يتوفى " بفتح الياء. وفيه تخريجان، أحدهما: أن الفاعل ضمير الباري تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r8.speaker: فرقة
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r8.claim: The other analysis makes من the subject and takes the meaning as reaching the end of one's appointed term, like 2:234.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r8.anchor: والثاني: أن الفاعل ضمير " من " أي: يتوفى أجله.

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r9.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Nāfiʿ are reported to read العمر with a quiescent ʿayn, a regular lightening like عنق.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#3/r9.anchor: وروي عن أبي عمرو ونافع أنهما قرآ " العمر " بسكون العين

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r1.claim: لكيلا is syntactically attached to يرد; a similar construction was discussed under Sūrat al-Naḥl.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r1.anchor: قوله: { لكيلا } متعلق ب " يرد ". وتقدم نظيره في النحل.

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r2.claim: هامدة is a circumstantial accusative because ترى describes visual perception.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r2.anchor: و " هامدة " نصب على الحال لأن الرؤية بصرية.

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r3.claim: Humūd means stillness or abasement; a land is هامدة when dry and ruined, and a garment is هامد when worn, as al-Aʿshā's verse illustrates.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r3.anchor: والهمود: السكون والخشوع. وهمدت الأرض: يبست ودرست. وهمد الثوب: بلي. قال الأعشى: 3372 قالت قتيلة

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r4.claim: Al-Aʿshā's line uses همدا of garments that have become worn.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r4.anchor: قال الأعشى: 3372 قالت قتيلة ما لجسمك شاحبا وأرى ثيابك باليات همدا

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r5.claim: اهتزت means moved; here movement figuratively describes the earth's sprouting after rain.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r5.anchor: والاهتزاز: التحرك، وتجوز به هنا عن إنبات الأرض نباتها بالماء.

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r6.claim: The common reading ربت means increased, from ربا يربو.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r6.anchor: والجمهور على " ربت " أي: زادت، من ربا يربو.

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r7.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, and a report from Abū ʿAmr read وربأت with hamza, meaning rose or elevated; the form is illustrated by ربأ بنفسه and ربيئة.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وعبد الله ابن جعفر وأبو عمرو في رواية " وربأت " بالهمز أي ارتفعت.

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r8.claim: The hamzated reading relates to a lookout on a high place, also called ربيء; a cited poetic line contains ربيئا.
