SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r8.anchor: ومنه الربيئة وهو من يطلع على موضع عال لينظر للقوم ما يأتيهم.

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r9.claim: The anonymous poetic line uses ربيئا for a lookout sent in advance.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#4/r9.anchor: ويقال له " ربيء " أيضا قال الشاعر: 3373 بعثنا ربيئا قبل ذلك مخملا

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#5/r1.claim: من كل زوج may qualify an omitted object, understood as colors or kinds from every pair.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#5/r1.anchor: قوله: { من كل زوج } فيه وجهان، أحدهما: أنه صفة للمفعول المحذوف

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#5/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#5/r2.claim: Alternatively, من is extra, yielding the sense أنبتت كل زوج; this analysis is accepted by Kufans and al-Akhfash.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#5/r2.anchor: والثاني: أن " من " زائدة أي: أنبتت كل زوج. وهذا ماش عند الكوفيين والأخفش.

SAMIN-DURR:22:5#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#5/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#5/r3.claim: بهيج means beautiful and pleasing to the eye; بهج means to be lovely, and أبهجني means that its beauty pleased me.
SAMIN-DURR:22:5#5/r3.anchor: والبهيج: الحسن الذي يسر ناظره. وقد بهج بالضم بهاجة وبهجة أي: حسن.

ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r1.claim: A reading opens the عين in al-baʿth; the Kufans allow such vowel alternation in a quiescent second radical when it is a guttural and the first is open, citing pairs such as نعل/نعل and شعر/شعر.

ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r2.speaker: البصريون
ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r2.claim: The Basrans say both forms are used only when both are attested; an unattested form such as وعد cannot be shifted, and the rule is not limited to guttural letters.
ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r2.anchor: فأما البصريون فيزعمون أن ما جاء

ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r3.claim: The challenge to doubters is to reflect on their own creation: divine power has no difficulty originating life or bringing the dead back.
ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r3.anchor: فتدبروا أمر خلقكم وابتدائكم فإنكم لا تجدون في القدرة فرقا بين ابتداء الخلق وإعادته

ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r4.claim: The stages are Adam created from dust, then his descendants created from a drop, a clot, and a morsel of flesh.
ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r4.anchor: خلقوا من تراب، وهو خلق آدم عليه السلام

ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r5.claim: A report says the embryo remains a drop for forty days, then a morsel for forty days, after which an angel is sent to breathe in the spirit.
ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r5.anchor: ويروى أن الإنسان يكون في البطن نطفة

ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r6.claim: Mukhallaqa describes the created forms or stages.

ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r7.claim: Some embryos complete the morsel stage and develop the organs that finish the human body's faculties, while others do not complete development.
ZAJJAJ:v3p411/r7.anchor: أو منهم من يتمم مضغته فتخلق له الأعضاء التي تكمل آلات الإنسان ومنهم من لا يتمم الله خلقه

ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r1.claim: The purpose clause refers to the account just given: God has described the stages of human creation.

ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r2.claim: Alternatively, God created people in this way in order to make matters clear to them.
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r2.anchor: ووجه آخر هو خلقناكم هذا الخلق

ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r3.claim: The verb نقر is read only in the indicative nominative, not as a purpose coordinated with لنبين.

ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r4.claim: It cannot mean that humans were created in order for God to keep embryos in wombs; human creation is for guidance and right conduct.
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r4.anchor: لم يخلق الأنام لما يقر في الأرحام

ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r5.claim: Although طفل is singular, it has the plural sense أطفال, as the address is plural; each person is brought out as a child.
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r5.anchor: في معنى أطفال، ودل عليه ذكر الجماعة

ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r6.claim: Ashudd means full strength and discernment, reached between ages thirty and forty.

ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r7.claim: The most decrepit age is the senility of old age, when a person loses reason, as the following clause explains.
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r7.anchor: أرذل العمر هو الذي يخرف فيه الإنسان من الكبر حتى لا يعقل

ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r8.claim: The earth is هامدة when dry and reduced to dust.

ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r9.claim: The earth's shaking is its movement when water falls on it and it begins to grow vegetation.
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r9.anchor: فاهتزازها تحركها عند وقوع الماء بها وإنباتها

ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r10.claim: The word is also read وربأت with hamza; the unhamzated reading derives from ربا يربو, to increase in any direction, while the hamzated form means it rose.
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r10.anchor: ومن قرأ: (وربت) فهو من ربا يربو

ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r11.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r11.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r11.claim: A bahij pair or kind means every beautiful species of plant.
ZAJJAJ:v3p412/r11.anchor: أي من كل صنف حسن من النبات

ASAD-NOTES:22:5#n4/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:22:5#n4/r1.speaker: Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah
ASAD-NOTES:22:5#n4/r1.claim: Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah interpret the two phrases as the various stages of embryonic development; Asad says his “complete yet incomplete” rendering conforms to their view.
ASAD-NOTES:22:5#n4/r1.anchor: mukhallaqah wa-ghayr mukhallaqah by Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah

ASAD-NOTES:22:5#n4/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:22:5#n4/r2.speaker: Tabari
ASAD-NOTES:22:5#n4/r2.claim: Tabari explains ghayr mukhallaqah as the mudghah stage before individual life, when no soul has yet been breathed into it.
ASAD-NOTES:22:5#n4/r2.anchor: Tabari explains the expression ghayr mukhallaqah as denoting the stage at which the embryonic lump (mudghah) has as yet no individual life

ASAD-NOTES:22:5#n4/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:22:5#n4/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:22:5#n4/r3.claim: Creation from dust indicates humanity's lowly biological origin and affinity with other earthy substances.
ASAD-NOTES:22:5#n4/r3.anchor: man's lowly biological origin and his affinity with other "earthy" substances

ASAD-NOTES:22:5#n5/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:22:5#n5/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:22:5#n5/r1.claim: Asad directs readers to his note on 16:70 for the parallel discussion of declining knowledge in old age.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p584/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p584/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p584/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses lā rayba fīhi as “there is no doubt,” with a verse by ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zibʿarī as Arabic evidence.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p584/r1.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: لا شك فيه. وشاهده قول عبد الله بن الزبعري

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p584/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p584/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p584/r2.claim: Bint al-Shāṭiʾ surveys Qur’anic uses of negated and unnegated rayb and its derivatives; the phrase شك مريب, repeated six times, shows rayb and shakk are not synonyms.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p584/r2.anchor: وقد يبدو تفسير الريب بالشك قريبا، لولا أن البيان القرآني أتى بالريب وصفا لشك فى (شك مريب) ست مرات، فلفت ذلك إلى فرق بين اللفظين لا يترادفان

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p585/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p585/r1.speaker: الطبري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p585/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains murīb as something that brings its possessor feared harm, from arāba for causing suspicion or committing a shameful act; an anonymous rajaz line illustrates the root.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p585/r1.anchor: وفى تأويل الطبرى لقوله تعالى، (إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا فِي شَكٍّ مُرِيبٍ)

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p585/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p585/r2.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p585/r2.claim: Al-Rāghib defines rayb as suspecting something and later finding it unlike one’s expectation; in rayb al-manūn, uncertainty concerns when death comes, not whether it comes.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p585/r2.anchor: قال: الريب أن تتوهم بالشيء أمرا فينكشف عما تتوهمه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p585/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p585/r4.speaker: القرطبي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p585/r4.claim: Al-Qurṭubī lists three senses of rayb: doubt, accusation, and need, supported respectively by verses from Ibn al-Zibʿarī, Jamīl, and Kaʿb ibn Mālik.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p585/r4.anchor: أحدها الشك ومنه قول ابن الزبعري

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p585/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p585/r5.speaker: ابن فارس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p585/r5.claim: Ibn Fāris says the root denotes doubt or doubt mixed with fear; rayb al-dahr refers to time’s reversals, imagined as crafty.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p585/r5.anchor: فى (مقاييس اللغة، ريب: أصل يدل على شك، أو شك وخوف

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p585/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p585/r6.speaker: ابن الأثير
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p585/r6.claim: Ibn al-Athīr gives rayb as doubt, sometimes joined with accusation, and distinguishes rābanī from arābanī in certainty about an accusation.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p585/r6.anchor: وقال " ابن الأثير" فى الريب: هو بمعنى الشك. وقيل هو الشك مع التهمة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#2/r10.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#2/r10.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#2/r10.claim: In al-Hajj, the Resurrection setting makes 'lifeless' apt: the earth revives, swells, and produces varied growth as evidence of resurrection.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#2/r10.anchor: إن الجو في السياق الأول جو بعث وإحياء وإخراج

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p797/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p797/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p797/r1.claim: طفل is not confined to one child: Arabic uses the same form for singular, dual, and plural, so its use in Qur'anic passages can be generic.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p797/r1.anchor: والطفل تأتي للمفرد والمثنى والجمع فنقول: جارية طفل وجاريتان طفل وجواري طفل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p797/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p797/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p797/r2.claim: In al-Hajj the verse describes human creation as a species, not individual children, which suits the generic singular طفل.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p797/r2.anchor: الآيات تتكلم عن خلق الجنس وليس عن خلق الأفراد فكل الجنس جاء من نطفة ثم علقة ثم مضغة لذا جاءت كلمة "طفل"

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p839/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p839/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p839/r1.claim: He distinguishes the joined لكيلا from لكي لا: من بعد علم means immediately after knowledge, while بعد علم can allow a time gap; the spelling reflects that temporal distinction.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p839/r1.anchor: فلمّا احتمل الفاصل فصل (لكي لا) وعندما وصل بينهما وصل (لكيلا)

NASHR:v2p154/r15.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p154/r15.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p154/r15.claim: كيلا is counted as joined in four places, including this verse, Aal Imran, the second Ahzab instance, and al-Hadid; the claim that the first Ahzab instance is joined is rejected.
NASHR:v2p154/r15.anchor: (وكيلا) كتب موصولا في أربعة مواضع في آل عمران لكيلا تحزنوا

NASHR:v1p3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p3/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
NASHR:v1p3/r1.claim: The Prophet quotes God: whoever is occupied by the Qurʾān instead of remembrance and asking will receive better than those who ask; al-Tirmidhī grades the report ḥasan gharīb.
NASHR:v1p3/r1.anchor: من حديث أبي سعيد الخدري - رضي الله عنه - قال: قال رسول الله

NASHR:v1p3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p3/r2.speaker: أبو العلاء الهمذاني
NASHR:v1p3/r2.claim: Some routes gathered by Abū al-ʿAlāʾ specify that reading the Qurʾān to learn or teach it occupies one instead of supplication and asking.
NASHR:v1p3/r2.anchor: وقد جمع الحافظ أبو العلاء الهمذاني طرق هذا الحديث وفي بعضها

NASHR:v1p3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p3/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
NASHR:v1p3/r3.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that the best act of worship is reciting the Qurʾān.
NASHR:v1p3/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة - رضي الله عنه - عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: أفضل العبادة قراءة القرآن

NASHR:v1p3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p3/r4.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
NASHR:v1p3/r4.claim: Al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr reports the Prophet saying that reciting the Qurʾān is his community’s best worship; al-Bayhaqī includes it in Shuʿab al-Īmān.
NASHR:v1p3/r4.anchor: عن النعمان بن بشير - رضي الله عنهما - قال

NASHR:v1p3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p3/r5.speaker: سفيان الثوري
NASHR:v1p3/r5.claim: Asked whether fighting or teaching Qurʾān is preferable, Sufyān al-Thawrī chooses teaching, citing the Prophetic saying that the best people learn and teach it.
NASHR:v1p3/r5.anchor: سألت سفيان الثوري عن الرجل يغزو أحب إليك أو يقرئ القرآن؟

NASHR:v1p3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
NASHR:v1p3/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Qurʾān reciters are not returned to decrepit old age; he reads the exception in 95:5, those who believe, as those who recite Qurʾān.
NASHR:v1p3/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس - رضي الله عنهما - قال:

NASHR:v1p3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p3/r7.speaker: عبد الملك بن عمير
NASHR:v1p3/r7.claim: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr says the most enduring in intellect are the Qurʾān’s reciters.

NASHR:v1p3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p3/r8.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
NASHR:v1p3/r8.claim: A report says Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal dreamt that God named His speech as the best approach and answered that understanding it or not understanding it both count.
NASHR:v1p3/r8.anchor: سمعت عبد الله بن أحمد بن حنبل يقول: سمعت أبي

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p32#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p32#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p32#2/r1.claim: Qatāda glosses the formed and unformed embryo as complete and incomplete.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p32#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ مخلقة وغير مخلقة ﴾ قال تامة وغير تامة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p32#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p32#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p32#2/r2.claim: Qatāda says the earth becomes beautiful and that rainfall is visible in its swelling.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p32#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ اهتزت وربت ﴾ قال حسنت وعرف الغيث في ربوها

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p32#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p32#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p32#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ اهتزت وربت ﴾ قال حسنت وعرف الغيث في ربوها ﴿ وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج

ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r1.claim: The verse presents proof to silence disputants after warning of their end; people here most likely means unbelievers who dispute and deny resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r1.anchor: إقامة للحجة التي تلقم المجادلين في البعث حجرا أثر الإشارة إلى ما يؤل إليه أمرهم واستظهر أن المراد بالناس هنا الكفرة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r2.claim: Calling their certainty of impossibility mere doubt signals the weakness of their case: even obstinate deniers can only allege doubt against clear evidence; indefinite wording and إن further diminish it.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r2.anchor: وأما الجزم بعدم الإمكان فخارج من دائرة الإحتمال كما أن تنكيره وتصديره بكلمة الشك للإشعار بأن حقه أن يكون ضعيفا مشكون الوقوع

ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r3.claim: The conditional wording avoids saying directly that they doubt the resurrection: any doubt lies on their side, and the phrase treats them as persistently immersed in it without implying it is strong.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r3.anchor: وإنما لم يقل وإن ارتبتم في البعث للمبالغة في تنزيه أمره عن شائبة وقوع الريب والإشعار بأن ذلك إن وقع فمن جهتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r4.claim: The preposition من is partitive in origin and attaches to an omitted adjective describing doubt; the author prefers doubt about resurrection's possibility, while occurrence is also possible but the following proof only establishes possibility and verse 22:7 already states it will occur.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r4.anchor: ومن ابتدائية متعلقة بمحذوف وقع صفة للريب واستظهر أن المراد في ريب من إمكان البعث

ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r5.claim: Al-Hasan reads البعث with a fatḥa on the ʿayn; Basrans treat it as a dialect variant, while Kufans call the usual sukūn a regular lightening of a middle guttural.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( من البعث ) بفتح العين

ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r6.claim: The clause explains the conditional answer, or means implicitly: consider your origin and your doubt will vanish; an estimate meaning I will inform you is less apt.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r6.anchor: دليل جواب الشرط أو الجواب بتأويل أي وإن كنتم في ريب من البعث فانظروا إلى مبدأ خلقكم ليزول ريبكم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r7.claim: Humanity's creation from soil means either the creation of Adam from it or the formation of semen from food grown in it; although food includes other elements, soil predominates, and the author prefers the first account.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r7.anchor: وخلقهم من تراب في ضمن خلق آدم عليه السلام منه أو بخلق الأغذية التي يتكون منها المني منه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r8.claim: Nutfah is a drop, from dripping, and here means the semen from which each individual is immediately created; al-Naqqash's view that it means Adam's semen is exceedingly remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r8.anchor: أي مني من النطف بمعنى التقاطر وقال الراغب

ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r9.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r9.claim: Al-Raghib defines nutfah as pure water and says it is used for a man's semen; the author replies that the word also denotes semen generally, so the definition does not exclude that usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r9.anchor: قال الراغب : النطفة الماء الصافي ويعبر بها عن ماء الرجل

ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r10.claim: An ʿalaqah is a formed piece of clotted blood, and a muḍghah is a piece of flesh formed from it, about the size of what can be chewed.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r10.anchor: قطعة من الدم جامدة متكونة من المني

ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r11.claim: The two forms are genitive adjectives of muḍghah; Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads both in the accusative as circumstantial qualifiers, a rare construction Sibawayh permits by analogy.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة بالنصب فيهما على الحال من النكرة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r12.claim: The common reading means a morsel whose form has become visible and one not yet formed; limbs first remain indistinct, then appear gradually. The unformed state comes second because it is privative, and intensive morphology reflects many separately formed organs.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p115#2/r12.anchor: أن المخلقة المستبينة الخلق أي مضغة مستبينة الخلق مصورة ومضغة لم يستبن خلقها وصورتها بعد

ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r1.claim: Another lexical reading takes mukhallaqah as smoothed and free of defect, from verbs meaning to smooth wood or a stone; the opposite has defects, yielding variation in people's forms, stature, and completeness.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r1.anchor: المخلقة المسواة الملساء من النقصان والعيب

ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r2.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والشعبي وأبي العالية وعكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r2.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, al-Sha'bi, Abu al-Aliya, and Ikrima say the formed one completes its term and develops stage by stage, while the unformed one miscarries before term.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r2.anchor: وعن مجاهد وقتادة والشعبي وأبي العالية وعكرمة أن المخلقة التي تم لها مدة الحمل

ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r3.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports that an angel asks God whether the settled semen is to be formed; if so, the angel asks its sex, fortune, lifespan, provision, and place of death. The report is treated as Prophetic.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r3.anchor: عن مسعود قال : النطفة إذا استقرت في الرحم أخذها ملك الأرحام

ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r4.claim: The people are described as coming from the kind of semen that completes formation or miscarries, not literally from both kinds, since a miscarried semen does not produce a person; the contrast magnifies divine power.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r4.anchor: والمراد أنهم خلقوا من جنس هذه النطفة الموصوفة بالتامة والساقطة لا أنهم خلقوا من نطفة تامة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r5.claim: Unlike 23:14, where each stage creates the next, here every stage is a starting point in the creation of human beings, further displaying God's power.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r5.anchor: وفي جعل كل واحدة من هذه المراتب مبدأ لخلقهم لا لخلق ما بعدها من المراتب كما في قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r6.claim: The purpose clause attaches to خلقنا; its object is omitted for grandeur and breadth, encompassing truths and subtleties beyond enumeration.

ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r7.claim: The gradual creation teaches the reality of resurrection: the one who originated humans from lifeless soil and transformed them through disparate stages can restore them, more easily by analogy.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r7.anchor: فإن من تأمل فيما ذكر من الخلق التدريجي جزم بأن من قدر على خلق البشر أولا من تراب

ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r8.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r8.claim: Some specify the omitted object as the matter of resurrection, but the author considers the broader, unstated object better.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r8.anchor: وقدّر بعضهم المفعول خاصا أي لنبين لكم أمر البعث

ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r9.claim: The author rejects as very far-fetched the claim that the point is to show creation is a choice of the agent, otherwise some embryos would not be formed.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r9.anchor: وأبعد جدا من زعم أن المعنى لنبين لكم أن التخليق اختيار من الفاعل

ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r10.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
ALUSI-FULL:v17p116/r10.claim: Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads ليبين with a third-person yāʾ, an instance of rhetorical shift in person.

ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r1.claim: The majority read ونقر with nūn; the clause resumes to describe what follows completion of the creation stages.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور بالنون والجملة استئناف مسوق لبيان حالهم بعد تمام خلقهم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r2.claim: The appointed term is birth; al-Ālūsī gives six months as the minimum and two years as the maximum gestation period in his school.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r2.anchor: هو وقت الوضع وأدناه ستة أشهر وأقصاه عندنا سنتان

ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r3.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r3.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī is reported to allow a maximum gestation period of four years, unlike al-Ālūsī's two-year limit.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r3.anchor: وعند الشافعي عليه الرحمة أربع سنين

ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r4.speaker: يعقوب
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r4.claim: Yaʿqūb reads نَقَرُّ with fatḥa on nūn and ḍamma on qāf, from a verb meaning to pour water.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r4.anchor: وعن يعقوب أنه قرأ ( ونقر ) بفتح النون وضم القاف من قررت الماء إذا صببته

ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r5.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r5.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb reads the nūn in نشاء with kasra.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r5.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب ما نشاء بكسر النون

ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r6.claim: God brings people out of the wombs after keeping them there until the appointed term is complete.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r6.anchor: أي من الأرحام بعد إقراركم فيها عند تمام الأجل المسمى

ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r7.claim: طفلا is circumstantial from the plural addressee, singular either by considering each person individually or as a collective that applies to many.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r7.anchor: طفلا ( حال من ضمير المخاطبين والأفراد إما باعتبار كل واحد منهم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r8.speaker: المبرد
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r8.claim: Al-Mubarrad treats طفل as a verbal noun, identical in form for singular and plural.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r8.anchor: أو لأنه مصدر فيستوي فيه الواحد وغيره كما قال المبرد

ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r9.speaker: جلال الدين السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r9.claim: Al-Suyūṭī transmits an analysis in which طفل طفل is understood, with the repetition elided.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r9.anchor: أو لأن المراد طفلا طفلا فاختصر كما نقله الجلال السيوطي

ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r10.speaker: عمر بن شبة
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r10.claim: ʿUmar ibn Shabba reads the verb with yāʾ, يخرجكم.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r10.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن ( شبة ) يخرجكم بالياء

ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r11.claim: أشدكم means full strength, intellect, and discernment.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r11.anchor: أي كمالكم في القوة والعقل والتمييز

ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r12.speaker: القاموس
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r12.claim: Al-Qāmūs places the age of full strength between eighteen and thirty years.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r12.anchor: وفي القاموس حتى يبلغ أشده ويضم أوله أي قوته وهو ما بين ثماني عشرة سنة إلى ثلاثين

ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r13.claim: The lexicon offers morphological accounts of أشد as a plural-like form without a matching singular, an unusual plural of شدة, or a proposed form related to شد.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r13.anchor: واحد جاء على بناء الجمع كآنك ولا نظير لهما أو جمع لا واحد له من لفظه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r14.speaker: أبو السعود
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r14.claim: Abū al-Suʿūd takes لتبلغوا as a purpose of bringing people out, alongside the implied purpose that they grow gradually and then mature.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r14.anchor: قال العلامة : أبو السعود : علة لنخرجكم معطوف على علة أخرى مناسبة لها

ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r15.claim: Another parse supplies an omitted verb: God then gives people time to reach maturity.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r15.anchor: وقيل علة لمحذوف والتقدير ثم نمهلكم لتبلغوا

ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r16.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r16.claim: Al-Ṭībī allows maturity to be understood as the purpose of the preceding retention in the womb and delivery.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r16.anchor: وجوز العلامة الطيبي أن يكون التقدير ( ثم لتبلغوا أشدكم ) كان ذلك الإقرار والإخراج

ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r17.claim: A proposed coordination of لتبلغوا with لنبين is criticized as damaging the eloquent structure; the accusative reading permits نقر and نخرج to coordinate with لنبين.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r17.anchor: وقيل إنه عطف على نبين وتعقبه العلامة بأنه مخل بجزالة النظم الكريم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r18.speaker: المفضل وأبو حاتم
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r18.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal and Abū Ḥātim read نقر and نخرج in the accusative, coordinated with لنبين; the former uses nūn and the latter yāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r18.anchor: وهي قراءة المفضل وأبي حاتم إلا أن الأول قرأ بالنون والثاني قرأ بالياء

ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r19.claim: On the accusative reading, gradual creation serves to disclose God's signs and keep people in the wombs, then deliver them as children and bring them to maturity.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r19.anchor: خلقناكم على التدريج المذكور لأمرين أحدهما أن نبين شؤننا والثاني أن نقركم في الأرحام

ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r20.claim: Although disclosure comes to completion after the stages, it is placed first to mark it as the ultimate and essential aim.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r20.anchor: وتقديم التبيين على ما بعده مع أن حصوله بالفعل بعد الكل للإيذان بأنه غاية الغايات

ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r21.claim: Repeating the purpose lām at maturity marks it as more fundamental than gestation and delivery, since maturity brings responsibility and the path to felicity or misery.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r21.anchor: للإشعار بأصالة البلوغ بالنسبة إلى الإقرار والإخرج إذ عليه يدور التكليف المؤدي إلى السعادة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r22.claim: The verse says people reach maturity rather than saying God brings them to it, focusing on their mature state and ability to act.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p117/r22.anchor: وإيثار البلوغ مسندا إلى المخاطبين على التبليغ مسندا إليه تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r1.speaker: ابن الحاجب
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r1.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib argues that making نقر accusative under لنبين is semantically weak: creation causes disclosure, not retention in the womb.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r1.anchor: قال في شرح المفصل : إنه مما يتعذر فيه النصب إذ لو نصب عطفا على ( نبين ) ضعف المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r2.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says نقر can only be nominative, since people were created for guidance and right conduct, not to remain in the wombs.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r2.anchor: وقال الزجاج : لا يجوز في ( ونقر ) إلا الرفع ويجوز أن يكون معناه فعلنا ذلك لنقر

ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r3.claim: The author answers that the ultimate aim is fitness for religious responsibility, so gestation and delivery can be included as prerequisites.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r3.anchor: وأجيب بأن الغرض في الحقيقة هو بلوغ الصلوح للتكليف لكن لما كان الإقرار وما تلاه من مقدماته

ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r4.claim: The author reads the criticism of the nominative coordination as an indirect allusion to al-Zamakhsharī's analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r4.anchor: فالظاهر أنه تعريض بالزمخشري حيث جعل العطف على ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r5.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r5.claim: Al-Kashf prefers the well-known nominative reading: نقر is coordinated with خلقناكم rather than serving as another purpose of creation.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r5.anchor: ففي الكشف أن القراءة بالرفع هي المشهورة الثابتة في السبع وهي الأولى

ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r6.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r6.claim: In al-Kashf's account, retention is not itself a purpose; maturity is the goal, while the present tense depicts the scene and marks special attachment.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r6.anchor: حتى لم يجعل الإقرار في الأرحام علة بل جعل الغرض منه بلوغ الأشد

ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r7.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r7.claim: The placement of ثم before reaching maturity marks maturity as the primary purpose for which humans were created.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r7.anchor: وكذلك في الإتيان بثم في قوله سبحانه ثم لتبلغوا دلالة على أنه الغرض الأصيل

ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r8.claim: Because the earlier stages make resurrection evident, the disclosure clause comes before the womb and delivery clauses.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118/r8.anchor: ولما كانت الأوائل في الدلالة على البعث أظهر قدم قوله تعالى لنبين على الإقرار والإخراج

ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r1.claim: The death and old-age clauses resume the account to distinguish outcomes after emergence from the womb, as the earlier clauses distinguished prenatal stages.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r1.anchor: ( ومنكم من يتوفى ( الخ استئناف لبيان أقسام الإخراج من الرحم كما استوفى أقسام الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r2.claim: Maturity is the state most deserving to be the purpose of creation, though some die before attaining it and others outlive it.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r2.anchor: وفيه تبيين تفضيل حال بلوغ الأشد وأنها الحقيق بأن تكون مقصودة من الإنشاء

ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r3.claim: Some people die before reaching full maturity.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r3.anchor: أي منكم من يموت قبل بلوغ الأشد

ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r4.claim: Arذal al-ʿumur is the worst and lowest stage of life, resembling childhood.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r4.anchor: أي أرداه وأدناه والمراد يرد إلى مثل زمن الطفولية

ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r5.claim: After much knowledge, the aged person knows nothing or nothing of what was known; the wording intensifies the reversal and loss of former ability.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r5.anchor: واللام متعلقة بيرد وهي لام العاقبة والمراد المبالغة في النتقاص عمله

ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r6.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r6.claim: Al-Baḥr says there is no fixed age for this decline; it varies with people's temperaments.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r6.anchor: وليس لزمان ذلك الرد حد محدود بل هو مختلف باختلاف الأمزجة على ما في البحر

ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r7.speaker: إرشاد العقل السليم
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r7.claim: The passive forms of يُتوفى and يُردّ follow the language of divine majesty because the agent is understood.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r7.anchor: وإيراد الرد والتوفي على صيغة المبني للمفعول للجري على سنن الكبرياء لتعين الفاعل

ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r8.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r8.claim: Al-Ṭībī calls maturity the best phase, when knowledge and action become firm; infancy is wondrous and decrepit old age is worst.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r8.anchor: أن بلوغ الأشد أفضل الأحوال والإخراج أبدعها والرد إلى أرذل العمر أسوؤها

ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r9.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r9.claim: Al-Ṭībī says old age reverses maturity by stripping away knowledge and the ability to act.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p118#2/r9.anchor: ثم يميتكم أو يردكم إلى أرذل العمر الذي يسلب فيه العلم والقدرة على العمل

ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r1.claim: The wording can mean some die after maturity; another possibility is death at maturity, though the author objects to its proposed circumstantial parsing.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r1.anchor: ويفهم منه جواز أن يكون المراد ومنكم من يتوفى بعد بلوغ الأشد

ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r2.claim: An unnamed analysis makes the clause circumstantial and takes death to occur at maturity; al-Ālūsī dismisses that parsing.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r2.anchor: وقيل : إن ذلك يجعل الجملة حالية ومن صيغة المضارع وهو كما ترى

ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r3.claim: A variant reads يتوفى as active; its subject may be God, who takes the person, or the person who completes his lifespan.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r3.anchor: وقريء ( يتوفى ) على سيغة المعلوم وفاعله ضمير الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r4.claim: Under the second analysis of the active reading, the subject is the person who fulfills his allotted lifespan.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r4.anchor: وجوز أن يكون ضمير من أي ( من ) يستوفي مدة عمره

ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو ونافع
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r5.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Nāfiʿ are reported to pronounce the mīm of العمر without a vowel.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r5.anchor: وروي عن أبي عمرو ونافع تسكين ميم العمر

ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r6.claim: Changing human states after birth, like the prenatal stages, alert people to resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r6.anchor: ما في اختلاف أحوال الإنسان بعد الإخراج من الرحم من التنبيه على صحة البعث

ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r7.claim: Revived earth is a second proof of resurrection, an outward cosmic sign complementing the earlier inward proof from human formation.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r7.anchor: حجة أخرى على صحة البعث معطوفة على ( إنا خلقناكم ) وهي حجة آفاقية

ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r8.claim: The address is to anyone capable of sight; another view addresses the disputant. The author takes ترى as physical sight, not intellectual inference.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r8.anchor: والخطاب لكل أحد من تتأتى منه الرؤية وقيل : للمجادل وصيغة المضارع

ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r9.claim: Hāmidah describes dead, dry earth; the root also describes worn cloth and a fire reduced to ashes.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r9.anchor: أي ميتة يابسة يقال همدت الأرض إذا يبست ودرست وهمد الثوب إذا بلى

ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r10.speaker: الأعشى
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r10.claim: Al-Aʿshā's line uses همدا for worn-out garments, illustrating the root's sense of decay.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r10.anchor: وقال الأعشى : قالت قتيلة ما لجسمك شاحبا وأرى ثيابك باليات همدا

ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r11.claim: The root's original image comes from a fire that has turned to ashes.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r11.anchor: وأصله من همدت النار إذا صارت رمادا

ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r12.claim: The water is most naturally rain because it is sent down; another view extends it to springs and rivers too.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r12.anchor: أي ماء المطر وقيل : ما يعممه وماء العيون والأنهار وظاهر الإنزال يقتضي الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r13.claim: The vegetation moves, with motion attributed to the earth figuratively; alternatively, the soil loosens as plants emerge. Motion in quality is an unlikely sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r13.anchor: تحرك نباتها فالإسناد مجازي أو تخلخلت وانفصل بعض أجزائها عن بعض

ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r14.claim: The earth swells and increases as water and vegetation enter it.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r14.anchor: ازدادت وانتفخت لما يتداخلها من الماء والنبات

ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r15.speaker: أبو جعفر وعبد الله بن جعفر وخالد بن الياس وأبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r15.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, Khālid ibn Ilyās, and one transmission from Abū ʿAmr read وربأت with hamza, meaning rose or elevated.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r15.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وعبد الله بن جعفر وخالد بن الياس وأبو عمرو في رواية ( وربأت ) بالهمز

ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r16.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r16.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya relates the hamzated reading to a lookout rising to high ground; the earth seems to stretch upward after rain.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r16.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : هو من ربأت القوم إذا علوت شرفا من الأرض طليعة عليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r17.claim: زوج means a kind or class of vegetation.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119/r17.anchor: ( وأنبتت من كل زوج ( أي صنف ( بهيج

ALUSI-FULL:v17p119#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p119#2/r1.claim: The closing description means a beautiful sight that pleases the viewer.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#2/r2.claim: The sequence of human creation is offered as evidence against those who deny resurrection after becoming dust.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#2/r2.anchor: وكان ينكر البعث وإحياء من صار ترابا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r3.claim: The first human, Adam, is meant by creation from dust; his descendants are meant by the subsequent stages.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r3.anchor: يعني: أباكم آدم الذي هو أصل النسل،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r4.claim: Nuṭfah is semen, literally a small quantity of water; its plural is nuṭāf.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r4.anchor: والنطفة هي المني، وأصلها الماء القليل وجمعها نطاف،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r5.claim: An ʿalaqah is thick, clotted blood; its plural is ʿalaq.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r5.anchor: وهي الدم الغليظ المتجمد، وجمعها علق،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r6.claim: The drop becomes thick blood and then flesh.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r6.anchor: وذلك أن النطفة تصير دما غليظا ثم تصير لحما،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r7.claim: A muḍghah is a small piece of flesh about the amount one could chew.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r7.anchor: وهي لحمة قليلة قدر ما يمضغ،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatādah say mukhallaqah is fully formed and ghayr mukhallaqah is incomplete.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس وقتادة: "مخلقة" أي تامة الخلق، "وغير مخلقة" غير تامة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r9.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r9.claim: Mujāhid says the terms mean shaped and unshaped, referring to a miscarriage.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r9.anchor: وقال مجاهد: مصورة وغير مصورة، يعني السقط.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r10.claim: Another view identifies the formed one as a child delivered at term and the unformed one as a miscarriage.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r10.anchor: وقيل: "المخلقة" الولد الذي تأتي به المرأة لوقته، "وغير المخلقة" السقط.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r11.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r11.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that an angel takes the settled drop and asks God whether it is to be formed; if not, it is expelled as blood, and if so the angel records its sex, fortune, lifespan, deeds, provision, and place of death from the Mother Book.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p365#3/r11.anchor: روي عن علقمة عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: إن النطفة إذا استقرت في الرحم أخذها ملك بكفه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r1.claim: The stages demonstrate the completeness of God’s power and wisdom in shaping creation and allow people to infer resurrection from the initial creation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r1.anchor: كمال قدرتنا وحكمتنا في تصريف أطوار خلقكم ولتستدلوا بقدرته في ابتداء الخلق على قدرته على الإعادة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r2.claim: Another explanation is that God clarifies what people should do, avoid, and need for worship.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r2.anchor: وقيل: لنبين لكم ما تأتون وما تذرون وما تحتاجون إليه في العبادة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r3.claim: God keeps in the womb what He wills rather than letting it be expelled or miscarried, until the appointed time of complete birth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r3.anchor: فلا تمجه ولا تسقطه، {إلى أجل مسمى} وقت خروجها من الرحم تامة الخلق والمدة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r4.claim: Ṭiflan is singular although the referent is plural because Arabic can use a singular noun for a group; another explanation likens it to verbal nouns such as ʿadl and zūr.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r4.anchor: ولم يقل: أطفالا لأن العرب تذكر الجمع باسم الواحد. وقيل: تشبيها بالمصدر مثل عدل وزور.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r5.claim: Ashudd means full maturity and strength.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r5.anchor: ثم لتبلغوا أشدكم} يعني: الكمال والقوة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r6.claim: Some die before reaching old age; others are returned to the most decrepit age, when their minds change and they know nothing after having known.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r6.anchor: من قبل بلوغ الكبر، {ومنكم من يرد إلى أرذل العمر} أي: الهرم والخرف،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r7.claim: Hāmidah describes dry land without vegetation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r7.anchor: هامدة} أي: يابسة لا نبات فيها،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r8.claim: Rain makes the land move as plants rise; it lifts and grows. Another ordering is “grew and moved,” with “its vegetation” understood as omitted.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r8.anchor: تحركت بالنبات وذلك أن الأرض ترتفع بالنبات فذلك تحركها،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r9.speaker: أبو جعفر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r9.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads rabaʾat with hamza, also in Fuṣṣilat, meaning that the land rose and became elevated.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p366/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر: " وربأت " بالهمزة، وكذلك في حم السجدة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p367/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p367/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p367/r1.claim: The land produces every pleasing kind of plant, a delight to whoever sees it; this is another proof of resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p367/r1.anchor: أي: صنف حسن يبهج به من رآه، أي: يسر، فهذا دليل آخر على البعث.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r1.claim: Doubt about resurrection concerns whether it is possible and within divine power.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r2.claim: A reading vocalizes البعث with fatḥa like الجلب.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r3.claim: Consider your beginning of creation: it removes doubt about resurrection by demonstrating the first creation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r3.anchor: أي فانظروا في بدء خلقكم فإنه يزيح ريبكم فإنا خلقناكم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r4.claim: Human creation is from dust through Adam, or through foods from which semen forms.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r4.anchor: بخلق آدم منه، أو الأغذية التي يتكون منها المني.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r5.claim: Nuṭfa is semen, named from flowing; ʿalaqa is a clotted piece of blood, and muḍgha a piece of flesh about the amount one chews.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r5.anchor: مني من النطف وهو الصب. { ثم من علقة } قطعة من الدم جامدة. { ثم من مضغة } قطعة من اللحم

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r6.claim: The pair may mean formed without flaw versus unformed, complete versus miscarried, or shaped versus not shaped.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r6.anchor: مسواة لا نقص فيها ولا عيب وغير مسواة أو تامة وساقطة أو مصورة وغير مصورة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r7.claim: Staged development displays power and wisdom and shows that what undergoes change and formation once can be formed again; the omitted object signals that these acts disclose more than can be enumerated.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r7.anchor: بهذا التدريج قدرتنا وحكمتنا وأن ما قبل التغير والفساد والتكون مرة قبلها أخرى، وأن من قدر على تغييره

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r8.claim: God keeps in the wombs those whom He wills to keep.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r8.anchor: ونقر فى الأرحام ما نشاء } أن نقره.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r9.claim: The appointed term is the time of birth: at least six months and at most four years.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r9.anchor: هو وقت الوضع وأدناه بعد ستة أشهر وأقصاه أربع سنين

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r10.claim: The accusative reading coordinates “we keep” and “we bring you out” with “to make clear,” expressing the aims of showing power and keeping people until birth, growth, and accountability; yāʾ readings occur in raised and accusative forms, alongside يقر.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r10.anchor: وقرىء «ونقره» بالنصب وكذا قوله: { ثم نخرجكم طفلا } عطفا على «نبين»

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r11.claim: In the form ونقر, the verb can derive from قررت الماء, “I poured the water.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r11.anchor: وقرئا بالياء رفعا ونصبا ويقر بالياء { ونقر } من قررت الماء إذا صببته

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r12.claim: Ṭiflan is circumstantial, construed distributively, generically, or as a word originally used as a verbal noun.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r12.anchor: طفلا } حال أجريت على تأويل كل واحد أو للدلالة على الجنس أو لأنه في الأصل مصدر.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r13.claim: Ašudd is full maturity in strength and reason; it is the plural of šidda, analogous to anʿām as the plural of niʿma.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r13.anchor: كمالكم في القوة والعقل جمع شدة كالأنعم جمع نعمة كأنها شدة في الأمور.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r14.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r14.claim: Some die when they reach maturity or before; a reading has يتوفاه الله instead of يتوفى.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r14.anchor: عند بلوغ الأشد أو قبله. وقرىء { يتوفى } أو يتوفاه الله تعالى.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r15.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r15.claim: The most decrepit age is senility and dementia; a reading has a still mīm.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r15.anchor: وهو الهرم والخرف، وقرىء بسكون الميم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r16.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r16.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r16.claim: At extreme old age a person returns to childhood’s weak intellect and limited understanding, forgetting what he did and denying what he knew.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r16.anchor: ليعود كهيئته الأولى في أوان الطفولية من سخافة العقل وقلة الفهم فينسى ما عمله

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r17.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r17.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r17.claim: This is a second proof that resurrection is possible: God brings about contrasting human conditions across the lifespan, and the one able to do that can recreate their like.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r17.anchor: والآية استدلال ثان على إمكان البعث بما يعتري الإنسان في أسنانه من الأمور المختلفة

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r18.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r18.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r18.claim: The earth is lifeless and dry; hāmidat derives from a fire becoming ash.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r18.anchor: ميتة يابسة من همدت النار إذا صارت رمادا.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r19.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r19.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r19.claim: After rain the earth moves with plants and swells; a reading, وربأت, means that it rises.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r19.anchor: تحركت بالنبات. { وربت } وانتفخت، وقرىء «وربأت» أي ارتفعت.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r20.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r20.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r20.claim: A pair means every species, and bahīj is pleasing and beautiful; this is a third proof, repeated because it is evident and observable.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:5/r20.anchor: من كل صنف { بهيج } حسن رائق، وهذه دلالة ثالثة كررها الله تعالى في كتابه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p131/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p131/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p131/r14.claim: The address can include all people or be aimed specifically at deniers; “people” marks a low rank because deniers and those who act like them make up most people.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p131/r14.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد المنكر فقط , وعبر بالناس الذي هو من أسفل الأوصاف

BIQAI-FULL:v5p131/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p131/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p131/r15.claim: The conditional “if” rebukes the audience rather than expressing the author’s doubt; the past tense and “in” indicate that their misgiving is entrenched.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p131/r15.anchor: وبين أنه ما عبر به إلا للتوبيخ , لا للشك في أمرهم , بجعل الشرط ماضيا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p131/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p131/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p131/r16.claim: Resurrection means bodies rise with their souls as they were before death; God invokes creation to answer their considering this beyond His power.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p131/r16.anchor: وهو قيام الأجسام بأرواحها كما كانت قبل مماتتها سواء , استعظاما لأن نقدر عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r1.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r1.claim: Al-Baghawī says the original sense of nuṭfa is a small amount of water.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r2.speaker: البيضاوي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r2.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī derives nuṭfa from the idea of pouring.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r3.claim: An ʿalaqa is a solid, red piece of blood without the capacity to flow.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r3.anchor: أي قطعة دم حمراء جامدة , ليس فيها أهلية للسيلان

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r4.claim: A muḍgha is a very small piece of flesh into which the sperm develops.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r4.anchor: أي قطعة لحم صغيرة جدا تطورت إليها النطفة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r5.claim: Some embryos are brought to complete human form; others are not completed, miscarry, are corrupted by heat, or form only incompletely despite having a spirit.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r5.anchor: وتارة لا يخلقها بل يخرجها من الرحم فاسدة , أو تحرقها حرارته , أو غير مخلقة تخليقا تاما

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r6.claim: Biqāʿī gives Shaqq, described as half a human, and Satiḥ, described as an upper body without a lower one, as examples of incomplete formation.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r6.anchor: كشق الذي كان شق آدمي , وسطيح الذي كان علوا بلا سفل ونحوهما

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r7.claim: The developmental variations display God’s complete power and wisdom; variation disproves nature as the cause, since nature would not produce differing outcomes.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r7.anchor: كمال قدرتنا , وتمام حكمتنا , وأن ذلك ليس كائنا عن الطبيعة , لأنه لو كان عنها لم يختلف

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r8.claim: The object of “make clear” is omitted to encompass anything human understanding can grasp.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r8.anchor: وحذف المفعول إشارة إلى أنه يدخل فيه كل مل يمكن أن يحيط به العقول

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r9.claim: God leaves in the womb and completes whichever embryo He chooses.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r9.anchor: أي من ذلك الذي خلقناه { ما نشاء } إتمامه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r10.claim: The appointed term may be six months or longer, according to the strength of the womb and fetus, their nourishment, and other conditions known only to their creator.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r10.anchor: قدرناه لإتمامه ما بين ستة أشهر إلى ما نريد من الزيادة على ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r11.claim: What God does not choose to complete is expelled before completion or consumed by the womb’s heat and disappears.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r11.anchor: فإن الأرحام تمجه بقدرتنا وتلقيه دون التمام أو تحرقه فيضمحل

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r12.claim: Infants emerge small and weak in body and senses, so their size does not destroy their mothers at birth.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r12.anchor: من صغر الجثة وضعف البدن والسمع والبصر وجميع الحواس

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r13.claim: The stages run from nursing through youth, puberty, and full strength; each person reaches the limit of strength appointed for them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r13.anchor: فيما بين الرضاع , إلى حال اليفاع , إلى زمان الاحتلام , وقوة الشباب والتمام

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r14.claim: Some die before reaching old age, while others are returned to it and lose their powers.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r14.anchor: ومنكم من يتوفى } قبل ما بعد ذلك من سن الشيخوخة { ومنكم من يرد } بالشيخوخة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r15.claim: The passive form portrays the return to old age as easy for God, though it would seem unlikely without repeated observation.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r15.anchor: وبناه للمجهول إشارة إلى سهولته عليه مع استبعاده لولا تكرر المشاهدة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r16.claim: The most decrepit age is senescence, when all one’s powers decline.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r16.anchor: وهو سن الهرم فينقص جميع قواه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r17.claim: The partitive min marks the short interval between knowledge and its loss; omitting a stated endpoint allows that knowledge may return or ignorance may last until death.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r17.anchor: أثبت ( من ) الابتدائية للدلالة على قرب زمن الجهل من زمن العلم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r18.claim: Biqāʿī contrasts the omitted endpoint here with the wording previously discussed in Sūrat al-Naḥl, which does not allow the same implication of possible recovery.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r18.anchor: وأفهم غسقاط حرف الانتهاء أنه ربما عاد إليه علمه , وربما اتصل جهله بالموت بخلاف ما مضى في النحل

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r19.claim: A person’s sudden loss of learning and return to childlike weakness show a voluntary divine act; nature would cause continued growth, and the one who reverses life can restore the dead.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r19.anchor: وقد علم - بعود الإنسان في ذهاب العلم وصغر الجسم إلى نحو ما كان عليه في ابتداء الخلق - قطعا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r20.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r20.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r20.claim: After the argument from human development, Biqāʿī adds a visible proof from the earth as the passage moves from an unseen first creation to sensible evidence.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r20.anchor: وكان أول الإيجاد فيه غير مشاهد فعبر عنه بما يليق به , أتبعه دليلا آخر محسوسا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r21.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r21.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r21.claim: The singular “you see” addresses each suitable observer individually.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r21.anchor: ولعله أفرد الضمير توجيها إلى كل من يصلح أن يخاطب بذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r22.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r22.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r22.claim: The earth is dry, level, and still like a corpse, with no vegetation.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r22.anchor: أي يابسة مطمئنة ساكنة سكون الميت ليس بها شيء من نبت

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r23.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r23.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r23.claim: Rain comes by God’s mighty power from a place where it is not otherwise found.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r23.anchor: فننزل عليها ماء من مكان لا يوجد فيه ثم ينزل منه بقدرة عظيمة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r24.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r24.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r24.claim: The earth quivers as plants sprout and comes alive, ready to produce vegetation; al-Rāzī defines the motion as vigorous movement in different directions.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r24.anchor: والاهتزاز : شدة الحركوة في الجهات المختلفة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r25.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r25.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r25.claim: It swells, its first visible sign, and grows through the vegetation formed from soil and water.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r25.anchor: أي انتفخت , وذلك أول ما يظهر منها للعين وزادت ونمت بما يخرج منهاا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r26.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r26.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r26.claim: A “pair” here means a plant kind matched with another kind that completes its usefulness.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r26.anchor: أي صنف عادلناه بصنف آخر جعلناه تمام نفعه به

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r27.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r27.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r27.claim: The vegetation delights the senses through its varied colors, tastes, scents, forms, uses, and sizes.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r27.anchor: في اختلاف ألوانها وطعومها , وورائحها وأشكالها , ومنافعها ومقاديرها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r28.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r28.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r28.claim: Al-Rāzī compares plants’ movement from deficiency to perfection with humans’ progress toward their perfected state in resurrection: eternal life, sufficiency, knowledge, purity, and freedom from worldly defects for the blessed.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p133/r28.anchor: قال الرازي : فكما أن النبات يتوجه من نقص إلى كمال , فكذلك الآدمي يترقى من نقص إلى كمال

DURR-FULL:v6p10/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r1.speaker: غير مسمى
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r1.claim: An unnamed alternate wording says an angel enters the settled embryo after forty or forty-five nights, records sex, felicity, deeds, lifespan, and provision, then closes the record.
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r1.anchor: يدخل الملك على النطفة بعدما تستقر في الرحم بأربعين أو خمس وأربعين ليلة فيقول: يا رب أشقي أو سعيد

DURR-FULL:v6p10/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report al-Suyuti says Ibn Abi Hatim authenticated, calls the formed embryo one that lived and the unformed one a miscarriage.
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {مخلقة وغير مخلقة} قال: المخلقة ما كان حيا {وغير مخلقة} ما كان من سقط

DURR-FULL:v6p10/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r3.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r3.claim: Ikrima glosses the clot as blood, the morsel as flesh, and the formed as fully formed; the unformed is a miscarriage.
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: العلقة الدم والمضغة اللحم والمخلقة التي تم خلقها {وغير مخلقة} السقط

DURR-FULL:v6p10/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r4.claim: Qatada glosses formed and unformed as complete and incomplete.
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r4.anchor: عن قتادة {مخلقة وغير مخلقة} قال: تامة وغير تامة

DURR-FULL:v6p10/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r5.claim: Abu al-Aliya identifies the unformed as a miscarriage.
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r5.anchor: عن أبي العالية قال {وغير مخلقة} السقط

DURR-FULL:v6p10/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r6.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r6.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says an embryo becomes formed upon entering the fourth stage of creation; one miscarried before that is unformed.
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r6.anchor: عن الشعبي قال: إذا دخل في الخلق الرابع كانت نسمة مخلقة وإذا قدم فيها قبل ذلك

DURR-FULL:v6p10/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r7.claim: Mujahid paradoxically describes a miscarried fetus as both created and uncreated.
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد {مخلقة وغير مخلقة} قال: السقط مخلوق وغير مخلوق

DURR-FULL:v6p10/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r8.claim: Mujahid glosses keeping the embryo in the womb until an appointed term as its completion.
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد {مخلقة وغير مخلقة} قال: السقط مخلوق وغير مخلوق {ونقر في الأرحام ما نشاء إلى أجل مسمى} قال: التمام

DURR-FULL:v6p10/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd says this means keeping it in the womb until it comes out.
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r9.anchor: عن ابن زيد في قوله {ونقر في الأرحام ما نشاء إلى أجل مسمى} قال: إقامته في الرحم حتى يخرج

DURR-FULL:v6p10/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r10.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r10.claim: Al-Suddi applies the phrase to a child carried to term rather than miscarried.
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r10.anchor: عن السدي {ونقر في الأرحام ما نشاء إلى أجل مسمى} قال: هذا ما كان من ولد يولد تاما ليس بسقط

DURR-FULL:v6p10/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r11.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r11.claim: Qatada says the developmental stages make clear that people themselves were once in their mothers' wombs in this way.
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r11.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {لنبين لكم} قال: إنكم كنتم في بطون أمهاتكم كذلك

DURR-FULL:v6p10/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r12.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r12.claim: Ibn Jurayj glosses the barren earth as having no vegetation.
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r12.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله {وترى الأرض هامدة} قال: لا نبات فيها

DURR-FULL:v6p10/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r13.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r13.claim: Qatada describes the earth as gray and crumbling; rain spreads over its saline ground, making it stir, swell, and grow every beautiful kind.
DURR-FULL:v6p10/r13.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {وترى الأرض هامدة} أي غبراء متهشمة {فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء اهتزت وربت} يقول: نفرق الغيث في سبختها

DURR-FULL:v6p11/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p11/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p11/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses a beautiful pair as something beautiful.
DURR-FULL:v6p11/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {زوج بهيج} قال: حسن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r1.claim: The first creation is a greater precedent than resurrection: the One who created humans from nothing can recreate them after they perish.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r1.anchor: وهو الخلق الأول . قال تعالى : { أفعيينا بالخلق الأول بل هم في لبس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r2.claim: The address principally targets polytheists, since they denied resurrection; their inclusion here is clearer than in the preceding address.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r2.anchor: ودخول المشركين بادىء ذي بدء في هذا الخطاب أظهر من دخولهم في الخطاب السابق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r3.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r3.claim: A reported view takes the address here as specifically directed to the polytheists.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r3.anchor: قيل إن الخطاب هنا خاص بهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r4.claim: The conditional presents their actual doubt as though it were uncertain, given the surrounding proofs that should dispel it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r4.anchor: وجعل ريبهم في البعث مفروضا ب ( إن ) الشرطية مع أن ريبهم محقق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r5.claim: The construction resembles the conditional in 43:5, where a condition is posed despite its factual premise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r5.anchor: أفنضرب عنكم الذكر صفحا أن كنتم قوما مسرفين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r6.claim: The preposition in ‘in doubt’ is figurative: doubt is portrayed as enclosing those who experience it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r6.anchor: شبهت ملابسة الريب إياهم بإحاطة الظرف بالمظروف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r7.claim: The creation clause occupies the answer’s position but is evidence for the answer, not its literal wording; the implied response is to know or consider resurrection possible.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r7.anchor: واقعة موقع جواب الشرط ولكنها لا يصلح لفظها لأن يكون جوابا لهذا الشرط بل هي دليل الجواب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r8.claim: The first human origin from dust is Adam and Eve; reproductive capacity was then established in Adam and his spouse, so later generation is from semen.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r9.claim: Nuṭfa means a man’s semen and is a noun on the pattern fuʿla with the passive sense ‘that which is poured’; the root denotes drops or pouring.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r9.anchor: اسم لمني الرجل ، وهو بوزن فعلة بمعنى مفعول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r10.claim: ʿAlaqa is a soft, clotted piece of blood.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r11.claim: Muḍgha is a piece of flesh about the size of a morsel to chew; its form conveys something chewed or of chewed size.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r11.anchor: القطعة من اللحم بقدر ما يمضغ مثله ،

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p196/r12.claim: Here thumma coordinates individual developmental stages and marks genuine temporal succession.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r1.claim: Every fetus has a divinely determined term in the womb, usually nine months and nine days, though an intervening cause may bring delivery sooner; all is known to God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r1.anchor: الأكثر استكمال تسعة أشهر وتسعة أيام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r2.claim: He connects the phrase ‘appointed term’ with the same wording in the debt verse, 2:282.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r3.claim: Thumma marks rank or importance here, because the fetus’s emergence is the point at issue.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r3.anchor: للدلالة على التراخي الرتبي فإن إخراج الجنين هو المقصود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r4.claim: Ṭiflan is a circumstantial accusative describing the addressees as infants; its singular form denotes the generic class and functions like a plural.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r4.anchor: أي حال كونكم أطفالا . وإنما أفرد { طفلا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r5.claim: The phrase ‘then that you reach maturity’ is linked to bringing infants out as its cause, with the lām expressing purpose.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r6.claim: Full strength is the complete wisdom behind human development: it is the body’s and mind’s strongest, clearest display of human capacities.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r6.anchor: وإنما جعل بلوغ الأشد علة لأنه أقوى أطوار الإنسان وأجلى مظاهر مواهبه في الجسم والعقل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r7.claim: The second thumma reinforces the earlier thumma in the sequence about being brought out as infants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r7.anchor: تأكيد لمثله في قوله { ثم نخرجكم طفلا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r8.claim: He presents his account of how this clause connects to its context and says the commentators’ alternative explanations, cited by al-Alusi, do not withstand scrutiny.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r8.anchor: هذا ما ظهر لي في اتصال هذه الجملة بما قبلها وللمفسرين توجيهات غير سالمة من التعقب ذكرها الألوسي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r9.claim: Ashudd means the age of youth, when one’s powers are fully gathered.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r10.claim: He points to Joseph receiving judgment and knowledge upon reaching full strength in 12:22.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r10.anchor: ولما بلغ أشده آتيناه حكما وعلما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r11.claim: Unlike 40:67, this proof omits old age because it emphasizes growth toward strength, not decline; 40:67 mentions old age as a life stage people desire, while this address warns that some will reach senility.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p200/r11.anchor: ولم يذكر في آية سورة الحج لأنها وردت مورد الاستدلال على الإحياء بعد العدم فلم يذكر فيها من الأطوار إلا ما فيه ازدياد القوة ونماء الحياة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r1.claim: The earth’s revival argument is coordinated with the earlier creation argument and addressed generally to anyone hearing the discourse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r1.anchor: عطف على جملة { فإنا خلقناكم من تراب }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r2.claim: This advances the proof by analogy from a visible event; the initial creation argument began with an unseen origin, whereas the earth’s revival can be observed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r2.anchor: وهذا ارتقاء في الاستدلال على الإحياء بعد الموت بقياس التمثيل لأنه استدلال بحالة مشاهدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r3.claim: The proof lies especially in water making the earth rise and grow: its barrenness images death, and its renewed growth images resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r3.anchor: فهمود الأرض بمنزلة موت الإنسان واهتزازها وإنباتها بعد ذلك يماثل الإحياء بعد الموت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r4.claim: Hamida describes dry earth with its vegetation gone; for fire, the related word means extinguished.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r4.anchor: فهمود الأرض جفافها وزوال نبتها ، وهمود النار خمودها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r5.claim: Ihtazz means movement upward; the earth is pictured as rising under rain and as its surface rises with grass, like something shaking upward.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r5.anchor: التحرك إلى أعلى ، فاهتزاز الأرض تمثيل لحال ارتفاع ترابها بالماء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r6.claim: Rabat means increased or swollen; here the land swells as plants and trees emerge through it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r6.anchor: وهو ازدياد الشيء يقال : ربا يربو ربوا ، وفسر هنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r7.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads rabāʾat with hamza after the bāʾ, meaning that the earth rose.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر { وربأت بهمزة مفتوحة بعد الموحدة ، أي ارتفعت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r8.claim: The hamzated reading is supported by ‘to rise above’ in rabāʾa binafsihi and by the lookout called rabīʾa, who stands on a hill to watch for enemies.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r8.anchor: ربأ بنفسه عن كذا ، أي ارتفع مجازا ، وهو فعل مشتق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r9.claim: Zawj first denotes a paired male or female kind, then came to denote either kind individually and, more broadly, any type or species, as here for plants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r9.anchor: أطلق عليه اسم الزوج تشبيها له بالزوج من الحيوان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r10.claim: Bahīj means pleasing to look at; the description embeds a grace for humanity, since beauty contributes no proof of resurrection.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r11.claim: The gratuitous mention of pleasing appearance parallels blessings in 16:6 and the adornment of the lowest heaven in 67:5.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p202#2/r11.anchor: ولكم فيها جمال حين تريحون وحين تسرحون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p204/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p204/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p204/r1.claim: The statement is a concluding summary and tailpiece referring to human creation, development and death, and the earth’s revival and vegetation.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p206/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p206/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p206/r1.claim: The new disputants passage continues the address about doubt: after the proofs, people divide into those convinced and those who still dispute without knowledge.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#2/r12.claim: The verse argues from the first creation and gives two examples; reflection makes resurrection rationally possible, then revelation confirms its occurrence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#2/r12.anchor: يا أيها الناس إن كنتم في ريب من البعث الآية هذا احتجاج على العالم بالبداءة الأولى وضرب الله تعالى في هذه الآية مثلين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r1.claim: The conditional ‘if you are in doubt’ embeds an implication of divine enabling or guidance.
