IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r2.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads al-baʿth with an open ʿayn; Basrans call it a dialect, while Kufans regard it as a lightened form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r2.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بن أبي الحسن «البعث» بفتح العين وهي لغة في البعث عند البصريين وهي عند الكوفيين تخفيف بعث

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r3.claim: Creation from dust first refers to Adam; the verb is then applied to his descendants because they come from him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r3.anchor: فإنا خلقناكم من تراب يريد آدم ثم سلط الفعل عليهم من حيث هم من ذريته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r4.claim: The nutfa is human semen, and the word may denote a small or large quantity of water.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r4.anchor: ثم من نطفة يريد المني الذي يكون من البشر، و «النطفة» تقع على قليل الماء وكثيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r5.speaker: النقاش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r5.claim: Al-Naqqāsh says the intended nutfa is Adam’s seminal fluid.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r6.claim: The ʿalaqa is blood into which the nutfa changes in the womb, or blood accompanying it; it is also called fresh or intensely red blood.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r6.anchor: ثم من علقة، يريد من الدم تعود النطفة إليه في الرحم أو المقارن للنطفة، والعلق، الدم العبيط وقيل العلق، الشديد الحمرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r7.claim: A muḍgha is a piece of flesh about the size of a bite that can be chewed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p107#3/r7.anchor: ثم من مضغة يريد بضعة لحم على قدر ما يمضغ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r1.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والشعبي وأبو العالية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r1.claim: Mujāhid, Qatāda, al-Shaʿbī, and Abū al-ʿĀliya explain fully formed as complete in structure, and not fully formed as incomplete, meaning miscarried.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r1.anchor: تعالى: مخلقة معناه متممة البنية، وغير مخلقة غير متممة أي التي تستسقط قاله مجاهد وقتادة والشعبي وأبو العالية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r2.claim: The intensive form reflects the many distinct organs in a person, each with its own well-formed creation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r2.anchor: ولما كان الإنسان فيه أعضاء متباينة وكل واحد منها مختص بخلق حسن في جملته تضعيف الفعل لأن فيه خلقا كثيرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r3.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r3.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads both mukhaḷḷaqa and ghayr in the accusative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة «مخلقة» بالنصب «وغير» بالنصب في الراء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r4.speaker: مالك والأوزاعي وغيرهما
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r4.claim: Mālik, al-Awzāʿī, and others count a slave woman who miscarries as an umm walad once the expelled lump is known to be her child.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r4.anchor: فقال مالك والأوزاعي وغيرهما: هي أم ولد بالمضغة إذا علم أنها مضغة الولد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r5.speaker: الشافعي وأبو حنيفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r5.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī and Abū Ḥanīfa require a discernible form, even one body part, before the miscarried child makes her an umm walad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r5.anchor: وقال الشافعي وأبو حنيفة: لا حتى يتبين فيه خلق ولو عضو واحد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r6.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r6.claim: One group takes li-nubayyina as clarifying resurrection, an explanatory parenthesis in the sentence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r6.anchor: وقوله تعالى: لنبين قالت فرقة معناه لنبين أمر البعث فهو اعتراض بين الكلامين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r7.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r7.claim: The group that understands clarification as concerning resurrection reads nuqirru in the indicative; this is also the majority reading.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r8.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r8.claim: Another group says incomplete embryos and miscarriages make the stages in the womb clear to people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r8.anchor: وقالت فرقة لنبين معناه بكون المضغة غير مخلقة وطرح النساء إياها كذلك نبين للناس أن المناقل في الرحم هي هكذا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r9.speaker: المفضل عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r9.claim: This second group reads nuqirra and nukhrijakum in the subjunctive, as reported by al-Mufaḍḍal from ʿĀṣim.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r9.anchor: وقرأت هذه الفرقة «ونقر» بالنصب وكذلك قرأت «ونخرجكم» بالنصب وهي رواية المفضل عن عاصم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r10.claim: Abū ʿAmr al-Dānī says al-Mufaḍḍal’s transmission has yaqir and yukhrijukum with yāʾ; the indicative works on this interpretation, but not the subjunctive on the other.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r10.anchor: وحكى أبو عمرو الداني أن رواية المفضل هذه هي بالياء في «يقر» وفي «يخرجكم» والرفع على هذا التأويل سائغ ولا يجوز النصب على التأويل الأول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r11.speaker: ابن وثاب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r11.claim: Ibn Waththāb reads mā nashāʾ with a kasra on the nūn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r11.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب «ما نشاء» بكسر النون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r12.claim: The appointed term varies for each fetus: some miscarry, while others complete development and are born alive.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r12.anchor: و «الأجل المسمى» هو مختلف بحسب جنين جنين فثم من يسقط وثم من يكمل أمره ويخرج حيا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r13.claim: Ṭiflan is grammatically a singular collective, meaning children.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r13.anchor: وقوله تعالى: طفلا اسم الجنس أي أطفالا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r14.claim: Authorities give the age of full strength as eighteen, thirty, thirty-two, thirty-six, forty, or forty-five; the word is shared, and this verse may mean general maturity or an orphan’s puberty.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r14.anchor: واختلف الناس في «الأشد» من ثمانية عشر إلى ثلاثين، إلى اثنين وثلاثين، إلى ستة وثلاثين، إلى أربعين، إلى خمسة وأربعين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r15.claim: The worst age brings physical debility preventing acts of worship and mental decline preventing required beliefs; it usually comes with age but may arrive younger through individual infirmity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r15.anchor: والرد إلى أرذل العمر هو حصول الإنسان في زمانة واختلال قوة حتى لا يقدر على إقامة الطاعات واختلال عقل حتى لا يقدر على إقامة ما يلزمه من المعتقدات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r16.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r16.claim: A report gives 75 as the worst age; Ibn Atiyya questions it, or takes it as an average if authentic, since many people remain sound at eighty.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r16.anchor: وقد ذكر عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه أرذل العمر خمسة وسبعون سنة وهذا فيه نظر وإن صح عن علي رضي الله عنه فلا يتوجه إلا أن يريد على الأكثر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r17.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r17.claim: The majority lengthen the vowel in al-ʿumur.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r18.speaker: نافع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r18.claim: Nāfiʿ reads al-ʿumur with a shortened vowel; the transmission is disputed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r18.anchor: وقرأ نافع «العمر» مخففة الميم واختلف عنه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r19.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r19.claim: The person forgets knowledge and recognition he once had; this shows that the One who manages these transformations can restore the bodies He first created.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108/r19.anchor: قوله تعالى: لكيلا يعلم أي لينسى معارفه وعلمه الذي كان معه فلا يعلم من ذلك شيئا فهذا مثال واحد يقضي للمعتبر به أن القادر على هذه المناقل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r1.claim: The earth’s revival after death is the second example making bodily resurrection possible to the observer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r1.anchor: هذا هو المثال الذي يعطي للمعتبر فيه جواز بعث الأجساد وذلك أن إحياء الأرض بعد موتها بين فكذلك الأجساد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r2.claim: Hāmida means still, worn out, or decayed; a garment that has worn out is also called hamida.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r2.anchor: وهامدة معناه ساكنة دارسة بالية ومنه قيل همد الثوب إذا بلي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r3.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s line describes a body as pale and clothes as worn out, using hamd to support the sense of hāmida.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r3.anchor: قالت قتيلة ما لجسمك شاحبا ... وأرى ثيابك باليات همدا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r4.claim: The earth’s shaking is its movement as vegetation grows and as other effects of water take place.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r4.anchor: واهتزاز الأرض هو حركتها بالنبات وغير ذلك مما يعتريها بالماء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r5.claim: Rabat means the land rose and swelled, as in rabwa for an elevated place.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r5.anchor: وربت معناه نشزت وارتفعت ومنه الربوة وهو المكان المرتفع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r6.speaker: جعفر بن القعقاع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r6.claim: Jaʿfar ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ reads rabaʾat with hamza, also reported from Abū ʿAmr and read by others; Ibn Atiyya deems it weak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ جعفر بن القعقاع «وربأت» بالهمز، ورويت عن أبي عمرو وقرأها عبد الله بن جعفر وخالد بن إلياس وهي غير وجيهة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r7.claim: The hamza reading may derive from rabʾ, to climb to high ground as a scout; it portrays the land rising with water.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r7.anchor: ووجهها أن تكون من ربأت القوم إذا علوت شرفا من الأرض طليعة فكأن الأرض بالماء تتطاول وتعلو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r8.speaker: قتادة وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r8.claim: Zawj means a kind, and bahīj means beautiful, from bahja, as Qatāda and others explain.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p108#2/r8.anchor: و «الزوج» النوع، و «البهيج» فعيل من البهجة وهي الحسن قاله قتادة وغيره

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r1.claim: The address is directed to the people of Mecca.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r1.anchor: يعني أهل مكة إن كنتم في ريب من البعث

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r2.claim: The soil refers to Adam and the sperm to his descendants; reflecting on their beginning shows that beginning and resurrection are equally within divine power.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r2.anchor: يعني خلق آدم ثم من نطفة يعني خلق ولده والمعنى إن شككتم في بعثكم فتدبروا أمر خلقكم وابتدائكم فانكم لا تجدون في القدرة فرقا بين الابتداء والاعادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r3.anchor: فأما النطفة فهي المني والعلقة دم عبيط جامد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r4.claim: One explanation defines ʿalaqa as thick, fresh, congealed blood.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r4.anchor: والعلقة دم عبيط جامد وقيل سميت علقة لرطوبتها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r5.claim: Another explanation derives ʿalaqa from its moistness and sticking to whatever it passes; when dry, it is no longer a clot.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r5.anchor: وقيل سميت علقة لرطوبتها وتعلقها بما تمر به فاذا جفت فليست علقة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r6.claim: Muḍgha means a small piece of flesh.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r6.anchor: والمضغة لحمة صغير قال ابن قتيبة وسميت بذلك لأنه بقدر ما يمضغ

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r7.claim: Ibn Qutayba says it is named for being roughly the size of a morsel one chews, like ghurfa is named for an amount scooped.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r7.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة وسميت بذلك لأنه بقدر ما يمضغ كما قيل غرفة لقدر ما يغرف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r8.claim: Ibn Masʿud identifies the formed as fully shaped and the unformed as what the womb expels as semen or blood before it becomes a formed creature.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r8.anchor: ما خلق سويا وغير المخلقة ما ألقته الأرحام من النطف وهو دم قبل أن يكون خلقا قاله ابن مسعود

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes the formed as completed with the spirit and born alive, and the unformed as a miscarriage that did not receive the spirit.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r9.anchor: ما أكمل خلقه بنفخ الروح فيه وهو الذي يولد حيا لتمام وغير المخلقة ما سقط غير حي لم يكمل خلقه بنفح الروح فيه هذا معنى قول ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r10.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the formed is pictured and the unformed is not pictured.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r10.anchor: أن المخلقة المصورة وغير المخلقة غير مصورة قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r11.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r11.claim: Al-Suddī describes miscarriages at successive stages: as semen, as a clot, partly shaped, or fully shaped.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r11.anchor: أن المخلقة وغير المخلقة السقط تارة يسقط نطفة وعلقة وتارة قد صور بعضه وتارة قد صور كله قاله السدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r12.speaker: الفراء وابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r12.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and Ibn Qutayba identify the formed as complete and the unformed as a miscarriage.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r12.anchor: أن المخلقة التامة وغير المخلقة السقط قاله الفراء وابن قتيبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r13.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r13.claim: One gloss is that people are created so God can show them what they should do and leave undone.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r13.anchor: خلقناكم لنبين لكم ما تأتون وما تذرون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r14.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r14.claim: A second gloss is that the Qurʾan explains the beginning of human creation and its successive states.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r14.anchor: لنبين لكم في القرآن بدو خلقكم وتنقل احوالكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r15.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r15.claim: A third gloss is that these transformations display the perfection of God's wisdom and power.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r15.anchor: لنبين لكم كمال حكمتنا وقدرتنا في تقليب أحوال خلقكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r16.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r16.claim: A fourth gloss is that God makes clear that resurrection is true.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r17.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r17.speaker: أبو عمران الجوني وابن أبي عبلة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r17.claim: Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī and Ibn Abī ʿAblah read ليبين لكم with a third-person yāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r17.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمران الجوني وابن أبي عبلة ليبين لكم بالياء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r18.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r18.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبو رجاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r18.claim: Ibn Masʿud and Abū Rajāʾ read ويقر with a raised initial letter, fatḥa on qāf, and nominative rāʾ, as described in the source.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r18.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وابو رجاء ويقر بباء مرفوعة وفتح القاف ورفع الراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r19.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r19.speaker: أبو الجوزاء وأبو إسحاق السبيعي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r19.claim: Abū al-Jawzāʾ and Abū Isḥāq al-Sabīʿī read ويقر with yāʾ, kasra on qāf, and accusative rāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r19.anchor: وقرأ أبو الجوزاء وابو اسحاق السبيعي ويقر بياء مرفوعه وبكسر القاف ونصب الراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r20.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r20.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r20.claim: What remains in the womb until the appointed term is what is not miscarried; the term is childbirth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r20.anchor: والذي يقر في الأرحام هو الذي لا يكون سقطا إلى اجل مسمى وهو أجل الولادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r21.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r21.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r21.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says ṭiflan occupies the place of aṭfālan; Arabic may use a singular form with plural meaning, as in Qurʾan 66:4 and the cited poetry.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p406/r21.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة هو في موضع اطفال والعرب قد تضع لفظ الواحد في معنى الجميع قال الله تعالى والملائكة بعد ذلك ظهير التحريم 4

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p408/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p408/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p408/r1.claim: A second poetic line is cited in connection with the argument about singular ṭiflan; its poet is not named.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p408/r1.anchor: وأنشد أيضا في حلقكم عظم وقد شجينا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p408/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p408/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p408/r2.claim: Another explanation says ṭiflan is singular because the plural suffix in nukh'rijukum already signals a group, so aṭfālan was unnecessary.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p408/r2.anchor: قال غيره إنما قال طفلا فوحد لأن الميم في قوله تعالى نخرجكم قد دلت على الجميع فلم يحتج إلى ان يقول اطفالا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395/r1.claim: To answer deniers of resurrection, Ibn Kathīr points to God's power in the observable beginning of human creation: Adam was made from soil and his descendants from a lowly fluid.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395/r1.anchor: لما ذكر تعالى المخالف للبعث، المنكر للمعاد، ذكر تعالى الدليل على قدرته تعالى على المعاد، بما يشاهد من بدئه للخلق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395/r2.claim: He describes development: after forty days sperm becomes a red clot for forty days, then an unformed flesh lump; it is shaped into the head, limbs, torso, and other organs, and miscarriages may occur before or after shaping.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395/r2.anchor: إذا استقرت النطفة في رحم المرأة، مكثت أربعين يوما كذلك، يضاف إليه ما يجتمع إليها، ثم تنقلب علقة حمراء بإذن الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395/r3.claim: Some pregnancies are not miscarried but remain in the womb until their appointed term, after which the child is brought forth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395/r3.anchor: وتارة تستقر في الرحم لا تلقيها المرأة ولا تسقطها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395/r4.claim: Mujāhid interprets the formed and unformed as a miscarried fetus, either formed or not formed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395/r4.anchor: كما قال مجاهد في قوله تعالى: {مخلقة وغير مخلقة} قال: هو السقط مخلوق وغير مخلوق.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395/r5.claim: In the Ṣaḥīḥayn, Ibn Masʿūd reports the Prophet saying that each person's creation passes through forty days as a drop, a clot, and a lump; an angel then writes the person's deeds, lifespan, provision, and fate before breathing in the spirit.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: حدثنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم -وهو الصادق المصدوق-:"إن خلق أحدكم يجمع في بطن أمه أربعين ليلة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395#2/r1.speaker: عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395#2/r1.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reports an angel taking settled sperm and asking whether it is formed; if unformed it is miscarried as blood, while for the formed embryo its sex, fortune, lifespan, deeds, provision, and death-place are decreed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395#2/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: النطفة إذا استقرت في الرحم، أخذها (6) ملك بكفه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395#2/r2.speaker: عامر الشعبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395#2/r2.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says that once the lump reaches its fourth formation it becomes a human being; if unformed, the womb expels it as blood.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395#2/r2.anchor: ثم تلا عامر الشعبي: {يا أيها الناس إن كنتم في ريب من البعث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395#2/r3.claim: A report from Ḥudhayfa ibn Asīd, transmitted in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, says an angel enters the settled sperm after forty or forty-five days, records its sex, deeds, provision, lifespan, and destiny, and then closes the scroll so nothing changes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p395#2/r3.anchor: عن حذيفة بن أسيد -يبلغ به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم-قال: "يدخل الملك على النطفة بعد ما تستقر في الرحم بأربعين أو خمس وأربعين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p396/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p396/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p396/r1.claim: The newborn is weak in body, senses, strength, and reason; God gradually strengthens the child while parents care tenderly for them, until full strength and youthful beauty.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p396/r1.anchor: أي: ضعيفا في بدنه، وسمعه وبصره وحواسه، وبطشه وعقله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p396/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p396/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p396/r2.claim: Some die in youth and full strength; others decline into senility, losing physical power, understanding, and memory, as also described in 30:54.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p396/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p396/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p396/r3.claim: Anas transmits a prophetic report: before puberty good deeds are credited to parents and sins are not charged; afterward deeds are recorded, with age-based blessings from forty through ninety, and at frailty past good works are still credited while sins are omitted.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p396/r3.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك -رفع الحديث-قال: "المولود حتى يبلغ الحنث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p397/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p397/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p397/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr calls the preceding age-blessings narration extremely unusual and severely objectionable, despite recording related versions.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p397/r1.anchor: هذا حديث غريب جدا، وفيه نكارة شديدة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p397/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p397/r2.speaker: أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p397/r2.claim: A version suspended at Anas says a Muslim at forty is spared three afflictions; later ages bring easier reckoning, repentance, heavenly love, accepted good deeds, forgiveness, and intercession, with the person called God's prisoner on earth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p397/r2.anchor: عن أنس قال: إذا بلغ الرجل المسلم أربعين سنة، أمنه الله من أنواع البلايا، من الجنون والجذام والبرص

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p397/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p397/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p397/r3.claim: A separate version raised to the Prophet through Ibn ʿUmar gives the same age-related blessings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p397/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر بن الخطاب، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، مثله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p397/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p397/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p397/r4.claim: Another report from Anas says that anyone who lives forty years in Islam is spared three kinds of affliction and then receives the age-based blessings described above.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p397/r4.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "ما من معمر يعمر في الإسلام أربعين سنة، إلا صرف الله عنه ثلاثة أنواع من البلاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p397/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p397/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p397/r5.claim: Al-Bazzār's version from Anas gives similar blessings by age: protection at forty, an easier account at fifty, repentance at sixty, forgiveness and heavenly love at seventy, acceptance at eighty, and forgiveness and intercession at ninety.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p397/r5.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ما من عبد يعمر في الإسلام أربعين سنة، إلا صرف الله عنه أنواعا من البلاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p398/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p398/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p398/r1.claim: The dormant earth is barren and without vegetation, providing another proof that God can revive the dead as He revives the earth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p398/r1.anchor: هذا دليل آخر على قدرته تعالى على إحياء الموتى، كما يحيي الأرض الميتة الهامدة، وهي القحلة التي لا نبت فيها ولا شيء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p398/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p398/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p398/r2.claim: Qatāda describes the dormant earth as dusty and broken up.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p398/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: غبراء متهشمة. وقال السدي: ميتة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p398/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p398/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p398/r3.claim: Al-Suddī glosses the dormant earth as dead.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p398/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: غبراء متهشمة. وقال السدي: ميتة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p398/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p398/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p398/r4.claim: Rain makes the land move and revive; it rises as soil settles within it, then produces fruits and plants of varied colors, tastes, scents, shapes, and uses.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p398/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p398/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p398/r5.claim: A beautiful pair means plants that are pleasing to look at and pleasant in scent.

JISHUMI:v7p4906/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4906/r3.speaker: عاصم
JISHUMI:v7p4906/r3.claim: A report from Asim reads nuqir with fatḥa on the rāʾ, coordinated with li-nubayyina; the other readers use the nominative, understood as wa-naḥnu nuqir.
JISHUMI:v7p4906/r3.anchor: وروي عن عاصم: ونقر بفتح الراء نسقا على قوله: (لنبين لكم) والباقون بالرفع على تقدير: ونحن نقر.

JISHUMI:v7p4906/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4906/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر
JISHUMI:v7p4906/r4.claim: Abu Ja'far reads rabāʾat with hamza, meaning rose or became elevated; the others read rabat, meaning increased.
JISHUMI:v7p4906/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر: وربأت بالهمز، وفي (حم) مثله أي: ارتفعت وعلت من قولهم: ربأ الرجل إذا صعد مكانا مشرفا

JISHUMI:v7p4906/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4906/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4906/r5.claim: The manifest reading has tāʾ with fatḥa; another reading reported from some uses ḍamma.
JISHUMI:v7p4906/r5.anchor: والقراءة الظاهرة: ترى بفتح التاء، وعن بعضهم بضمها

JISHUMI:v7p4913/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4913/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4913/r1.claim: The earth is barren, dry, and worn of vegetation; when rain falls it stirs with plants, swells from the rainfall, and grows every beautiful species in form, appearance, and color.
JISHUMI:v7p4913/r1.anchor: ثم ذكر دليلا آخر فقال سبحانه: وترى الأرض هامدة يابسة دارسة من أثر النبات فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء وهو المطر اهتزت تحركت بالنبات وربت زادت بمجيء الغيث

JISHUMI:v7p4913/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4913/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4913/r9.claim: The human and plant signs invite reflection and show that God can bring the dead back to life.
JISHUMI:v7p4913/r9.anchor: وتدل على أن الإعادة؛ بما بين من الدلائل من حال الإنسان، وأحوال النبات، ومن تفكر فيها علم أنه قادر على الإعادة

JISHUMI:v7p4913/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4913/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4913/r10.claim: The resurrection includes restoring bones and flesh, refuting the claim that the addressed person is only a constituent located in the heart.
JISHUMI:v7p4913/r10.anchor: وتدل على أنه يعيد العظام واللحوم، فيبطل قول من يقول: إن المخاطب جزء في القلب

JISHUMI:v7p4913/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4913/r11.speaker: إسماعيل بن إسحاق
JISHUMI:v7p4913/r11.claim: Isma'il ibn Ishaq infers that miscarriage ends the waiting period even before the fetus is visibly formed, since it is counted among human creation like the formed fetus.
JISHUMI:v7p4913/r11.anchor: واستدل إسماعيل بن إسحاق بقوله تعالى: (وغير مخلقة) على أن السقط تنقضي به العدة وإن لم يتبين خلقه

JISHUMI:v7p4913/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4913/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4913/r12.claim: The author calls that inference far-fetched: the verse argues against polytheists, not about waiting periods; alternatively, unformed can mean imperfectly formed, in which case the waiting period ends by agreement.
JISHUMI:v7p4913/r12.anchor: وهذا يبعد؛ لأن الغرض بالآية الاحتجاج على المشركين بعد بيان حكم العدة، على أنا إذا حملناه

JISHUMI:v7p4913/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4913/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4913/r13.claim: Ghayr mukhallaqa may mean incomplete, such as blind, deaf, or otherwise deficient in form.
JISHUMI:v7p4913/r13.anchor: أنه غير تمام، بأن يكون أعمى، أو أصم، أو ناقص الخلق

JISHUMI:v1p849#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p849#2/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p849#2/r8.claim: The sūra first establishes the Book and faith in resurrection and divine unity, then prophethood, recounts Israel’s story and its scriptural foretelling of Islam and the Prophet, and proceeds to Islamic laws beginning with the qibla change.
JISHUMI:v1p849#2/r8.anchor: ذكر تعالى في أول السورة الكتاب وما يلزم الإيمان به من البعث والتوحيد، وغيره في قوله: (ياأيها الناس اعبدوا ربكم)

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r1.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads al-baʿth with a vowel; the commentary compares this pattern to al-jalb and al-ṭard.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r1.anchor: قرأ الحسن { من البعث } بالتحريك ونظيره : الجلب والطرد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r2.claim: For anyone doubting resurrection, reflection on the stages of initial creation removes the doubt.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r2.anchor: كأنه قيل : إن ارتبتم في البعث فمزيل ريبكم أن تنظروا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r3.claim: An ʿalaqa is a piece of clotted blood.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r3.anchor: العلقة : قطعة الدم الجامدة . والمضغة : اللحمة الصغيرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r4.claim: A muḍgha is a small piece of flesh, about the size of what is chewed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r4.anchor: والمضغة : اللحمة الصغيرة قدر ما يمضغ . والمخلقة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r5.claim: Mukhallaqa means smoothed and complete, without defect; embryos vary in completeness, corresponding to human variation in form, size, and stature.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r5.anchor: والمخلقة : المسواة الملساء من النقصان والعيب . يقال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r6.claim: The gradual transformations display God's power and wisdom and argue that the one who originated humans from unlike substances can restore them, a fortiori and more easily by analogy.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r6.anchor: وإنما نقلناكم من حال إلى حال ومن خلقة إلى خلقة { لنبين لكم } بهذا التدريج

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r7.claim: Leaving the verb “make clear” without an expressed object signals that these acts reveal aspects of God's power and knowledge beyond human comprehension or description.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r7.anchor: وورود الفعل غير معدي إلى المبين : إعلام بأن أفعاله هذه يتبين بها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r8.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r8.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAblah reads liyubayyina lakum with a yāʾ.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة : ليبين لكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r9.claim: The verbs are reported in variants with yāʾ or nūn and with indicative or subjunctive endings; nūn forms also occur in the following verb nukh’rijukum.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r9.anchor: ويقر ، بالياء وقرىء ( ونقر ) ونخرجكم ، بالنون والنصب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r10.speaker: يعقوب
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r10.claim: Yaʿqūb reads nuqirru with nūn and ḍamma on the qāf, deriving it from qarra al-māʾ, “he poured the water.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r10.anchor: وعن يعقوب : يقر بالنون وضم القاف ، من قر الماء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r11.claim: The indicative reading states that God keeps in the womb whatever He wills until delivery—six months, nine months, two years, four years, or whatever He decrees—and expels or miscarries what He does not will to remain.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r11.anchor: فالقراءة بالرفع إخبار بأنه يقر { فى الارحام ما * يشاء } أن يقره من ذلك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r12.claim: The subjunctive reading makes “keep” a second purpose coordinated with “make clear”: God retains whom He wills until birth, growth, and accountability.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r12.anchor: والقراءة بالنصب : تعليل معطوف على تعليل . ومعناه : خلقناكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r13.claim: The following singular “then that you reach maturity” supports the subjunctive construction, with the singular used to indicate the generic human kind.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r13.anchor: ويعضد هذه القراءة قوله : { ثم لتبلغوا أشدكم } وحده

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r14.claim: The phrase can mean that God brings each individual out as a child.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r14.anchor: ويحتمل : نخرج كل واحد منكم طفلا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r15.claim: Al-ashudd is full strength, intellect, and discernment; it is a plural-form word with no singular used, suggesting strength in multiple respects.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r15.anchor: الأشد : كمال القوة والعقل والتمييز ، وهو من ألفاظ الجموع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r16.claim: Some die, while others reach senility and dementia, returning to the weakness and limited understanding of childhood; God's power both raises and lowers human capacities.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r16.anchor: وقرىء ( ومنكم من يتوفى ) أي يتوفاه الله { أرذل العمر } الهرم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r17.claim: The aged person quickly forgets learned information, even asking who someone is again moments after being told.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r17.anchor: من بعد علم شيئا } أي : ليصير نساء بحيث إذ كسب علما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r18.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r18.speaker: أبو عمرو
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r18.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads al-ʿumur with a quiescent mīm.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r18.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو : العمر ، بسكون الميم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r19.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r19.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r19.claim: Hāmidah describes earth that is dead and dry.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r19.anchor: الهامدة : الميتة اليابسة . وهذه دلالة ثانية على البعث

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r20.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r20.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r20.claim: Reviving barren earth is a second proof of resurrection; God repeats it throughout the Qurʾān because it is evident and directly observable.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r20.anchor: ولظهورها وكونها مشاهدة معاينة ، كررها الله في كتابه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r21.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r21.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r21.claim: The earth stirs with vegetation and swells; the variant rabaʾat means that it rose.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r21.anchor: اهتزت وربت } تحركت بالنبات وانتفخت ، وقرىء ( ربأت )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r22.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r22.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p145/r22.claim: Bahīj means beautiful and pleasing to the viewer.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r1.claim: The creation from dust refers to Adam.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r2.claim: The descendants of Adam are meant by the drop of semen.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r3.claim: The drop becomes a clinging clot in the womb.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r3.anchor: يعني أن النطفة تصير في الرحم علقة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r4.claim: A مضغة is the mass of flesh about the size of what can be chewed; the clot becomes that mass.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r4.anchor: يعني أن العلقة تصير مضغة , وذلك مقدار ما يمضع من اللحم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿud says the formed is what becomes a creature, while the unformed is what the womb expels before the seed becomes formed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r5.anchor: ما صار خلقا , وغير مخلقة ما دفعته الأرحام من النطف فلم يصير خلقا , وهو قول ابن مسعود

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r6.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r6.claim: Qatada interprets the pair as complete and incomplete in formation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r6.anchor: معناه تامة الخلق وغير تامة الخلق , وهذا قول قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r7.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r7.claim: Mujahid interprets them as shaped and unshaped, such as a miscarried fetus.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r7.anchor: معناه مصورة وغير مصورة كالسقط , وهذا قول مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r8.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets them as reaching full term or not reaching full term.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p6#3/r8.anchor: يعني التام في شهوره , وغير التام , قاله الضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r1.claim: The Quran explains the beginning of human creation and the successive stages through which people pass.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r1.anchor: يعني في القرآن بدء خلقكم وتنقل أحوالكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r2.claim: Mujahid says the appointed term is completion.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r3.claim: Some die before reaching decrepit old age.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r3.anchor: يعني قبل أن تبلغ إلى أرذل العمر

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r4.claim: Alternatively, some die before reaching full adulthood.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r5.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r5.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam interprets the most decrepit age as old age.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r5.anchor: الهرم , وهو قول يحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r6.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r6.claim: Al-Naqqash says it is a return to a state like that at birth from the mother's womb.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r6.anchor: إلى مثل حاله عند خروجه من بطن أمه , حكاه النقاش

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r7.speaker: اليزيدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r7.claim: Al-Yazidi interprets it as loss of intellect.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r8.claim: One explanation is that an elderly person can no longer acquire knowledge of things he once knew.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r8.anchor: لا يستفيد علما ما كان به عالما

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r9.claim: Another explanation is that he no longer understands anything after having possessed reason.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r9.anchor: لا يعقل بعد عقله الأول شيئا

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r10.claim: The author adds that it may mean he can no longer act after knowing, since old age affects action more than knowledge and action depends on knowledge.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r10.anchor: ويحتمل عندي وجها ثالثا : أنه لا يعمل بعد علمه شيئا

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r11.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r11.claim: Qatada says هامدة means dusty or gray.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r12.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r12.claim: Ibn Jurayj says it means dry and unable to grow anything.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r12.anchor: يابسة لا تنبت شيئا , وهذا قول ابن جريج

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r13.claim: A third explanation takes هامدة as worn-out or barren, citing al-Aʿsha's line about clothes that are faded and worn.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r13.anchor: أنها الدراسة , والهمود : الدروس , ومنه قول الأعشى : قالت قتيلة ما لجسمك شاحبا

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r15.claim: Alternatively, the plants themselves sway, with their movement becoming vigorous; a poem compares it to a branch in green leaves.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p8/r15.anchor: معناه اهتز نباتها واهتزازه شدة حركته , كما قال الشاعر

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p9/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p9/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p9/r1.claim: One explanation is that the earth increases or multiplies its growth.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p9/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p9/r2.speaker: الحسن، أبو عبيدة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p9/r2.claim: Al-Hasan and Abu ʿUbayda say the earth swells as plants emerge; on this reading, “swelled” precedes “stirred” in meaning, while the first reading needs no inversion.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p9/r2.anchor: معناه انتفخت لظهور نباتها , فعلى هذا الوجه يكون مقدما ومؤخرا وتقديره : فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء ربت واهتزت , وهذا قول الحسن وأبي عبيدة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p9/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p9/r3.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p9/r3.claim: Ibn Shajara interprets each زوج as each kind or species.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p9/r3.anchor: يعني من كل نوع , وهو قول ابن شجرة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p9/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p9/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p9/r4.claim: Another possibility is every color, since plants vary in green, red, and yellow.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p9/r4.anchor: من كل لون لاختلاف ألوان النبات بالخضرة والحمرة والصفرة

MUJAHID:v2p419#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p419#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p419#2/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the formed and unformed as a miscarried fetus, formed and unformed.
MUJAHID:v2p419#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ مخلقة وغير مخلقة ﴾ قال هو السقط مخلوق وغير مخلوق

MUJAHID:v2p419#2/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p419#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p419#2/r2.claim: “We cause to remain in the wombs” refers to carrying a pregnancy to completion.
MUJAHID:v2p419#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ ونقر في الأرحام ما نشاء ﴾ يعني التمام

MUQATIL:22:5/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:5/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:5/r1.claim: Muqatil addresses the unbelievers of Mecca, who doubt resurrection, and urges them to consider how they were first created.
MUQATIL:22:5/r1.anchor: يعنى كفار مكة { إن كنتم فى ريب من البعث } يعنى فى شك من البعث بعد الموت

MUQATIL:22:5/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:5/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:5/r2.claim: Human beings began as nothing and were created from earth.

MUQATIL:22:5/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:5/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:5/r4.claim: The formed morsel is formed from the drop of fluid.
MUQATIL:22:5/r4.anchor: يعنى من النطقة مخلقة { وغير مخلقة } يعنى السقط يخرج من بطن أمه

MUQATIL:22:5/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:5/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:5/r5.claim: The unformed morsel is a miscarriage: it may leave the womb formed or unformed.
MUQATIL:22:5/r5.anchor: يعنى السقط يخرج من بطن أمه مصورا، وغير مصور

MUQATIL:22:5/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:5/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:5/r6.claim: God keeps in the womb what He wills, so it does not miscarry, until its appointed term and birth.
MUQATIL:22:5/r6.anchor: فلا يكون سقطا { إلى أجل مسمى } يقول: خروجه من بطن أمه

MUQATIL:22:5/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:5/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:5/r7.claim: The age of full strength runs from eighteen to forty years.
MUQATIL:22:5/r7.anchor: ثمانى عشرة سنة إلى أربعين سنة

MUQATIL:22:5/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:5/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:5/r8.claim: Some die before reaching full strength; others, after youth, return to the decrepit age of old age and lose what they once knew.
MUQATIL:22:5/r8.anchor: من قبل أن يبلغ أشده { ومنكم من يرد } بعد الشباب { إلى أرذل العمر } يعنى الهرم

MUQATIL:22:5/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:5/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:5/r9.claim: The earth is dead, without plants, and broken or crumbling.
MUQATIL:22:5/r9.anchor: يعنى ميتة ليس فيها نبت يعنى متهشمة

MUQATIL:22:5/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:5/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:5/r10.claim: The earth “moves” with vegetation; 28:31 compares this movement to a serpent.
MUQATIL:22:5/r10.anchor: الأرض، يعنى تحركت بالنبات، كقوله: تهتز كأنها جآن

MUQATIL:22:5/r11.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:5/r11.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:5/r11.claim: The earth increases and multiplies its vegetation.

MUQATIL:22:5/r12.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:5/r12.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:5/r12.claim: It produces every beautiful kind of plant.
MUQATIL:22:5/r12.anchor: يعنى من كل صنف من النبات حسن

MUQATIL:22:5/r13.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:5/r13.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:5/r13.claim: The stages of human creation and the revival of dead earth demonstrate resurrection: the One who began creation can restore the dead.
MUQATIL:22:5/r13.anchor: ليعتبروا فى البعث، فإن البعث ليس بأشد من بدء الخلق، ومن الأرض

NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r1.claim: Nasafi argues that doubters should consider their first creation: humans began as soil and fluid, and their objection to resurrection is only that the created being becomes soil and fluid again.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r1.anchor: يعني أن ارتبتم في البعث فمزيل ريبكم أن تنظروا في بدء خلقكم وقد كنتم في الابتداء قرابا وماء

NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r2.claim: We created you from dust refers to creating your father, Adam, from dust.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r3.claim: An alaqa is a piece of clotted blood.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r4.claim: A mudgha is a small piece of flesh about the size of what is chewed.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r4.anchor: أي لحمة صغسيرة قدر ما يمضغ

NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r5.claim: The formed embryo is smooth and free of deficiency or defect.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r5.anchor: المخلقة المسواة الملساء من النقصان والعيب

NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r6.claim: Embryos differ: some are fully formed and smooth, others deficient; this variation yields differences in people's forms, stature, height, and completeness.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r6.anchor: يخلق المضغ متفاوته منها ما هو كامل الخلقة أملس من العيوب ومنها ما هو على عكس ذلك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r7.claim: The stages display God's complete power and wisdom and prove His ability to restore what He initiated, despite the dissimilarity of soil and fluid.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r7.anchor: بهذا التدريج كمال قدرتنا وحكمتنا وإن من قدر على خلق البشر من تراب أولا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r8.speaker: المفضل
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r8.claim: Everyone except al-Mufaḍḍal reads nuqirru in the nominative, beginning a new sentence after a pause.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r8.anchor: بالرفع عند غير المفضل مستأنف بعد وقف

NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r9.claim: God retains in the womb whatever He wills to remain until the appointed time of birth; what He does not will to remain is miscarried.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r9.anchor: ﴿ ونقر ﴾ بالرفع عند غير المفضل مستأنف بعد وقف أى نحن نثبت ﴿ في الأرحام ما نشاء ﴾ ثبوته ﴿ إلى أجل مسمى ﴾ أي وقت الولادة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r10.claim: Tiflan is circumstantial and can be a generic singular, or the wording can mean that each of you is brought out as a child.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r10.anchor: ﴿ ثم نخرجكم ﴾ من الرحم ﴿ طفلا ﴾ حال واريد به الجنس فلذا لم يجمع أو اريد به ثم نخرج كل واحد منكم طفلا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r11.claim: The phrase implies that God raises you until you reach the fullness of your intellect and strength.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r11.anchor: ﴿ ثم لتبلغوا ﴾ ثم نربيكم لتبلغوا ﴿ أشدكم ﴾ كمال عقلكم وقوتكم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r12.claim: Ashudd is a plural form with no singular used for it.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r12.anchor: وهو من الفاظ الجموع التي لا يستعمل لها واحد

NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r13.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r13.claim: Some die upon reaching maturity, before it, or after it.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r13.anchor: عند بلوغ الأشد أو قبله أبو بعده

NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r14.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r14.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r14.claim: The most decrepit age means old age and senility.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r15.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r15.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r15.claim: One reading of the sense is that an old person no longer knows anything after having known it.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r15.anchor: أي لكيلا يعلم شيئا من بعد ما كان يعلمه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r16.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r16.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r16.claim: Alternatively, the person ceases to acquire knowledge and forgets what he once knew.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r16.anchor: أو لكيلا يستفيد علما وينسى ما كان عالما به

NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r17.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r17.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r17.claim: Nasafi introduces the reviving earth as a second proof of resurrection.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r17.anchor: ثم ذكر دليلا آخر على البعث

NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r18.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r18.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r18.claim: The earth is dead and dry.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r19.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r19.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r19.claim: It moves with the vegetation, swells, and rises.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r19.anchor: ﴿ فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء اهتزت ﴾ تحركت بالنبات ﴿ وربت ﴾ وانتفخت

NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r20.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r20.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r20.claim: Zawj means a kind or species; bahij means beautiful and pleasing to those who see it.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p95#3/r20.anchor: ﴿ وأنبتت من كل زوج ﴾ صنف ﴿ بهيج ﴾ حسن سار للناظرين إليه

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r1.claim: The verse argues for resurrection from the first creation, and its conditional wording challenges the hearer to consider that proof.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r1.anchor: هذا احتجاج على العالم بالبداءة الأولى

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r2.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r2.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan reads al-baʿth with an open ʿayn; Basrans call it a dialect form, while Kufans analyze it as a lightened form.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r2.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بن أبي الحسن «البعث» بفتح العين

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r3.claim: Creation from soil refers to the creation of Adam, the origin of humanity.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r3.anchor: أي خلقنا أباكم الذي هو أصل البشر يعني آدم عليه السلام

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r4.claim: Nuṭfa is semen and takes its name from being a small amount of water, though the word can also refer to much water, as in a hadith about the two seas.

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r5.claim: Nuṭf can mean drops; naṭafa is to drip, and layla naṭūfa is a night of steady rain.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r5.anchor: نطف ينطف وينطف. وليلة نطوفة دائمة القطر.

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r6.claim: ʿAlaqa is congealed blood; ʿalaq can also mean fresh blood or blood of an intense red.

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r7.claim: Muḍgha is a small lump of flesh, about the amount one can chew; a hadith also calls a part of the body a muḍgha.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r7.anchor: وهي لحمة قليلة قدر ما يمضغ

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r8.claim: The developmental stages total four months; Ibn Abbas says the soul is breathed in during the ten days afterward, matching the widow's waiting period of four months and ten days.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس: وفي العشر بعد الأشهر الأربعة

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r9.claim: Ibn Masud and Ibn Umar report that when the drop settles in the womb, an angel asks God about sex, blessedness, lifespan, deeds, and place of death; the angel finds its account in the Mother Book and the person's provision, path, death, and burial place are decreed.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5/r9.anchor: عن ابن مسعود وعن ابن عمر أن النطفة إذا استقرت في الرحم أخذها ملك بكفه

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#2/r1.speaker: أنس بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#2/r1.claim: A sound report from Anas, raised to the Prophet, says God appoints an angel over the womb; at each stage the angel asks about the drop, clot, and lump, then asks sex, blessedness, provision, and lifespan and writes the decree in the womb.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#2/r1.anchor: إن الله قد وكل بالرحم ملكا فيقول أي رب نطفة

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#2/r2.speaker: حذيفة بن أسيد الغفاري
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#2/r2.claim: A sound report from Hudhayfa ibn Asid says that after forty-two nights an angel shapes the drop and forms its hearing, sight, skin, flesh, and bones, then asks whether it is male or female.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#2/r2.anchor: عن حذيفة بن أسيد الغفاري قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#2/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#2/r3.claim: In a sound report, the Prophet says the embryo is a drop for forty days, then a clot for the same, then a lump for the same; an angel then breathes in the soul and receives four decrees: provision, lifespan, deeds, and blessedness or wretchedness.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#2/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: حدثنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو الصادق المصدوق

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#2/r4.claim: The Ibn Masud hadith clarifies the earlier reports: each stage lasts forty days, then the angel breathes in the soul, making four months; the author connects this to Ibn Abbas's account of the widow's waiting period.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#2/r4.anchor: فهذا الحديث مفسر للأحاديث الأول فإن فيه:

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#2/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masud explains embryo gathering in the womb: after the drop enters and God wills a human from it, it spreads beneath the woman's nails and hair for forty days, then becomes blood in the womb; this is the gathering and the clot stage.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#2/r5.anchor: سئل الأعمش: ما يجمع في بطن أمه؟ فقال حدثنا خيثمة قال: قال عبد الله:

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#2/r6.claim: Attributing formation to the angel is figurative: all shaping occurs by God's power and creation; the Qur'an assigns actual creation to God and denies independent creative power to creatures.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#2/r6.anchor: نسبة الخلق والتصوير للملك نسبة مجازية لا حقيقية

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r1.claim: Qurtubi links human creation to 23:12–13, 64:2, 40:64, 95:4, and 96:2, arguing that decisive proofs establish the Lord alone creates every creature.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r1.anchor: ولقد خلقنا الإنسان من سلالة من طين * ثم جعلناه نطفة في قرار مكين

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r2.claim: The angel's breathing is only a means through which God creates the soul and life; all ordinary causes likewise operate by God's origination, against naturalist doctrines.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r2.anchor: أي أن النفخ سبب خلق الله فيها الروح والحياة. وكذلك القول في سائر الأسباب المعتادة فإنه بإحداث الله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r3.claim: Scholars agree that the soul is breathed into the fetus after 120 days, completing four months and entering the fifth, as established by the hadiths discussed earlier.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r3.anchor: لم يختلف العلماء أن نفخ الروح فيه يكون بعد مائة وعشرين يوما

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r4.claim: The certainty of fetal movement at this stage informs rulings on disputed paternity attribution and maintenance owed for a divorced woman's pregnancy.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r4.anchor: وعليه يعول فيما يحتاج إليه من الأحكام في الاستلحاق عند التنازع، وفي وجوب النفقات

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r5.claim: One proposed wisdom for a widow's four-month-and-ten-day waiting period is that the interval establishes an empty womb if no pregnancy appears.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r5.anchor: وقد قيل: إنه الحكمة في عدة المرأة من الوفاة بأربعة أشهر وعشر

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r6.speaker: مالك وأصحابه
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r6.claim: A nutfa expelled before settling in the womb has no legal status; once it becomes a clot, expulsion of a clot or later-stage morsel counts as delivery, ending the waiting period and establishing umm walad status.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r6.anchor: وهذا مذهب مالك رضي الله عنه وأصحابه

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r7.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r7.claim: Al-Shafi'i does not count an expelled clot; recognition of human form controls, and when a fleshy fetus has no visible form, two views are transmitted or derived, with the stated view ending idda but not making her umm walad.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r7.anchor: وقال الشافعي رضي الله عنه: لا اعتبار بإسقاط العلقة، وإنما الاعتبار بظهور الصورة والتخطيط

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r8.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r8.claim: Al-Farra defines mukhallaqa as fully formed and ghayr mukhallaqa as a miscarriage.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r8.anchor: قال الفراء: «مخلقة» تامة الخلق، «وغير مخلقة» السقط

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r9.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r9.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says that if the term follows its root, the nutfa, clot, and morsel are all mukhallaqa because all are God's creation; the alternative imaging-based sense continues in the next segment.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#3/r9.anchor: إذا رجعنا إلى أصل الاشتقاق فإن النطفة والعلقة والمضغة مخلقة لأن الكل خلق الله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r1.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r1.claim: If mukhallaqa means reaching the endpoint of formed appearance, Ibn al-Arabi identifies that interpretation with Ibn Zayd's account of developed body parts.

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r2.claim: Qurtubi prefers the broader derivation: takhliq means creating repeatedly, so every developmental stage, even a nutfa, is created and mukhallaqa; 23:14 supports successive creation.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r2.anchor: فما تتابع عليه الأطوار فقد خلق خلقا بعد خلق

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r3.claim: Another view applies the contrast to individual children: God completes some fetuses' limbs while others are born premature and incomplete.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r3.anchor: منهم من يتم الرب سبحانه مضغته فيخلق له الأعضاء أجمع

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r4.claim: A further view takes mukhallaqa to mean that the woman gives birth at full term.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r4.anchor: المخلقة أن تلد المرأة لتمام الوقت

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas defines mukhallaqa as a living fetus and ghayr mukhallaqa as a miscarriage.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r5.anchor: ابن عباس: المخلقة ما كان حيا

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r6.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r6.claim: An unattributed poetic line asks why one should cry over the unformed miscarriage, illustrating the term's use.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r6.anchor: أفي غير المخلقة البكاء فأين الحزم ويحك والحياء

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r7.claim: Scholars agree that an enslaved woman becomes umm walad if she miscarries a child fully formed.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r7.anchor: أجمع العلماء على أن الأمة تكون أم ولد بما تسقطه من ولد تام الخلق

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r8.speaker: مالك والأوزاعي
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r8.claim: Malik, al-Awza'i, and others establish umm walad status from a morsel whether formed or unformed, provided it is known to be a morsel.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r8.anchor: وعند مالك والأوزاعي وغيرهما بالمضغة كانت مخلقة أو غير مخلقة

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r9.speaker: الشافعي وأبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r9.claim: Al-Shafi'i and Abu Hanifa establish umm walad status when any human feature, such as a finger or eye, is visible.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r9.anchor: إن كان قد تبين له شيء من خلق بني آدم أصبع أو عين

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r10.speaker: مالك وأبو حنيفة والشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r10.claim: The jurists agree that a newborn who cries aloud is prayed over; Malik, Abu Hanifa, al-Shafi'i, and others do not pray over one who does not cry.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r10.anchor: أجمعوا على أن المولود إذا استهل صارخا يصلى عليه فإن لم يستهل صارخا لم يصل عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r11.speaker: ابن عمر وابن المسيب وابن سيرين
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r11.claim: Ibn Umar, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Ibn Sirin, and others are reported to pray over a miscarriage even without the usual cry.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r11.anchor: روي عن ابن عمر أنه يصلى عليه وقاله ابن المسيب وابن سيرين وغيرهما

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r12.speaker: المغيرة بن شعبة
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r12.claim: Al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba ordered prayer, naming, washing, shrouding, and perfuming for miscarriages, saying Islam honors its young and old, and recited this verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r12.anchor: وروي عن المغيرة بن شعبة أنه كان يأمر بالصلاة على السقط

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r13.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r13.claim: Ibn al-Arabi interprets al-Mughira's miscarriage as one with visible formation; an unformed loss, he says, has no existence.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r13.anchor: لعل المغيرة بن شعبة أراد بالسقط ما تبين خلقه فهو الذي يسمى

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r14.speaker: بعض السلف
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r14.claim: Some early authorities say a miscarriage is prayed over once the soul has been breathed into it and four months are complete.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r14.anchor: يصلى عليه متى نفخ فيه الروح وتمت له أربعة أشهر

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r15.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r15.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that a newborn who cries aloud inherits.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r15.anchor: وروى أبو داود عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r16.speaker: سفيان الثوري والأوزاعي والشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r16.claim: For Sufyan al-Thawri, al-Awza'i, and al-Shafi'i, movement, sneezing, breathing, or crying establishes life and inheritance.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r16.anchor: وإلى هذا ذهب سفيان الثوري والأوزاعي والشافعي

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r17.speaker: الخطابي
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r17.claim: Al-Khattabi calls the position of the jurists of opinion the best view on signs of life for inheritance.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r17.anchor: قال الخطابي: وأحسنه قول أصحاب الرأي

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r18.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r18.claim: Malik denies inheritance absent a cry, even if the fetus moves or sneezes; this view is also transmitted from Ibn Sirin, al-Sha'bi, al-Zuhri, and Qatada.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r18.anchor: لا ميراث له وإن تحرك أو عطس ما لم يستهل صارخا

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r19.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r19.claim: Malik awards the ghurra for a morsel, clot, or known fetus miscarried after the woman's abdomen is struck.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r19.anchor: قال مالك رضي الله عنه: ما طرحته المرأة من مضغة أو علقة أو ما يعلم أنه ولد

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r20.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r20.claim: For Malik, a miscarriage that does not cry brings the ghurra even if it moves or sneezes; a crying newborn brings full blood money.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r20.anchor: قال مالك: إذا سقط الجنين فلم يستهل صارخا ففيه الغرة

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r21.speaker: الشافعي وسائر فقهاء الأمصار
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r21.claim: Al-Shafi'i and jurists elsewhere require full blood money when movement, sneezing, crying, or another certain sign establishes the fetus was alive.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r21.anchor: وقال الشافعي رضي الله عنه وسائر فقهاء الأمصار: إذا علمت حياته بحركة أو بعطاس أو باستهلال

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r22.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r22.speaker: القاضي إسماعيل
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r22.claim: Qadi Isma'il says a miscarriage ends the woman's waiting period because it is a pregnancy, citing 65:4.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#4/r22.anchor: التاسعة: ذكر القاضي إسماعيل أن عدة المرأة تنقضي بالسقط الموضوع

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#5/r1.speaker: القاضي إسماعيل
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#5/r1.claim: Qadi Isma'il's proof that the miscarried fetus existed as a child and pregnancy is that it inherits from its father.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#5/r1.anchor: قال القاضي إسماعيل: والدليل على ذلك أنه يرث أباه، فدل على وجوده خلقا وكونه ولدا وحملا

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#5/r2.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#5/r2.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says none of these legal consequences attach unless the fetus is formed.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#5/r2.anchor: قال ابن العربي: ولا يرتبط به شيء من هذه الأحكام إلا أن يكون مخلقا

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#5/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#5/r3.claim: Qurtubi argues that the hadith about human formation in the womb and the language of pregnancy support ending idda when a clot or morsel settled in the womb is expelled, under 65:4.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#5/r3.anchor: «إن أحدكم يجمع خلقه في بطن أمه» يدل على صحة ما قلناه

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#5/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#5/r4.claim: The expelled clot or morsel is the embryo's embodied beginning, like the outlined fetus, so the woman's claim to have been pregnant and delivered is evident.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#5/r4.anchor: ولأنها وضعت مبدأ الولد عن نطفة متجسدا كالمخطط، وهذا بين

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#5/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#5/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that a miscarried child sent ahead is dearer to him than a horseman left behind; al-Hakim's version says a thousand horsemen.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#5/r5.anchor: لسقط أقدمه بين يدي أحب إلي من فارس أخلفه خلفي

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#5/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#5/r6.claim: Lunubayyina means God displays the perfection of His power by moving human creation through its stages.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#5/r6.anchor: { لنبين لكم } يريد: كمال قدرتنا بتصريفنا أطوار خلقكم

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r1.speaker: أبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r1.claim: Abu Hatim transmits the accusative readings nuqirra and nukhrija from Asim through Abu Yazid and al-Mufaddal, parsing them by coordination.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r1.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: النصب على العطف

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r2.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj insists on nominative nuqirru: creation is not for the purpose of keeping fetuses, but to guide people to right conduct; he takes the resurrection clarification as parenthetical.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r2.anchor: وقال الزجاج: «نقر» بالرفع لا غير لأنه ليس المعنى

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r3.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r3.claim: The majority read nuqirru in the nominative, meaning, 'We keep in the wombs what We will.'

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r4.speaker: قراءة
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r4.claim: A variant reads yuqirru and yukh'rijukum in the third person, with the nominative also valid in that reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r4.anchor: «ويقر» و«يخرجكم» بالياء، والرفع على هذا سائغ

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r5.speaker: ابن وثاب
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r5.claim: Ibn Waththab reads the nun of nasha' with kasra.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب «ما نشاء» بكسر النون

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r6.claim: The appointed term differs for each fetus: some miscarry, while others complete development and emerge alive.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r6.anchor: والأجل المسمى يختلف بحسب جنين جنين فثم من يسقط وثم من يكمل أمره

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r7.claim: The wording ma rather than man refers to the pregnancy, including the morsel, which is inanimate.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r7.anchor: وقال «ما نشاء» ولم يقل من نشاء لأنه يرجع إلى الحمل

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r8.claim: Tiflan is a generic singular used for the plural sense, 'as children'; it may also mean each one of you as a child.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r8.anchor: أي أطفالا فهو اسم جنس. وأيضا فإن العرب قد تسمي الجمع باسم الواحد

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r9.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r9.claim: The poet uses a singular noun for a plural group, as the line's plural reproaches are paired with the singular amir.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r9.anchor: يلحينني في حبها ويلمنني إن العواذل ليس لي بأمير

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r10.speaker: المبرد
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r10.claim: Al-Mubarrad says tifl can function as a verbal noun like rida and adl, applying to singular and plural; 24:31 gives another use.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r10.anchor: كالرضا والعدل، فيقع على الواحد والجمع قال الله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r11.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r11.claim: Al-Tabari parses tiflan as an accusative of specification, comparing 4:4.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r11.anchor: وقال الطبري: وهو نصب على التمييز، كقوله تعالى: فإن طبن لكم عن شيء منه نفسا

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r12.claim: Tifl applies from a child's separation at birth until puberty, and is also used for offspring of wild animals.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r12.anchor: والطفل يطلق من وقت انفصال الولد إلى البلوغ

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r13.claim: The form tifl can describe one or multiple girls or boys, and has dual and plural forms, but Arab usage does not say tiflat.

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r14.claim: Atf alat means a woman has become a mother; mutfila describes a gazelle or camel with its young soon after birth, with plural forms mutafil and mutafil.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r14.anchor: والمطفلة: الظبية معها طفلها، وهي قريبة عهد بالنتاج

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r15.claim: With fatHa on the ta, tifl means soft or delicate, as in a gentle girl or fingers.

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r16.claim: The verb tafila for night describes darkness beginning to fall.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r16.anchor: وقد طفل الليل إذا أقبل ظلامه

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r17.claim: With the noun's vowelled form, al-tifl denotes the time after midafternoon as the sun approaches sunset.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r17.anchor: بعد العصر إذا طفلت الشمس للغروب

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r18.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r18.claim: Tifl also means rain, as shown by the poetic phrase about a rain shower driven by the Pleiades.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#6/r18.anchor: والطفل بالتحريك: بعد العصر إذا طفلت الشمس للغروب. والطفل أيضا: مطر قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r1.claim: Some grammarians treat thumma as redundant, like the waw in 39:73.

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r2.claim: Ashudd means mature intellect and the peak of physical strength.

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r3.claim: The worst age is senility and dementia, when a person loses understanding, so that after knowledge he knows nothing; compare 36:68.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r3.anchor: أي أخسه وأدونه وهو الهرم والخرف حتى لا يعقل

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r4.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r4.claim: The Prophet sought refuge from miserliness, cowardice, returning to the worst age, worldly temptation, and grave punishment; al-Nasa'i reports it from Sa'd.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r4.anchor: اللهم إني أعوذ بك من البخل وأعوذ بك من الجبن وأعوذ بك أن أرد إلى أرذل العمر

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r5.speaker: سعد
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r5.claim: Sa'd says the Prophet taught these supplications to his sons as a teacher instructs boys.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r5.anchor: وكان يعلمهن بنيه كما يعلم المكتب الغلمان

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r6.claim: The earth's revival offers stronger proof of resurrection: the wording shifts from plural addressees to a singular observer while the argument remains directed at resurrection-deniers.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r6.anchor: ذكر دلالة أقوى على البعث فقال في الأول: «فإنا خلقناكم من تراب»

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj says hamida means dry and unable to grow anything.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r7.anchor: { هامدة } يابسة لا تنبت شيئا قاله ابن جريج

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r8.claim: Another explanation is dārisa, worn away; al-A'sha's verse about a pale body and worn clothes illustrates this usage.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r8.anchor: وقيل: دارسة. والهمود الدروس. قال الأعشى

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r9.speaker: الهروي
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r9.claim: Al-Harawi glosses hamida as dry and soil-like.

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r10.speaker: شمر
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r10.claim: Shammar gives several senses: land's trees wither, voices fall silent, and soil is lifeless without vegetation or rain; garments wear out and fires subside.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r10.anchor: وهمود الأرض ألا يكون فيها حياة ولا نبت ولا عود ولم يصبها مطر

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r11.claim: In the hadith phrase that hunger nearly makes someone yahmid, the verb means to perish.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r11.anchor: وفي الحديث: " حتى كاد يهمد من الجوع " أي يهلك

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r12.claim: Hamida is also used of a garment becoming worn.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r12.anchor: يقال: همد الثوب يهمد إذا بلي

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r13.claim: Ihtazzat means moved vigorously; the earth is said to shake because growing plants subtly push its soil apart, a metaphorical usage.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r13.anchor: قوله تعالى: { فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء اهتزت } أي تحركت. والاهتزاز: شدة الحركة

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r14.speaker: المبرد
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r14.claim: Al-Mubarrad instead takes the phrase as 'its plant shook,' with the genitive noun omitted.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#7/r14.anchor: وقيل: اهتز نباتها، فحذف المضاف قاله المبرد

QURTUBI-FULL:22:5#8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
